chapters.html:
Aglaea hurried to the place that arrogant man had indicated. It was rare for him to ask, not a call, but a plea... in Anaxa's way, of course... for her to come immediately to a certain place.

That place, surprisingly, was his home. Aglaea could never forget that homely scent of paper and candles.

She had always believed that place exuded that warm feeling thanks to that idiot's sister... but she couldn't help blushing when she realised that, despite so much time having passed... so many cycles... that sensation was still within her.

That happiness that house still causes on her...

''Oh, you're finally here'' came the voice that caused her such mixed feelings.

Fortunately, Aglaea maintained her firm posture, her eyes cold and blind, keeping her gaze on that man. ''You called me. Why?''

She heard Anaxa begin to walk, and knowing the man, she began to follow him, for she was sure that was what he wanted.

''Be careful. There will be stairs.''

''Why are you taking me to your room?''

''Just be quiet and follow me.''

Aglaea obeyed him, unable to help feeling nervous when her feet hit the end of the wooden staircase...

She felt sad for had forgotten a path that she had once memorised completely...

So much that she forgot that treacherous corner of the man's house where she stumbled... but Anaxa's hands immediately reached out to her, holding her in place.

''This new world has made you clumsier'' he replied mockingly, Aglaea swallowing the snort she wanted to throw at him.

She wasn't going to let him, of all people, make her lose her composure.

''We're here'' he announced, his hand still on Aglaea's wrist, guiding her as he opened the door.

For some reason, the woman did not shake off that touch. She did not want to admit it, but... she longed for that kind of human touch.

Not like Hyacine's or Castorice's, or even her sweet and chaotic Cipher's.

Or... or her precious Phainon's.

Anaxa's touch, as much as she wanted to deny it, was so different. So... necessary...

But her thoughts remained stuck on Phainon. On that man whom Aglaea would always see as her child. Like that lost and frightened child, with that horrible sense of taste in clothing.

He was her child, her student, her protégé... and she had not been able to save him from that horrible fate.

She was so immersed in her guilt at not having been able to do anything for Phainon when he had given more than his life for them that she could have sworn she was detecting his figure with her ability.

She froze when she detected another familiar breath in the room, supposedly Anaxa's.

She heard the man's soft, almost delicate sigh, feeling his hand on her shoulder, squeezing it with... she could almost say affection.

''It's him, Aglaea.''

Aglaea couldn't even utter a word.

She clumsily approached the bed, patting the mattress until she managed to touch a knee. She continued climbing up, with extreme care, with the desperate touch of a mother, until she reached that face she had caressed so many times to comfort him in the past, before she completely lost her humanity.

But now it had returned to her, just like Phainon.

By the Titans... Phainon was there with her. With them.

''Phainon...'' Aglaea whispered painfully, able to sense with her ability the horrible face the hero wore.

She could feel his sweaty, feverish forehead, and his body was completely bandaged.

What had happened to him?

''It's a miracle he made it all the way from where I found him to my house'' said Anaxa's voice, and Aglaea felt him sit down beside her. ''He's a tough boy.''

''What happened to him?'' she asked aloud this time.

Anaxa shrugged. ''I know as much as you do. I saw a shooting star fall near the border of the Grove and went to investigate. And... there he was. His whole body bleeding, barely breathing and—'' Anaxa sighed again, gently taking Aglaea's hands and guiding them to Phainon's left shoulder.

And then she understood everything.

''No...'' Aglaea whispered in terror ''Phainon, what... what have they done to you?''

The woman could resist no longer and embraced the boy she had basically raised, kissing his feverish forehead, not caring that her lips were wet with sweat.

She was so affected by the state of her young pupil that she did not notice how his breathing had calmed down, and obviously she could not see how the frown caused by the possible nightmares that still plagued his mind had vanished.

'“I knew I had to bring you here. You're good for him, Aglaea.”' Aglaea did not respond to Anaxa's words, but when she raised her head, her hand still on the young hero's cheek, she decided that she should take him to Okheima as soon as possible.

''Why?'' Anaxa replied in disgust.

''Why? Because it's his home!''

''In that case, take him to Aedes Elysiaea. I'm sure it's been rebuilt in this new world.''

''And without any inhabitants, I bet'' snorted Aglaea, defensively.

''He's too injured and sick to travel.''

''I'll call Hyacine to help us with transport. And I'm sure that if we have to carry him, Mydei will be more than happy to—''

''Why on the name of Cerces do you want to take him away when he's being treated well here, Aglaea!?'' Anaxa snorted, leaving the woman impressed, as she did not expect such a loss of composure from her former lover, and even less so for Phainon.

''I want him to be well cared for.''

''Phainon would be dead if it weren't for me. So what you said is utter nonsense'' he replied in the same defensive tone.

Aglaea opened her mouth, closing it without being able to say anything, repeating that movement at least three times. ''Wh-What's your problem?''

''Excuse me?'' Anaxa laughs, incredulous.

''Now you care about him? Seriously!?'

''When have I not cared about him? If you've never believed that about me, it's because back then, this idiot didn't need absolute protection. But now? After suffering who knows what kind of torture at the hands of creatures even more powerful than our Titans? When he has all those wounds and his arm—''

Aglaea could sense how tightly Anaxa was clenching his mouth, exhaling a resigned sigh.

''He's my student. My student who has gone through unimaginable torture to save us all. He's staying here, in my house.''

Aglaea pursed her lips, sighing resignedly. ''But I'm not leaving either. I'm not going to leave him alone.''

Anaxa responded with a mocking smile, the kind he knew the woman hated so much. ''So be it, dear Aglaea.'' She felt the weight of the mattress ease, and Anaxa's voice grow fainter. ''You know you've always been welcome in my home.''

✃ 𓇢𓆸

Anaxa returned quickly, and Aglaea could detect from her nostrils that he was carrying medicines and antiseptics.

He approached to the bed again, watching how Aglaea continued to stroke the young hero's hair.

''Will you help me heal him?'' Aglaea nodded, taking the antiseptic from the man's hands while Anaxa adjusted Phainon so he could remove his dirty bandages and replace them with new ones, his wounds now disinfected and clean again.

The man hears Phainon's uncomfortable groan as he was moved not only from that comfortable position, but also from no longer feeling the touch of the woman who had saved him in the past in his hair, letting out a relieved sigh when Aglaea reassured him, touching his cheek, promising that they would be done soon.

''I did well to call you. I doubt I could have calmed him down like that.''

''Did you even try?'' Aglaea snapped, Anaxa shrugging. ''I still doubt it would have worked.''

''Because you never dare to think about how much Phainon cares for you. I'm sure he can't even believe that it was you who saved him.''

Surprisingly, Anaxa did not respond sharply to the woman's comment, as she had expected.

She felt him sit down beside her and begin to undo the young hero's dirty bandages. Aglaea collected them while Anaxa cleaned the wounds which, although she could not see how serious they were, Aglaea could smell the state they were in.

She couldn't help but embrace Phainon by the shoulders to not bother Anaxa with the healing, giving him another kiss on his hair, which was in desperate need of a wash and a good brushing.

''When do you think we can bathe him?''

''Not yet. His wounds are still serious and open'' Anaxa replied, Aglaea nodding with a sigh.

While Anaxa finished treating the multitude of cuts and lacerations all over his body, Aglaea wiped his sweat, asking helplessly if she could help with anything else.

She felt Anaxa lift Phainon's stump, hearing his mutter ''The cut on his arm is clean, but it still needs to be monitored.'' Carefully, he handed the woman a couple of wet gauze pads. ''Clean that wound.''

''It seems like you're giving me a useless job'' replied Aglaea, annoyed.

''You're not being useless at all. Do you know how difficult it was to heal this idiot when I found him? How he kept thinking that my hands belonged to the person or thing that caused this?'' Anaxa replied calmly. ''If you want to heal your boy to 'feel useful' by doing the same job as me, do that, which is the least important thing, but you're being just as useful as me just by holding him and keeping him calm.''
Anaxa moved the back of his hand to Phainon's chest, feeling his weak heartbeat against his skin. ''Believe me, right now, feeling safe is what he needs most.''

Aglaea sighed, without replying to the man, leaving behind the gauze he had given her to settle Phainon in her lap.

She continued to stroke his hair, starting there and ending at his neck, right where she knew he had that special mark.

She could feel Phainon breathing more and more calmly, as if instead of fighting for his life, he were simply in a peaceful sleep, when suddenly Anaxa stopped and Aglaea couldn't help but worry.

''What's wrong?'' The woman tried to sit up. ''Why have you stopped!?''

''Be quiet!'' Anaxa hissed firmly but quietly. Aglaea obeyed immediately, as it was unusual for Anaxa, despite his sharp tongue, to speak to her that way.

She felt Anaxa right next to her. She could even feel his breath on her face, but from the way he was breathing, she knew that his gaze was not on her, but on the badly injured man.

''Phainon'' Anaxa called to him ''How are you feeling, boy?''

''He's awake?'' Aglaea asked, incredulous. Excited.

She only heard Anaxa's dissatisfied murmur, and then his sigh. ''He just has his eyes open. He's still... quite disoriented.'' Aglaea clenched her jaw, saddened, caressing beneath those eyes that had witnessed so much pain and death. She couldn't help but smile when she heard a sigh from Phainon, surprised when Anaxa spoke again. ''Yes, idiot, it's her. She's taking care of you, like only a lioness takes care of her cubs, so behave yourself and let us heal you.'' Anaxa approached Aglaea and whispered in her ear ''He's looking at you. Fiercely''

Aglaea laughed, shaking her head, relieved. ''You've heard your beloved professor'' she whispered affectionately, continuing to caress him. ''Soon you'll be fine and everything will go back to normal.''

''Back to normal? Have we ever had a normal life?''

Aglaea's sweet smile broke at Anaxa's comment. ''Only you would be capable of ruining a moment like this.''

''The last thing the poor man hopes for, and surely all of us as well, is to return to our former lives. He has sacrificed himself so that we can aspire to a better one.''

''Are you seriously correcting my chosing of words?''

''An incorrect way of speaking given the situation.''

Aglaea sighed, irritated, turning her face away from that fussy professor.

She knew he was back to the healing task, but she was surprised to hear a laughter coming from the man.

It was not malicious or ill-intentioned. She made a sound to indicate that she was curious as to why he had started laughing.

''He has closed his eyes again.'' Aglaea's gaze softened at this information, and she lowered her fingers to Phainon's cheek. ''But you made him smile when you started arguing with me. How sweet.''

''Please don't ruin that information with your sarcasm.''

Anaxa did not respond immediately, Aglaea hearing the strips of bandages tearing as he wrapped the young man's wounds.

''I wasn't being sarcastic at all. It was really sweet how calm and happy he looked with you.''

Aglaea didn't respond, wishing that the imbecile couldn't see the blush that had appeared on her cheeks, settling back into the bed to better support the wounded man.

Anaxa finished, getting up from the bed and asking if she wanted something to eat. When Aglaea replied that she did, she could clearly hear a smile forming on his lips, the woman never guessing whether it was genuine or with an amused glint behind it.

''I was thinking of making tzatziki for dinner. Would you like that?''

''You're an idiot.''

''But I haven't still said anything bad!'' Anaxa smiled mockingly, leaving the room ''Anyone would think I'm going to make you your favourite meal.''

Aglaea sighed, irritated not only by Anaxa's behaviour, but also by her own.

Why did he always manage to get on her nerves?

And why... did she like it so much? Did she like having his attention so much?

''Phainon, get well soon so we can go back to Okhema and I never have to see this idiot again.''

Chapter Summary

It's Anaxa's turn to comfort Phainon from his nightmares

Chapter Notes

Anaxa returns to his own room, unsure of how to feel about the scene before him.

Aglaea was sleeping soundly, still in the same position, with Phainon's head resting on her lap and her fingers, now motionless, resting on his white hair.

Anaxa couldn't help but approach her, an impulse to wake the woman and suggest she go to sleep, even if it was in his sister's room, which still had its bed.

But he knew Aglaea would refuse, and with a simple glance at Phainon, Anaxa simply couldn't risk disturbing the peaceful sleep the young hero had finally found.

He sighs deeply, massaging his temple, trying to gather his thoughts.

His eye opens again, unable to tear themselves away from Aglaea's figure.

He can stare at her for all eternity and never get tired of it.

And he can't help but feel something different from when they first met, in whatever cycle that was for Phainon.

When they connected their coreflames. When Anaxa saw the few humanity she had left.

How that information hurt him. To see that coldness in those eyes that were once warmer than the sun itself.

But now... that humanity, that warmth, had returned to her. And Anaxa simply didn't know how to behave.

With a resigned sigh, he tried to leave that place, to be the one sleeping in his sister's bed, when an uncomfortable moan caught his attention.

He peeked into the room, seeing Phainon's body trembling slightly.

Worrying that he would wake Aglaea, Anaxa approached him, biting his lip, concerned to see him once again immersed in his nightmares.

His attention is on the two sleeping figures, one peaceful, whom he doesn't want to wake, and the other in agony, whom he wants to calm down.

He whispered softly, his hands not touching any part of Phainon's body, as he still remembers what happened days ago.

How broken his body was, and yet he still had the strength to resist. To fight.

How Anaxa's attempts to comfort him were useless. How he had to use force, weakening his badly injured student even more, in order to heal him once and for all.

And there he was again. Fighting his demons, Anaxa unable to do anything.

Phainon buried his face in Aglaea's knee, murmuring in pain, his closed eyelashes glistening as his body shook more and more.

Although he feels bad for her, Anaxa could no longer tolerate this suffering and goes to wake Aglaea, when the conversation they had hours earlier comes to mind.

''Did you even try? You never dare to think about how much Phainon cares for you. I'm sure he can't even believe that it was you who saved him.''

Anaxa snorts, as if Aglaea were awake at that very moment, reproaching him for waking that boy when he himself could ease Phainon's torment.

''This isn't going to work'' he thought as he knelt down in front of the injured man.

He takes his hand to the other's cheek, cradling it, more clumsily than Aglaea had done, but it was enough to, if not calm him, at least get the hero's attention.

"Shhh... Phainon, it's me. Anaxagoras. Remember to call me that, not Anaxa.'' Skatá, he didn't even know what he was saying. ''You're safe, boy. You're with Aglaea. And well, with me." Phainon grunted, shaking his head even more, as if he wants to hide from the world. It was a miracle that Aglaea hadn't woke up yet.

Fearing that he would finally fulfil that purpose, he carefully hold his head and shoulders, moving him to the other side of the bed so that he would leave Aglaea alone and go to rest in his lap.

But Phainon suddenly grabbed his wrist tightly, digging his nails into Anaxa's flesh. And... the professor would have sworn that his skin was starting to burn...

He also watches with horror how his bandages begins to bleed again, a part of his chest that was uncovered opening up, when Anaxa would have sworn that there was no wound there, oozing more golden blood.

The mere thought of waking Aglaea and having her solve this did not even cross his mind, as he only wanted to relieve and calm his poor student. And unlike the first time, when he was very scared and really unsure that it would work, Anaxa decides to listen to the woman and imitate her, hugging his clumsy student while stroking his soft hair. "Easy, boy, easy... you're alive. You're safe, with us. The others are alive too, thanks to you. We'll be reunited with them soon, okay? But first you need to rest.''

Phainon loosens his grip on Anaxa's wrist, and what had been a savage growl turned into a frightened and vulnerable whimper. ''I know you're scared and confused, but just follow my voice and trust me. You're safe, and Aglaea and I are going to get you back on your feet. So you can live the life you deserve, Phainon. Don't sink into those nightmares, and drift off into a peaceful sleep."

Only a few minutes passed, Anaxa in that position, imitating Aglaea's comfort caresses, while Phainon drifts further and further away from his previous state.

The new wound remained, but fortunately it stopped bleeding. Anaxa sighs irritably at having to heal the poor man again, but feels a great relief when he saw that, as Aglaea had told him, he had managed to calm him completely.

Anaxa couldn't avoid to caresses his forehead, a soft smile he didn't know it could form on his face, looking with immeasurable affection at the sleeping face. ''There you are. Good job, boy''

At those words, Phainon's eyelids flutters, and that golden glow appears. Anaxa blinks, not knowing what to say, watching Phainon take a deep breath before using his vocal cords.

''Prof...ssor... Ana...xa'' and as if saying those two words, those 13 letters, was enough effort, Phainon closes his eyes again, his body melting at the touch of his beloved teacher, whose caresses helped him dispel any trace of bad memories of all the torture he had endured.

Anaxa sighs again, brushing away a few strands of white hair, caressing each one with the utmost tenderness. ''It's Professor Anaxagoras, anóitos'' he corrects, for the first time, not at all annoyed.

🌤 🌤

When Anaxa wakes up, he finds Aglaea staring at him, mischievously.

If it weren't for Phainon sleeping peacefully on his lap, he would have kicked the woman without hesitation for giving him such a fright.

Aglaea laughs when she realised he was awake, striking a flirtatious pose. ''How cute you are. You'll sure look like a tender family portrait.''

''Pfft'' was all Anaxa could says, making sure Phainon was still asleep.

Although he still has those horrible dark circles under his eyes, his face showed no sign of pain or distress, so he asks Aglaea to help him settle him on the pillow, and the woman obeys, still wearing that mocking smile.

''I told you'' she obviously couldn't help pointing out.

''Yeah, yeah. I too have the power to calm down literally a god. Oh... how powerful I feel''

''Phainon is not just a god. At least, not to us'' Aglaea replies, annoyed.

''You're really not in the mood for jokes, are you?''

He waits for a new retort from the woman. What he didn't expect was how her blind gaze fell, her lip curling into a helpless grimace. "I truly believed he was dead. No one knew anything about him, no one had seen him anywhere. Stelle even told us... about his transformation. His fate...'' Aglaea's voice broke a little, and Anaxa hated how happy it made him to hear the woman he had loved so much and lost in the worst possible way, to break down like that. To show that humanity. ''33,550,336. So many cycles, Anaxa."

''I know.''

''That... is horrible. Inhuman. How... how could he deal with that? How could he resist? And all alone?''

''Aglaea, shhh...'' Anaxa hushes her delicately, but to being honest, her cries did not bother Phainon at all.

It was as if the young man needs his mentor's voice as another form of oxygen.

But Aglaea apologies, her jaw clenched with rage and helplessness. ''Don't apologise. It's normal to feel that anger.''

''He suffered and is suffering so much...''

"And now he's here, with us. If I have to be honest, when you told me that Phainon was the last one to show up, I thought we had lost him completely. That... he had died, or that he simply wouldn't be able to enjoy this enormous and precious second chance." Anaxa tenses when he hears Aglaea cries.

It was silent, and tears barely fell down her cheeks... but the woman was crying.

How long had it been since he had seen that look?

He couldn't help it, and he closes his hand around hers, sighing with relief when Aglaea accepted it immediately. "But he's here. And even though he looks different and bears the clear signs of his torture from those horrible cycles... he recognises us.

And that's enough for us to fight for him until he's our Phainon again.''

''What if that Phainon never comes back?'' she asks what they both feared, Anaxa shrugging his shoulders, simply. ''Then we'll love this new Phainon, reborn from his ashes. Whoever he is, he'll always have us by his side.''

Aglaea nods at that statement, her fingers distractedly playing with Anaxa's, the man letting her, as if his body did not want to move away from the slightest touch caused by that woman.

''He woke up yesterday. And he spoke to me.'' Aglaea looks up, curious. ''He called me Anaxa.''

''Don't tell me you corrected him after seeing the state he's in?'' aglaea asks, amused.

''Only when he went back to sleep. But I plan to scold him about it when he's more lucid, trust me.''

He manages to make Aglaea laughs, grateful that she's blind so she couldn't see the silly smile she had caused on him. ‘I call you Anaxa too'' her voice suddenly rang out, surprising him with what had come out of her mouth. ''And you've never corrected me.''

''I don't have to correct you.''

''Why?''

''Are you really asking me that, dear Aglaea?''

Anaxa laughs at the blush he had caused on the woman, although he was the last person who should have been laughing at something like that.

Fortunately, their attention immediately return to Phainon, Aglaea resting her palm on the young man's thin belly. ''Should we wake him up so he can eat something?''

''Let's wait until nightfall to see if he wakes up on his own. If not, I'll go to the hospital so we can feed him without him having to wake up.''

''Is it so bad to wake him up?''

''He needs to sleep, Aglaea. Who knows when he last had a decent rest?“”

Aglaea nods, her hands returning to that soft hair, smiling when she felt Phainon move closer to her touch. To her warmth.

“'When should we tell the others that Phainon is here? Alive”' Aglaea asks in a low voice.

Like... hesitant.

“'When he's fully recovered”' Anaxa determines. Seeing Aglaea's surprise at this answer, he clarifies ''It's not for him, but for them. They deserve to enjoy this second chance, and not wasting by taking care of their badly injured friend.''

But he sees how Aglaea shakes her head, a sad smile on her face. ''You truly think they're enjoying this second chance while they think one of their friends didn't make it?''

Anaxa sighs irritably, but did not argue with the blonde. ''Let's call them then. But just so you know, I don't want so many people in my house.'' And before Aglaea could open her mouth... ''And he's not leaving here until he's recovered, even if it's only 60%.''

Aglaea nods weakly, Anaxa grunting in dissatisfaction, knowing that the woman was keeping something from him.

''What do we do with Mydei?''

''Huh? The prince? What do you mean?''

''Should we tell him?''

''It's not right to tell all the heirs except him, don't you think?''

''That's not what I mean...''

''Oh, you mean like a protective mama boy who wants to be the only one to take care of her little boy'' Anaxa mocks , getting what he wanted.

Annoy and enrage the blonde.

''You know that's not what I mean!''

''Then what is it?''

''How Phainon will feel if he sees Mydei, Anaxagoras, damn it!''

Anaxa blanches, as he wasn't used to Aglaea calling him by his full name. It never meant anything good when she did.

''I... I don't understand, Aglaea.''

''Phainon was the Flame Reaver. The one who... who killed Mydei, who knows how many times...''

''And Castorice. And Cipher. And Hyacine. And those three would also be eager to take care of Phain—''

''I know they would, just like Mydei, but... I don't know if it would be the same for Phainon to see them as it would be for him.''

''Why not? Are you implying that Phainon doesn't care that he killed the three of them? Trinnie?''

''No'' Aglaea replies again, softly "But they didn't die in all those cycles because of his blade.

They weren't immortal. Mydei was. And Mydei entrusted Phainon with his only way to kill him. Thanks to that, the Flame Reaver achieved his goal.''

''And that's how Phainon gives us this precious second change'' Anaxa replies simply.

''You don't understand what I mean, Anaxagoras.''

''First of all, stop calling me that.''

''It's what you want everyone to call you.''

''You're not everyone, as I say before! It sounds weird for you to call me by my full name.'' Aglaea rolls her eyes, resigned. ''And secondly...'' Anaxa was about to replies, but immediately found himself at a loss for words.

All he hears was Aglaea's faint sigh. ''Do you understand what I'm trying to explain? Even you are not sure if it's good for Phainon's fragile state to have Mydei by his side. Because if we tell him that he's alive and in this situation, no one will take Mydei away from this bed. You can be sure of that, Anaxa.''

Anaxa sighs irritably again, but agreeing with her. ''What do you suggest? That we keep it to ourselves?''

''From what the trailblazer told us, you and I are the only ones Phainon has barely spilled our blood on...''

''Barely, but there were occasions.''

''Unlike the many times with the others. Unlike Mydei, always falling under his sword.''

Anaxa takes a deep breath at how stubborn that damn woman could be. "Do you think it doesn't hurt me to suggest this decision? Mydei left Okhema immediately to go look for him. Hyacine is not resting, waiting for him to arrive in our city at any moment. Castorice continues to visit the River of Souls, hoping to find him there so she can get him out. But...'' Aglaea slumps, unable to continue, her blind gaze fixed on the wounded figure.

Anaxa grumbles, this time more calmly. ''You fear for the boy's mental health."

''He's asleep now. And... and he's barely interacting with us. But do you really think he'll be okay? Are you sure, after all the notes Stelle has lent us... he won't feel guilty? That he doesn't... hate himself for what he had to do, even if it was to save us?''

''Let's not tell the prince then. He's not in Okhema, as you said. He doesn't need to know.''

But Aglaea rejects Anaxa's suggestion. "As you said, it's unfair to tell the others and not Mydei. Besides, I don't want to lose his trust like that. I'm gonna to lose it one way or another when he find out the truth, but I prefer if it's not in that way''

Anaxa nods, patting her awkwardly on the back in a show of support, eliciting a sarcastic laugh from Aglaea. ''You've always been the best at comforting people'' she said ironically.

''At least I try.''

''If that's the best you can do, don't even bother then.''

‘'Hah'' was Anaxa's reply, managing to elicit a smile from the blonde.

But the gloom return to the room, the guilt obvious on Aglaea's face for withholding information that the other heirs so desperately needed to know.

This time, Anaxa's consolation was warmer. ''You're making the right decision. They'll understand.'' Aglaea nods weakly. ''And as for the prince, if he doesn't understand, well, that's his problem.''

''He's going to be really angry with us when he finds out'' Aglaea replies, with a tired half-laugh.

''I don't care if we piss off a kid'' Anaxa scoffs, making the blonde roll her eyes in exasperation. ''So be it. Two exes forced to be in the same room looking after their child.''

''You're indeed the biggest idiot of Amphoreus, Anaxagoras.''

''Ha, I know.''

Phainon was back in that dark place. Nanook stood before him. Impassive. Cold.

The black tide horde headed towards him, and releasing all his gathered rage, Phainon charged towards them.

He killed them, three by three, five by five, ten by ten.

He laughed as he felt the blood dripping onto his skin, annoyed by the appearance of this strange foreigner.

It didn't matter how many times it hurt him. It didn't matter that it left him without his arm. Without his wings.

He would attack.

He would attack until he had no breath left. Until that wasteland was filled with the blood of his enemies.

Until Nanook got what he deserved.

But when he turned into pure fire, heading towards Nanook, his body froze in pain. And he returned to that place again.

And to when he first arrived in Okhema.

When he saw his village burn.

When he had to kill his friends.

...

When he had to kill him.

He kept reliving those events at unceasing speed.

It was impossible to end them. He had repeated them so many times...

And yet, he couldn't take it anymore. The stress, the fear, the helplessness... the misfortune of having witnessed that, and all directed by his own sword...

Phainon couldn't take it anymore and screamed, begging for it to stop. For them to give him even a minute of peace.

Amidst all the chaos, he heard a voice. A voice he never thought he would hear again.

That sweet but firm voice. Cold as ice and at the same time as warm as the baths of Okhema.

He couldn't even say goodbye to her. She died without Phainon being able to do anything for her.

Before he could thank her for all her sacrifices and efforts she had made for him.

Everything... the love she had given him before completely sacrificing her humanity so that Phainon could take her place.

This time, his body travels to a different place.

It's small, closed and homely. It looks like a room, but there she is. Looking at him with concern, so similar to that of centuries ago, cycles ago, when she found him dying and wounded, having just fled the catastrophe of Aedes Elysae...

Phainon couldn't believe she was standing in front of him, and he reachs out his hand to touch her. To feel her...

But as soon as he feels the tender, warm hand of the woman who had become his mother figure, she disappears into her corpse.

Golden blood flowed from her head, and those eyes, though they had always seemed cold and lifeless, were now empty. Dull. More than ever.

And although he knew that Caenis was the one with Aglaea's blood on her hands, Phainon couldn't help but look at his own, and indeed see that he too was responsible for the death of the light of Okhema, of Amphoreus.

Just as he had been with Castorice.

With Hyacine.

With... with Mydei.

Phainon's scream was so shrill that poor Aglaea had to cover her ears because she feels like her eardrums were going to burst.

It didn't sound like a frightened, wounded human being.

No...

It sounded... like a creature. A creature from the cosmos, cornered.

''Phai—Phainon, wait,'' Aglaea whispers, trying to approach her frightened student. ''It's m—''

Out of nowhere, amputated wings sprout from his back, and Aglaea was knocked down by Phainon as he got up from the bed, intending to throw himself out the window and flee.

But Anaxa arrived before he could break the window, small pieces of glass sticking to his already torn skin, avoiding Phainon escaping.

He screams again in that horrible way that made the skin freeze, but Aglaea, despite the blow she had received from falling face down on the floor and the pain she feels in her nose, had the strength to get up and help Anaxa.

Phainon tries with all his might to free himself from them and get out of there, until Anaxa suddenly hit him in the stomach with his knee, and Aglaea took advantage of this to immobilise him, wrapping her hands tightly around his neck.

Phainon continues to try to free himself from those hands, his primitive scream being replaced by frightened and disoriented whimpers. Finally, his voice, that precious voice that Aglaea thought she would never hear again, sounded once more.

...

But honestly, Aglaea would have preferred not to have heard Phainon's first words at this new dawn if that was what was going to come out of his mouth.

Pleas. Cries. Begging for them to end his life. To end his suffering.

''I shouldn't have survived. I shouldn't be here'' he repeats, over and over again, as tears that never reached his mouth because they evaporated fell down his cheeks. ''I'm a danger. A plague. Kill me. Kill me, please, kill me, kill me...“”

Aglaea couldn't take it anymore and hugs her distressed pupil again, relieved that Phainon was clinging to her as if she was his lifeline.

His pleas to end his life continues, but they grew quieter and lower. More and more resigned.

Until nothing came out of Phainon's mouth, and the next thing they heard was the irregular, nervous breathing of a unconscious hero.

Both Anaxa and Aglaea sigh, exhausted, carrying Phainon's limp body back to bed.

“'Wait”' Aglaea stops him. ''Let's change his sheets, now that he's not lying down'' Without letting Anaxa replies, Aglaea settles Phainon in the man's arms while she removes the sheets, which are not entirely dirty, but clean, fresh and perfumed ones would undoubtedly be better for the hero's recovery.

Anaxa sighs, resigned. ''Do you know where they are—'' Aglaea left before Anaxa could ask if she knew where the clean sheets were. That way of ignoring him was a yes.

And while Anaxa waits for the blonde, he turns his attention back to Phainon, who, as expected, was riding a wave of nightmares.

From time to time, Phainon's knees reacted, trying to get up. To try to escape again.

But Anaxa holds him firmly, trying to calm him down as he had done the day before... this time failing miserably.

Curious, he moves his eye to his wings, for when he found Phainon, they were out too, but as soon as he managed to defeat the wounded man who was still fighting to avoid being touched, he hid them behind his back.

During those days, Anaxa came to believe that those wings were just his imagination.

Would it hurt him if he took them out? Was it normal for him to have them like that?

Couldn't he regenerate them?

He sees Aglaea return with the clean sheets, laughing at the woman's clumsiness in making the bed. ''It's been a long time since you made your own bed, hasn't it? You've gotten used to having servants.''

''Shut up'' the blond snorts, making the man laugh.

Getting up, still holding Phainon, he helps Aglaea finish, the woman taking Phainon from behind so that Anaxa could hand him over, and between the two of them they put him back to bed.

''He needs his bandages to be change again.''

''Ugh, this boy is going to leave the Grove without bandages.''

Aglaea turned around to head for the bathroom. ''Where are they?'' she asks from the hallway, Anaxa following her. ''Don't leave Phainon alone! Just tell me—''

''I have to treat your nose.''

Aglaea blinks, incredulous. "My... my nose? Are you stupid or something? How can you worry about my nose when Phainon just had an episode like that!?''

''An episode where he hit you and I think he broke your nose'' Anaxa replies, delicately.

''HE DIDN'T DO IT ON PURPOSE!" Aglaea defends his pupil, with tooth and nail.

''I never said that. But that nose needs to be treated.''

Aglaea flashes a nervous, impatient smile. ''My injury is nothing compared to—''

''If you don't let me treat your nose, I won't help you heal Phainon.''

''What!?''

''You heard me. It's your eyes that aren't working, not your ears.'' Aglaea hears Anaxa head for the bathroom. ''So it's your decision.''

Aglaea stood still, incredulous. Furious.

She approaches the room, listening to Phainon's breathing.

It didn't sound difficult. Just stressed. Arrhythmic, but that wasn't exactly due to his physical condition. The glass stuck to his skin had barely scratched him.

Understandably, after everything the poor boy had been through, a few broken pieces of glass were nothing to him...

Defeated, she sighs, heading to be healed by that detestable man.

﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏﹏

Aglaea bits her tongue at the slowness with which Anaxa passes a gauze pad over her wound.

She could feel his breath on her cheeks, his intense gaze fixed on her.

''Phainon hit me too when I found him. Well, hit... he almost beat me up.''

That was the first thing Anaxa had said since he got away with that threat. ''It was the same thing as here. He got scared, he thought I was someone I wasn't, or that he was in the wrong place and... he defended himself.''

''I told you—''

''It's not about that. I know perfectly well that you don't blame the boy for hitting you. I'm talking about myself. Just so you know, I'm not angry with Phainon for what he did to you.''

''But you'd rather heal me than him, when he needs it more'' the woman replies, sullenly.

"He doesn't. That's just your imagination. Those crystals barely grazed his skin. And I'm not sure it's a good idea for him to feel the sting and itch of the antiseptic when he's just recovering from an... hallucination like that one.''

Aglaea was about to replies, but she swallows her words, sighing resignedly and nodding in agreement with Anaxa's reasoning. ''I'm also doing this so you can see that you matter too. That you're also a priority.''

''Pardon?''

''I don't want you to neglect your health to take care of Phainon because you feel indebted to him.''

''Because I'm indebted—ha, are you kidding, Anaxágoras?''

''I told you not to call me—''

"Then don't talk nonsense! You think I'm taking care of him because I'm indebted to him? How dare you even suggest that!?''

Faced with Anaxa's silence, Aglaea became even more enraged. ''If I'm by his side, if I'm taking care of him, if... if I'm not angry about what just happened, it's because I love him, Anaxa! The same way I love Cipher! And Castorice and Hyacine! They're my children! The only company I've ever had, the ones who've had to watch me lose my humanity, my very self, just for this fucking Era Nova could be real!" the woman shouts, as if to vent her feelings.

Anaxa remains silent, letting her take the reins. Let her calm down by herself. Let the conversation continue. Letting her know that he was there to listen to her. Forever.

''I need him to be okay'' the woman confesses, almost bringing her hand to her face to cover it, but Anaxa wouldn't let her because he was still treating her nose.

But if the woman needed to vent about everything she had been through, about everything she had suffered, Phainon wouldn't be the only one to enjoy the hugs of that stubborn and unfriendly professor.

Aglaea melts at that touch, hiding her face in that soft cloak that was always clean and smelled good.

They stayed in that position for who knows how long, Aglaea pulling away immediately when she thought she heard a noise coming from the room where Phainon is.

They both ran towards it, Aglaea being stopped by Anaxa as she was about to enter.

''What are you doing?'' Anaxa says, in an irritated tone. ''Why do you think it was a good idea to get up on your own?''

Aglaea tries to approach, curious about what was happening, but Anaxa stops her again, assuring her that he would take care of it.

''Come on, idiot, get up. And don't move again.'' Aglaea finally goes to the bed when she hears movement, sitting on it and resting her hand on Phainon's hip.

The young man had his back to them, but Aglaea could sense his tension. ''Are you hurt?''

After a few seconds of pure silence, Anaxa sighs. ''She can't see you, boy. Tell her.''

''N... no'' Phainon whispers, weakly.

''Falling from the bed... Dumb and clumsy, your perfect name if you want to work in a circus.''

''Leave him alone'' Aglaea replies, with a half-smile.

''No. He needs to know his limits and, above all, ask for help.'' Anaxa approaches him, seriously. ''Do you remember what happened just a moment ago? Why you and Aglaea look like that?''

''Anaxa, don't you dare'' the woman warns him, but Phainon nods weakly.

''Then if you felt like you were falling into a nightmare again, why didn't you call us? Do you want to have another reaction like the one you had a few minutes ago?'' Anaxa reproaches him gently, ignoring the blonde woman's warning.

He hears Aglaea's angry sigh, but she had to understand that Phainon needed to hear those words! He was in a very delicate state, it was essential that he asked for help so that he could get better!

But Anaxa felt sorry for the boy when he watches him scratch the sheet, his tired eyes closing tightly. ''I still don't believe... that this is real...'' he confesses in such a low voice that both carers struggled to hear him. ''I'm sorry... I... I thought you were him...''

Anaxa sighs, resigned, but he doesn't say anything more, and Aglaea caresses his shoulder, feeling Phainon shrink, as if trying to avoid her touch.

But Aglaea did not allow it and hugs him from behind, relieved when the young man accepted her touch, can't avoid to feel happy to hear him cry.

It was just what he needed. No more repressing his feelings. Allowing himself to be vulnerable, because now he didn't have to protect anyone else. No more sacrificing himself for anyone else.

Now it was his turn to be cared for and loved. It was their job, his friends, his... his new family, to make him feel safe. At peace.

''Sleep, you idiot'' Anaxa's voice suddenly rang out. Aglaea was curious as to why he had said that. ''I can see his eyes closing and he's resisting it. Just sleep.''

''I feel like that's all I've been doing since you found me.''

''He found you'' Aglaea corrected him. ''It was Anaxa who found, healed, cared and brought you to his home to recover.'' Aglaea's blind eyes sparkles mischievously as she turns them towards Anaxa. ''But obviously he needed me.''

''Tsk'' Anaxa snorts , making Phainon laugh, deepening a murmur as he feels the fingers of the woman he loved like a second mother in his hair. ''But he's right, Phainon. Sleep, darling.''

''What if I come back—''

''We will monitor you in case you do not listen to us. If... if your mind causes you to revisit whatever you faced to secure our dawn, we will act accordingly. But sleep now.'' Anaxa's tone was completely firm, but his face softens at Phainon's vulnerable and surprised gaze. As if he still couldn't believe the information Aglaea had given him, Anaxa softens his tone as well. ''You need it, boy.'' Phainon nods weakly.

He curls up in Aglaea's arms, his eyes closing, and soon fell asleep. A peaceful sleep, fortunately.

The two old companions sigh, tired but relieved, when Aglaea's telestate sounds, causing her to jump up, looking worried, but immediately relieved.

''It's nothing serious, I guess.''

''Tribbios. Asking how I'm doing'' Aglaea whispers, blocking her telestate. Anaxa raises an eyebrow, amused. ''Aren't you going to answer?''

Anaxa laughs at Aglaea's irritated grunt, surprised when his telestate also sounded.

He couldn't help but laugh out loud, being scolded by Aglaea in case the wakes up Phainon, hearing Anaxa chuckling with his tongue.

Aglaea hears her telestate again, receiving a message from Anaxa.

It was a copy and paste of whatever he had received seconds before, so that her telestate with the app that let her read the messages could reads it for her.

''Who said that!?'' Anaxa laughs again, at Aglaea's indignation. ''Tell me!''

''My sweet, innocent Hyacine.''

''Ugghh...''

''Should we reply?''

''I don't know if I feel with the mood of answering all of Tribbios's nosy questions right now…'' Aglaea mutters, massaging her forehead with her knee because her arms were busy.

''She won't be worried at your silence?''

''I'll tell her I'm busy right now, but that I'm fine''

''Hmm... feeding her curiosity. How wicked you are, dear Aglaea.''

''And you, Professor Anaxa?'' she replies in the same tone. ''What do you plan to say to your beloved student?''

Anaxa makes a sound similar to shrugging his shoulders so that Aglaea could hear him, achieving his precious goal.

Irritate the woman.

After a few seconds of silence, Anaxa mentioned the elephant in the room. ''You still don't want to tell them anything, do you?'' Aglaea did not answer. ''Don't you think you're being a little patronising to the prince of Castrum Kremnos? I remind you that he is the bearer of Nikador's coreflame''

''You know that if I don't want him to know, it's not because of him, but because of Phainon'' Aglaea replies, defensively.

''Don't you think he's capable of dealing with Phainon's delicate condition?''

''Ag—of course he is! But it's him I'm worried about!'' Aglaea snorts, pointing with her chin at the figure in her arms. ''You heard him! He still finds it hard to believe that we're real. That... that he's finally safe. Do you really think that seeing Mydei won't harm his condition?''

''I don't know, Aglaea. Maybe it will, maybe it won't. What if you're wrong? Won't having the man he obviously loves by his side help him a lot more?''

''I don't want to risk it. Neither of them deserves that.''

''Agla–''

''Think about Mydei. You say I shouldn't patronise him, but all I'm doing is thinking about him! Worrying about him too! How would you feel if the person you love couldn't even see you because every time they did, they remembered all the times they had to kill you to save you!?''

''We don't know yet if that's what will happen to Phainon."

''Ha... you don't know him very well then'' Aglaea snorts, the man sighing wearily. ''What if what happened to us happens to Mydei or... or Hyacine. Imagine if he attacks them because he thinks they're the enemy?''

''Neither of them would be affected by that, nor the rest of u—''

"Agh, of course not! I already know that! Just like I didn't mind him breaking my nose, but we're talking about him, Anaxa!" Aglaea growls a little loudly, disturbing the sleeping figure.

Aglaea deeps her embrace, stroking his hair to prevent him from waking up, her eyes saddened by this loss of composure that could have disturbed the wounded man's rest.

Anaxa just sighs again, not knowing what to say in this uncomfortable and desperate situation.

''I... I want them to know the truth. I want all of us being together, as we deserved...'' Aglaea whispers, her voice miserable and very low. "There's nothing I want more. Even when I was completely broken, empty, I could sense the love they had for each other. How necessary they were to each other.

That's why... I can't risk ruining something so precious for something as stupid as rushing. Patience. That's all I ask, Anaxa.''

Anaxa groans, but this time he nods to the woman. ''You're supposed to be the reincarnation of the Titan of Romance. You should know more than anyone about this subject."

Aglaea thanks him, listening to Anaxa type something. She asks cautiously what he had replied to Hyacine, receiving another copy and paste from Anaxa and hearing his laugh.

''You're a real idiot.''

''I've upset Hyacine.''

''You deserve it.''

˚ˋঌ˖ ˚ˋঌ˖ ˚ˋঌ˖ ˚ˋঌ˖

''Oh, De! What a surprise!'' Tribbie shouts, excitedly.

Mydei greets her politely, allowing the little Oracle to hug his leg.

After the rebirth of all the heirs, plus those who had fallen victim to the black tide, Mydei immediately left for his homeland in search of survivors.

In search... of him.

''What are you doing here?'' the Oracle asks, the prince tilting his head. ''I just wanted to visit you. To see how you are doing.''

''Awww, how sweet!''

''Pff... it's not sweetness! It's concern for my friends'' the prince snorts, unable to get angry with the little Oracle (even though she was much older than him).

Tribbie laughs, agreeing with him as if he were a child, taking him by the hand to lead him to where the others were.

''You've come at just the right time! Almost everyone is here!''

''Oh.''

''Cas will be so happy to see you! You weren't able to met her in our strange rebirth.''

''Yes... that's true. I owe her an apology.''

''Do you think she'll accept it?''

''Mmm... I doubt it'' Mydei smiles, because deep down he wants to see all his companions with whom he had forged a deep and sincere friendship.

Tribbie walked happily, pulling Mydei along, a beautiful family scene, but the prince's face darkened. ''Lady Oracle...''

''Call me Tribbie now. We don't have that position anymore. Hee hee, what a joy, right?''

Mydei nods weakly. ''Tri... Tribbie'' the little woman made a sound, letting him know she was listening. ''Have... have you found out anythi—''

''If we knew anything about him, you'd be the first one to know, De'' Tribbie whispers, still walking, but it was obvious that her joy had also faded.

Mydei nods guiltily. ''Yes, you're right. Forgive me, Lady Tribbie.''

''There's nothing to forgive, De. We all... we all miss him very much.''

The road to where the other former heirs were was long, so Mydei decided to lighten the mood he himself had ruined. ''You say almost all of them are here?'' Tribbie nods ''Who's missing?''

''Agy!''

''Lady Aglaea? Leaving Okhema? Is it serious?''

''Not at all'' Tribbie laughs. Mydei was relieved to hear the former oracle's laughter again. ''Naxy simply called her, asking for her help, and she went right away.'' Mydei raised his eyebrow, amused by Tribbie's gesture. ''And they've been together for three days ~~''

''And why are you making that face?'' asks Mydei, unable to stop himself from laughing. Truly, how happy that powerful little woman made him.

"You don't know? Agy and Naxy were lovers a long time ago! Even before Agy met Snowy!'' Mydei struggles not to grimace at the mention of that nickname. ''But when Agy took our mission so seriously... Naxy seemed to get angry with her, asking if she was willing to risk her humanity for the Titans, what sense did it make for them to stay together..."

''I don't know that man very well, but he seems like someone who would say that without worrying about the consequences of his words.''

''Naxy isn't the villain of the story, De. It hurt him deeply to see the woman he loves becoming colder and colder.''

''But... Aglaea, at least the one I knew...''

''Believe me, she was nothing compared to how she was centuries ago. Agy... Agy was more than a person, she was a refuge. A home.''

''And you deny that when I met her, or when our whole journey happened, it wasn't like that? Because that's how I felt.''

''But you weren't in love with her, De. Naxy would see it differently...''

Mydei sighs, but did not argue. Tribbie was right, he couldn't judge that man when he hadn't been in his situation.

...

Even though he was living in a similar situation.

The discovery of Phainon's true identity. Of the Flame Reaver...

And yet... Mydei still loves him. He still misses him so much.

Had he really lost him? Was Phainon really not going to be able to enjoy the dawn he had given them with his pain and sacrifice?

''De?'' Tribbie asks, worried.

''Oh, sorry, I got lost in my thoughts'' the prince apologises. Tribbie sighs sympathetically ''Your situation with Naxy is not at all the same. And well, Naxy and you... are not the same person either. It's unfair to judge that when two people will never react to the same situation in the same way.''

''You're right, Lady Tribbie. I... I wasn't judging, just...''

I just envy that man for having the opportunity to reconcile with his lost love...

He felt Tribbie's hand comforting him, but no words were spoken. She had already given him hope a few minutes ago; she shouldn't continue feeding him the possible lie that they would find Phainon sooner or later.

''So... she's been at the professor's house for three days, all alone?''

''Yes!'' Tribbie smiles.

''Wow... then I'm glad they're finally giving themselves a second chance.''

''Tell that to Cas!'' says another familiar voice as Hyacine and Castorice approached the pair.

''Why do you say that, Cinny?''

''Cas doesn't believe that the professor and Lady Aglaea are spending so much time together, without giving any sign of life, precisely because of a reconciliation.''

''Ha, you thinking that when you writes those novels? Curious'' Mydei teases her, Castorice laughing at that.

"Hello, Mydei. I missed you'' the woman smiles, Mydei nodding in agreement, hugging his friend who meant so much to him. Who understood him so well. ''And yes, despite what I write, I doubt those two are romantic enough to give themselves a second chance.''

''Uh... Cas... Lady Aglaea is the reincarnation of the Titan of Romance."

''And when Anaxa is around, all that romance dies like leaves on a tree in autumn.''

''Oh, how lyrical,’ whispers Mydei sarcastically, Castorice laughing at that. ''But I'm with Hyacine. I highly doubt they'll be together for long, without talking to all of you and... and not them talking about how to fix their relationship. Or at least how to be friends again.''

Tribbie nods to Mydei. ''We're in the Era Nova. If Agy has the chance to get back with the only love of her life, she'll take it. Besides, she deserves it.''

''Of course she deserves it, as well as the professor, and I hope they get back together.'' adds Castorice. ''But I can't help thinking about that shooting star.''

''Uh? What shooting star?'' asks Mydei, surprised.

"A shooting star fell very close to the Grove. From what I've been able to find out, no one else but the people who were near that place saw it in the sky. Knowing the professor, I can see him investigating that event rather than paying attention to any attempt at reconciliation on Lady Aglaea's part.''

''Then why did he calls her?'' Hyacine whispers, not quite sure of that logic.

''To help him? The professor respects and admires Lady Aglaea very much. I find that option more reasonable, knowing both of them and the relationship they have, that they are in that house... reminiscing about old times.''

''Hehehe'' Tribbies laughs, making Castorice blush.

''Hmm... a shooting star that only people near the Grove could see... We should go to the professor's house to see if your theory is true, Cast—''

''DON'T YOU DARE!'' Tribbie shouts, the three of them startled, surprised to see the sweet former oracle shout, ''If there's any chance that Agy will get back together with the love of her life, no one here is going to ruin it, you hear me!?''

''Yes, ma'am'' they all said at once.

Tribbie, relieved, began to walk away, Hyacine following her with a big smile on her lips, both of them theorising about what the other two might be doing.

Castorice went to follow them when he saw Mydei standing still. ''Are you coming, Mydei?''

Mydei, who has his gaze lost in the sky, nods slowly. ''Do you think that shooting star could be an important event? Something... that requires our attention to study?''

''If it fell near the Grove, the professor will be studying it, and if it didn't require our help, then it's not important.'' Mydei nods, not very sure, closing his eyes, calm, feeling his friend's touch on his arm. ''Don't keep wallowing in that pessimism and guilt. He wouldn't want that.''

Mydie nods again, finally following Castorice in an attempt to let his friends' company clears his mind.

He doesn't want that... but what he wants is him, na párei.

Chapter End Notes

⪩ 'na párei' it's supposed to be 'damn it' in greek. as always, please correct me if it's wrong.
