Chapter Summary

A fever, another hallucination and a necessary visit

Chapter Notes

Sorry for the delay x) I was enjoying my last days on holidays and the returning to this horrible capitalist system ruins my entire week and drains my energy.

But this fic always bless my day so hope it bless your day too (੭´꒳`)ᯓ★

See the end of the chapter for more notes

If they thought that Phainon's condition would improve because they had been able to talk to him, they were both very much wrong.

Two days after that horrible hallucination, Phainon developed such a high fever that even Anaxa became concerned.

''Do I need to call Hyacine?'' Aglaea asks, alarmed, immediately picking up her telestate when Anaxa did not answer.

His silence was the answer she needed.

''Wait! Let me think!'' Anaxa finally snorts, coming out of his trance.

''I'm not going to stand idly while a fever is killing him! And obviously we can't do anything for him! It's beyond our reach!''

Aglaea finally dialled the healer's number, but Anaxa grabbed the phone.

''WHAT ARE YOU DOING!?'' Aglaea roars like a lioness. ''ANAXA, I SWEAR BY ALL THAT IS HOLY, GIVE ME BACK—''

''Hyacine,'' Anaxa says, grabbing Aglaea's wrist with controlled force. "Yes, it's me. Yes, yes, I know it's Aglaea's telestate. I need you to come here, to my house, okay? Alone. And it's urgent.'' Anaxa's thumb traced a circle on Aglaea's skin to calm her down while he continues his conversation. ''You can trust me, Hyacine, but I need you here now. And please, use any excuse that isn't too suspicious. I don't want any heir in the Grove except you, okay? Aham... aham, yes. Thank you, Hyacine.''

Anaxa hung up, taking a deep breath, without letting go of the blonde's wrist. ''If you had spoken to her, Hyacine would have started crying, and Tribios would have come here immediately to find out what the hell had happened to you."

Aglaea nods, biting her lip. ''It's hard to believe what I've become.''

''An human?'' Anaxa raises his eyebrow.

''Someone who can't control her emotions.''

''An human.''

''Ugh, shut up!''

Aglaea slowly pulled away from Anaxa's grip, as if a greater force were compelling her to no longer feel the man's touch, and headed for the feverish man's room.

She sat down immediately at his side, changing the cloth on his forehead, Anaxa announcing that he would go and fetch another bowl and more clean cloths.

Aglaea thanks him, even though her blind gaze remained fixed on the sick man.

She couldn't see what he was doing, but it was obvious that he was still battling his nightmares. His memories.

...

His... eternal cycles.

Helpless, she rested her palm on the young hero's cheek, wishing her words would have the same effect as they had a few days ago.

But a few days ago, Phainon wasn't breathing as if it were his last breath.

A few days ago, they didn't have to clean his body of his own sweat every hour.

Anaxa was right. Phainon was in a bad way, and recovery would be difficult. But, and forgive her if she was being ignorant and deluded, Aglaea felt that Phainon had already suffered too much torment to have to endure that horrible fever in order to live.

To have that damn second chance he so deserved.

Aglaea opens her eyes in panic when Phainon began to murmur ''It burns... it burns.''

What did he mean? When he burned his own village and Phainon felt each of the flames licking his skin? All the golden, friendly blood he had spilled on his body? His... his transformation? Would his own body hurt him for all the coreflames he had accumulated? Would he suffer that torment... for life?

''No... enough, please... burns... it burns...'' he muttered hoarsely, fighting against something invisible, that tear spilling down his cheek unable to be dried due to Aglaea's blindness. ''M... mitéra... mitéra, where are you? Patéras... mit... éra...’'

The blonde shuddered when she hears Phainon call out to his parents like that. It sounded just like years ago, hell, centuries ago, when a still-human Aglaea found a poor lost and frightened child on the border of Okhema.

She saw his wounds and scars with a golden hue, and she took him in immediately, becoming a second mother to him, as she was to Cipher.

She remembered his nightmares, his cries, his screams, and how Aglaea or Cipher were always there to comfort him. To listen to him.

Her first instinct was to take his hand to show her support, but she found nothing there, having forgotten for a moment the young hero's new physical disability, so she sat closer to him, resting her forehead against Phainon's sweaty one.

•⋅⋯ ⋯⋅•

''Lady Aglaea?''

''Mm?'' murmured the then young heiress.

''I... I need to go''

''Hmm… G…go? Go where?''

''You know… gooo''

''Lady Aglaea... I'm thirsty…''

''You know you'll wake me in a few minutes to go to the bathroom, do you?''

''Haha''

''Lady Aglaea...''

.

.

.

Aglaea sighs internally when she hears the door, opening her eyes, curious, when a certain childish voice didn't wake her.

Her room was empty, but she swears she hears that door, and only one person will dare to enter at that hour.

When she goes outside, it wasn't difficult to find that boy. He was just next to the door, resting his head between his knees, surprised, like he was catched doing a bad thing, when he notices her presence.

''Why you didn't wake me up?''

''I… I didn't want to bother you more…''

Aglaea sighs again, that needle of guilt piercing her heart. She sits at his side, leading him to a hug, who he accepts gladly.

It was a nightmare, he says.

It was a memory.

''Do you want to sleep with me?''

•⋅⋯ ⋯⋅•

''Do you remember when Cipher discovered us and joined us? How we could hear the bedsprings groaning under the weight?'' Aglaea laughs bitterly, for the person she pictured was not the imposing, attractive hero who had all of Amphoreus in love.

Who had even charmed the prince of Castrum Kremnos himself.

No...

She would always picture Phainon as that little boy who shyly asked if he could sleep with her because of his nightmares, after so many nights waking her up to get a glass of water and, a few minutes later, waking her up again to go to the bathroom.

That innocent smile, those eyes shining with curiosity... for her, Phainon would always be that pure being of light and charisma.

Not the Flame Reaver.

Not pure chaos.

''I know I'm not your mother... but please, let me be enough for you, at least for now, so that you can stop suffering. I beg you, let me take away that pain, Phainon, dear, please'' she whispers in a choked sob as she felt the fever rise and the moans of terror and pain increase as well.

Aglaea tensed when Anaxa abruptly pulled her away from Phainon, demanding to know why he had done that. ''You scared me! Seeing you in that position and crying like that... I feared the worst!'' explains the man, turning his attention back to the feverish boy, unable to help but let out a sigh of relief.

''He's... he's dreaming about the destruction of his home... What do we do?'' she asks, lost and heartbroken. ''What can I do to take away his pain?'' Anaxa did not answer, knowing that Aglaea had already done everything in her power to calm the feverish man. ''I need Cipher... she would know what to do...'' she says, without thinking seriously about it.

It was a cry for help. A plea for a miracle to calm the delusions and nightmares of the man she loves like her own child.

Hearing him breathe like that... that hoarse, choked breathing, those trembling moans, full of fear... his constant but weak movement in bed, as if he were still fighting...

Every sound of pain that Phainon made was like daggers piercing her whole body. It was torture for her eardrums.

Anaxa sighed heavily, taking out one of the damp cloths to wipe the feverish boy's face and part of his chest. ''Come on, lad, you have to calm down. Don't you remember where we are?''

''Do you really think he can hear you?'' replied Aglaea, wearily.

''There's no harm in trying one more time.''

After several attempts, Phainon's body seemed to relax, and both carers sighed with relief, as they did not want to claim victory just yet.

But a cold shiver ran down Anaxa's spine when Phainon suddenly opened his eyes, the same golden colour as when he found him, and a cold, inexplicable gaze was directed at Aglaea.

As quickly as he could, Anaxa pushes Aglaea away from Phainon's attack. The young hero, having failed to achieve his goal, turns towards the alchemist, his wings regenerated, sprouting once more from his back.

Anaxa moves away with the same speed with which he had saved Aglaea from those black claws that had also appeared on Phainon's only arm, but with one of his wings, he struck him with such force that when he crashed into the wall of the room, Anaxa was left breathless for a few seconds.

Phainon tries to approach him, but his knees immediately buckles, a look of pure hatred directed at his professor. ''Flame... Reaver...'' Phainon whispers menacingly. Anaxa couldn't help but laugh at how surreal the situation was.

Now the fool was confusing him with himself.

''Boy, I hate to disappoint you, but...''

Anaxa fell silent as Phainon leapt towards him, like an eagle swooping down on a rabbit, ready to sink his claws into its soft fur.

But Phainon's wings were caught and tightly gripped by a golden thread, the transformed young hero hitting the ground much harder than Anaxa had.

Phainon raises his head angrily towards the culprit, turning towards Aglaea, his wings still immobile. Anaxa screams so terrified that anyone who heard him would doubt that it was their steadfast professor.

But Aglaea stopped Phainon's claw with her newly appeared sword, trapping him again with her threads and dodging all his attacks with an elegance worthy of the most beautiful of dances.

Finally, Phainon was completely trapped, a guttural growl rising from his chest as Aglaea maintained an indecipherable gaze on the young hero. On her foster son.

...

But she would not allow anyone attack Anaxa.

Phainon continued to struggle among the threads, like a trapped animal, his angry growls, full of rage, becoming stressed until they turned into nothing more than pitiful and confused whimpers.

And Aglaea loosens her grip...

''Phainon...''

Even though he was still bound, Aglaea kneels beside him, undoing the grip, her heart breaking when Phainon pulled away from her touch with a warning snort.

''Ph–Phainon, I... I'm sorry. I only meant to–''

''Aglaea, watch out!'' Anaxa shouts, the blind woman hearing desperate footsteps trying to reach her.

The last thing she felt was something warm on her cheek, and from the touch, she guessed it was blood. She senses Anaxa in front of her, struggling again with Phainon.

He held his only arm, trying to bend it, Aglaea coming to his aid immediately. ''Hold him tight, I'll be right there!'' Anaxa yells, Aglaea nodding and taking his place, trying to ignore the stressed and frightened, but angry yelps coming from Phainon's throat.

Anaxa was quick to arrive, also grabbing his arm and stretching it out, immediately explaining to the woman what he was going to do. ''I didn't want to recur to this. Not so soon, at least.''

Aglaea tries to help as best she could, holding the rest of Phainon's body while Anaxa continued to struggle to keep his arm still.

''Come on... don't be stubborn'' Anaxa snorts.

But when he manages to stick the syringe in, without administering the sedative, Phainon kicked him in the face, Anaxa cursing the young hero's entire family tree.

As he got up, his nose and lip bleeding profusely, Anaxa couldn't help but smile when Aglaea masterfully held Phainon down and squeezed the syringe, realising what her former partner was trying to do, as it was still stuck in his arm.

Phainon looks at the woman with pure hatred, his hand reaching for her neck, Anaxa trying to stop him in terror, but Aglaea was quicker and although Phainon's claws reached her skin, he grabs her by the shoulder, the woman remaining still and impassive in the face of the pain the young hero was causing her.

At least it wasn't her neck...

Anaxa slowly approaches them, standing still, his hands raised to show that he was no danger when Phainon looks at him again, as if he were his enemy.

As if... as if he really were the Flame Reaver. The cause of all his nightmares.

But Phainon's eyelids finally fell, and after uttering a bitter curse, he fell unconscious, the greatest sigh of relief ever uttered by the bearers of the coreflames of Romance and Reason being exhaled.

''Málakas...'' Anaxa snorts, wiping the blood that was still dripping from his cloak.

Aglaea pulled Phainon's claws out of her skin, as if they were knives, and the back of her hand immediately went to the young man's forehead. ''He still has a high fever.''

''Hyacine will be here soon. In fact, I thought she would have arrived already... better, I suppose.''

Aglaea nods, asking for help to lift him up, finally realising why he was larger and what she had managed to catch with her threads. ''Have his wings regenerated?'' Anaxa nodded with a sound. ''How?''

''I'd like to know that too.''

They stood still when they heard Phainon muttering again with rage and pain, the alchemist snorting, ''Don't make me give you a second injection, you damn paliópaido''

''Is it safe to have sedated him in that state?''

''It was either that or let him kill us, Aglaea.''

Aglaea nods, though she was not very happy about it.

''I... well, I wanted to thank you.'' Aglaea was surprised by this. ''If it hadn't been for your reflexes and quick thinking... ha, the brat could have killed me.''

''You saved me too. Where did he hurt you when you got between him and me?''

''He almost slit my throat, but I'm fin—''

Anaxa fell silent when he feels Aglaea's fingers on the wound Phainon's claws had inflicted. How could that woman express so much with her blind eyes?

Anaxa sighs softly, unable to resist resting his lips on the woman's hair. ''I'm fine. It could have been worse.''

''Those claws... they could have reached your neck...'' he recalled with horror, while his hands instinctively wrapped around the woman's figure, as a way of ensuring that they were both okay.

Aglaea responds to that touch by resting her forehead on the curve of the alchemist's neck, both remaining in that embrace, silent and calm, for barely a minute but wishing it could last forever.

''We should heal ourselves before Hyacine arrives and sees us like this'' Anaxa broke the spell, much to his regret.

When they called the young healer, it was morning. They waited for her arrival in the afternoon, but Hyacine did not arrive until late at night.

When Anaxa opens the door, he could not help but laugh at the terrified look his student gave him.

And how could she not... with his face bruised like that and his chest bandaged.

''It's nothing, don't worry.''

''What did you say to Lady Aglaea, Professor Anaxa!?''

''It's Anaxágoras, and that idiot didn't do this to me. Do you really think she's that brutish!?''

''Who are you calling an idiot?'' a voice sounds in the background, Hyacine smiling as she saw Aglaea coming down the stairs.

Her smile immediately faded when she saw her bandaged shoulder. She completely ignored the fact that the blond was wearing one of her beloved professor's pyjama's T-shirts. ''Why are you both injured? Is that why you made me come?''

''Do I look like I want to waste your time like that, child?'' Anaxa snorts, Hyacine placing her hands on her hips. ''Then why—''

Hyacine's question was cut short by a scream. A scream that Anaxa and Aglaea were already too accustomed to hearing, but obviously for Hyacine it must have been... shocking. Overwhelming.

The healer paled when she recognises the voice that belonged to that scream, and after seeing the two figures she most respected in Amphoreus nod weakly, Hyacine ran towards the room where the scream was coming from.

When she opens the door, she couldn't help but freeze, her beautiful blue eyes wet, tears streaming down her face.

Phainon was curled up on the bed, the sheet tangled between his legs, one arm ending in a clawed hand scratching his head hard, and an expression of anguish and pain showing on his closed-eyed face.

Hyacine turned to demand explanations from the other two, but when Phainon groans this time in anguish and pain, the healer shook her head and ran to him, immediately assessing his condition.

''How long has he had this fever?'' she asks with a trembling voice.

''For about two days'' Anaxa replies.

''And why didn't you tell me right away?'' Hyacine snorts, both surprised at how sharp the sweet and understanding healer sounded.

But... could they blame her?

Before Anaxa could answer, Aglaea spoke up for him. ''We thought we could handle it. But clearly we couldn't. His fever keeps rising and his nightmares...'' Hyacine twists her lip in sorrow, looking back at her friend. ''They're getting worse.''

Hyacine nods, getting down to work.

A halo of water grew around Phainon's head, and Hyacine's hands glowed. But the young hero's face remained unchanged, when normally, just being touched by Hyacine meant finding peace of mind.

''How long has he been with you?''

''For two weeks'' Anaxa replies.

''Ha... so Cas was right... You didn't call Lady Aglaea to...'' Hyacine press her lips together, making no attempt to hide her sobs. ''You should have told us right away.''

''We wanted to, but...''

''Phainon's condition is still too delicate for him to have so many people looking after him'' this time it was Anaxa who came to Aglaea's aid.

''We would have waited!''

''We both know you wouldn't have, Hyacine. Castorice would respect the decision, but she wouldn't be resting. The last thing Tribios needs is to feel useless because she can't do anything for his Snowy. Cipher would be capable of committing a crime to help Phainon and Mydei... Ha. Don't get me started on him.''

''How would you feel if it were Aglaea lying here instead of Phainon?'' Hyacine replies angrily, leaving Anaxa speechless.

The alchemist sighs resignedly, Aglaea approaching the young healer, squeezing her shoulder affectionately. "I was afraid, Hyacine. Afraid of... of telling you and getting your hopes up. Of hurting you more. Of hurting him more. All these wounds were caused by Phainon. How do you think he would feel if he hurt you? Or Castorice or Cipher? How is it going to fix his situation if he hurts Mydei or Tribios again?''

''We... we would never hold it against him" Hyacine replies, weakly.

''Another one like you,'' Anaxa snorts , Aglaea laughing weakly, answering for him. "I know perfectly well. Just like Anaxa and I, we're not angry with him for breaking both our noses. But him? How do you think he'll feel when he remembers everything he did in the previous cycles? Do you think he only killed you once? Castorice or Cipher? I remind you that, as far as we know, in all those cycles, more than 30 million, it was he who killed Mydei, a supposedly immortal being." Hyacine bits her lip, but did not cut the woman off.

Her healing was still underway, but her shoulders trembled at everything she was experiencing at that moment.

Her friend was alive, but in that state. The lies of the people she respected most, and at the same time, she understood the reason for those lies.

The... the torture that Phainon had suffered and continued to suffer...

Despite still being angry with him, Hyacine accepted the touch of her beloved professor, sobbing when he kissed her on the top of her head. A gesture he had only made once in his life and one she would always treasure. ''We are very sorry we didn't tell you. And we will apologise to the rest of our companions. But Aglaea is right, Hyacine. Until Phainon's mental state improves, it is best that as few people as possible know about it.''

''Mydei will now be very suspicious. Why do you think I took so long to come? He's wondering about that meteorite that only fell in the Grove.'' Hyacine looked up, hurt. ''It was him, wasn't it?'' Anaxa nods, now hugging her student, unable to continue with the healing.

Anaxa continued to hug her while Aglaea stroked her back, until a frightened groan from Phainon broke that comfort, Hyacine getting back to work, as if she were letting Phainon die by breaking down like that upon hearing such information.

Hyacine looked at his friend's body, her lips widening in sorrow at the sight of his stump. ''I need you to tell me everything about him. From when you found him until now. I need to know what he's going through so I can heal him as he needs and deserves.''

Both elders nodded, and it was Anaxa who gave him all the information, from how he found him in the Grove and cared for him, to the arrival of Aglaea and the two occasions when Phainon hallucinated and attacked them.

''So the second time was the one of this morning?''

Anaxa nods.

''It's really been a relief that you were so late'' Aglaea confessed.

''Yeah... It would have been really awkward if you had arrived just as we were trying to stop this idiot from killing us'' Anaxa replies, earning an amused snort from Aglaea.

Hyacine nodded weakly, a false, tired smile appearing on her face.

The poor girl didn't know what to feel. She was still hurt by what the people she admired most in all of Amphoreus had done.

And Phainon's situation...

Fortunately, her healing was taking effect, and for several minutes now, Phainon's breathing had returned to near normal, as had his fever, which, although it had not disappeared, had dropped significantly.

Aglaea also noticed this when she touched the young man's forehead, Hyacine observing how Phainon's face softened, turning towards her palm. After taking his temperature, the palm of the Okhema leader rested on the feverish man's cheek.

Hyacine finally managed to smile sincerely, though still tired, at the scene she witnessed, Aglaea raising her eyebrow curiously at the soft laugh that had been heard.

''I had forgotten that you basically raised Phainon. He seems so calm with you.''

Aglaea nods, pleased to be the second person to say that, when Hyacine let out an excited and nervous sound.

Asking what was wrong, Hyacine replies that he had woken up.

''Phai... you're awake'' the healer smiles, not hiding her tears. ''How are you feeling?''

''Where is Anaxa?'' Aglaea asks when she did not hear the man speak. ''He was here a moment ago.''

Although her palm was still on the wounded man's cheek, she did not like the atmosphere in the room. She needed him now.

''Huh? I-I don't know. If he left the room, I didn't notice. Phainon, can you understand me?'' Hyacine immediately dismissed Aglaea's question, as it was quite clear that at that moment all she cared about was being able to talk, even if only for a millisecond, with the friend she thought he would never see again.

But Aglaea still felt uncomfortable, cursing her blindness for not being able to see Phainon's expression. But she knew that silence when his eyes were open very well.

''Hyacine,'' Aglaea whispers, trying to push her away from the mattress with her other arm. The other looking confused and frightened. ''Wh-what's going on?''

''Find Anaxa, please. Tell her to com—''

''I'm already here. What the hell is going on?'' the man snorts, grumpy.

''Where were you!?''

''Just seeing if we have all the necessary food for the din— who cares!? What's wrong!?''

''Tell me how Phainon looks'' Aglaea got straight to the point.

Hyacine stiffens when Anaxa also paled and tried to pull her away from her friend. She backed away, indignant. ''What's going on? Have I done something wrong and I can't see it?''

''No, dear! You haven't done anything wrong'' Aglaea tries to reassure her.

''But he's not fully awake. And when he's this disoriented, he's quite unpredictable.''

''He's basically been unpredictable since I brought him home'' didn't say Anaxa.

Hyacine opened her mouth to argue, turning to Phainon, her hands trembling. ''Can I at least talk to him?''

The elders looked at each other but nodded, Hyacine taking her place again, bringing her hands close to Phainon's body but without touching him. ''Phai... I... haha, just...'' Her tears prevented her from continuing, shaking her head because she needed to talk to him. She needed to hear his answer. To hear his voice again... ''I'm so glad you're here...''

''Go away'' Phainon whispers, frightened.

The three tighten up at this request, and above all, at Phainon's tone.

Hyacine blinks, confused, trying to get closer to Phainon. ''Please, go'' the young man begs again, getting up from the bed to get away from Hyacine's touch.

Faced with this reaction, Hyacine pulled her arm away as if she had been burned, her beautiful face contorted with pain and confusion.

Hyacine whispers his name again, affected. Confused and hurt, Phainon hid his face with his only remaining palm, and tears that evaporated instantly fell from his eyes.

Blue eyes but with a golden glow.

Anaxa did not want to risk facing a god with Phainon's face again, so he gently took Hyacine's shoulders and accompanied her to the door.

But Hyacine couldn't help turning back, needing, as if it were oxygen, an answer to that reaction. ''Phai... I—if I hurt you, if when you had to fight me I hurt you on any occasion, I'm sorry—''

''I killed you...'' whispers Phainon, with a regret that was devastating.

With a coldness that could freeze even the stars themselves.

''I killed you... so many times...'' he repeats again, shaking his head. ''Your screams... your... pleas...''

Phainon's claw reappeared, but fortunately not his wings. ''I'm sorry... I'm sorry...''

Anaxa warns Aglaea to grab his wrist and pull it away from his face, as he was digging his own claws into his skull, golden blood spurting from between the whitish strands, while he kept apologising incessantly to her healer friend.

''Let's go'' Anaxa says firmly, pulling Hyacine out of the room, hurt by her student when he handled her as if she were a rag doll.

⌞ ────────⌝

Closing the door behind her, Anaxa took her to the kitchen and sat her down on a chair while he fetched something, anything, that might cheer the young woman up.

But she remained lost in thought, dark circles already forming on her face from all the tears she had shed.

Anaxa sighed affectionately, taking a clean cloth to wipe her face.

''I don't want to bring it up again, but do you understand why we've kept it from all of you?'' Anaxa whispers, with a gentleness that even surprised him.

Hyacine did not answer. She was still crying, silently, breaking down completely when her beloved teacher hugged her.

While he held her warmly and tightly in his arms, letting her cry and release all that bitterness while she could feel safe, Anaxa took out his telestate and asked Aglaea how Phainon was doing.

Anaxa blocks the telestate, sighing regretfully, stroking the back of his beloved student.

Really... why did everything have to be so complicated?

So unfair!?

Anaxa managed to convince the young healer to rest in the other room, Hyacine moving as if she were a puppet controlled by the man she trusted most.

After assuring her that not only would they talk tomorrow, but that Phainon might be alive thanks to her, Anaxa let her rest, debating whether or not to enter his own room.

He had heard no screams or blows, and he knew that Aglaea had not left the room.

Would they be all right? Was Aglaea still reassuring a terrified Phainon about seeing again the friend whom fate had forced him to kill her so many times?

If Anaxa, deep down felt a little guilty when his words had hurt his students, how much more painful would it be to hear the screams of terror and pain of your loved ones and know that you were the cause of that horror?

Desperate to know the boy's condition, he opened the door carefully, laughing softly but relieved at the scene he witnessed.

''Aglaea... you are... málakas, you are unique'' thought the alchemist, approaching the bed.

Aglaea was lying on her side, her left arm resting on Phainon's side while the other stroked his hair.

The claw had disappeared, and the layer of sweat that had been on him for two days was also nowhere to be seen.

Anaxa couldn't help but approach to witness that ethereal and magnificient face, arching his eyebrow amusedly when those blind eyes opened.

''What kind of magic do you do?'' he whispers softly so as not to wake the sleeping man.

''I can't believe it worked either'' the woman replies. ''To be honest, it took me a while to calm him down.''

''But you did. You calmed the grief of a man who has had to watch a friend he has killed for millions of cycles. Don't be humble now.''

Aglaea snorts, eliciting another laugh from the alchemist. ''How is she?''

''Bad. We'll talk more tomorrow.''

''I hope the fever is gone by tomorrow. I don't want both of them to have to deal with something similar as today all over again'' Aglaea whispers, kissing the feverish forehead gently.

Anaxa nodded with a sullen sigh. ''He calmed down when I hummed the same lullaby my mother used to sing to me'' Aglaea's voice sounded again.

''Oh? Hummed? You denied Phainon the privilege of hearing your beautiful voice?''

''I swear to all the Titans, I can't stand you'' Aglaea snorts again. ''Please leave before you wake him up'' she growls softly when Anaxa laughs, a little low.

But he approaches the bed, cursing Aglaea's blindness, for she would have given anything to see his smile that said, ''I'm only here to annoy you.''

Although, to tell the truth, she didn't even need to see his expression. Just by sensing his presence, the woman was already able to perceive the man's intentions. ''Anaxágo—''

''Ah, ah, ah'' he cuts her, she rolling her eyes in exasperation. ''Is he listening to us?''

''I hope not, because if you wake him up—''

''Because he's just as calm as he was two days ago. Ha, you little brat. It calms him down to hear us arguing.''

''It's more likely that it calms him to hear you bothering me'' Aglaea replies.

''Tsk tsk, how awful of you, Phainon, to enjoy your mother's suffering.''

''I'm not her—ugh, Anaxa, please. Today has been a very hard day.''

''And I can see your lips struggling not to form a smile'' Anaxa replies smugly.

Aglaea pressed her lips even tighter, finally forming that relieved and sincere smile, followed by a small laugh. ''What a day... what am I saying, what a week, damn it.''

''It's possible that the boy reacted that way because of what happened this morning. Maybe another day, when he's had several decent breaks like the one he's having now, he'll be able to see Hyacine or anyone else.''

''I hope so...''

Aglaea returns to her initial posture, resuming her caresses of the whitish strands. Anaxa couldn't help but let out a sigh laden with many emotions.

''You have no idea how happy it makes me to see you like this'' he couldn't help but confess, seeing the woman's tension at those words.

Faced with Aglaea's silence, Anaxa turned away, announcing that he would sleep on the sofa in the dining room, as Hyacine deserved to rest in a bed after all she had done for them.

But before he closed the door, Aglaea called him back, Anaxa's heart, his new heart, untouched by experiments, beating strongly and nervously.

"...

Thank you... for letting me know. For accepting me... accepting us into your home.

I missed it.''

Anaxa nods, once again stopped by Aglaea's whisper, smiling from ear to ear, finally closing the door behind him.

''I missed you.''

Chapter End Notes

⪩ As always, málakas it's supposed to be ''damn, fuck'' and paliópaido like ''brat''. Please correct me if that's wrong. Mitéra and Patéras ofc it's supposed to be ''mother'' and ''father''

⪩ Sorry Phainon, you're being written by a girl who loves whump, so don't mind if you're suffering a little more (｡•́ ̫ •̀｡)

⪩ Someone catch the reference in the flashback between Aglaea and child Phainon? 𐔌՞. .՞𐦯

⪩ So Aglaea was right after all. Phainon can't deal with the fact that he has to kill his friends, over and over again. When I play 3.4, I truly thought the battle against Mydeimos will be the one who broke my heart but nope... that scene with Hyacine... her cries... her fear... I'm playing HSR in chinese and her VA do a magnificient work, she made me shear tears ;__; 3.4 it's a fucking trauma, I swear.

⪩ And finally, Aglanaxa is moving forward (˶˃ ᵕ ˂˶) I should add the slowburn tag to both of the ships of this fic 𐔌՞. .՞𐦯

Chapter Notes

Sorry for being so late!! I like to have at least one chapter ahead before posting a new one, and the next chapter was so difficult to write it ~~

See the end of the chapter for more notes

When Hyacine woke up, her professor had already prepared breakfast for her.

She couldn't help but smile faintly when she sees exactly what she likes best. Was that man really that observant?

''How was your night?'' he asks.

She simply shrugged, Anaxa nodding sympathetically.

He urges her to sit down and eat, squeezing her shoulder as he walked behind her, joining her for breakfast.

''What about Lady Aglaea?''

''She'll have breakfast in her room.''

Hyacine nods, her feet shifting nervously, biting her lip hard enough not to hurt herself.

Before she could speak, Anaxa sighs. ''He's fine. Aglaea managed to calm him down in the end.''

''Heh, they really are like mother and son.''

''Don't tell her that, it sounds like we're disrespecting Phainon's biological parents by even suggesting that'' Anaxa rolls his eyes, making his student laugh.

Hyacine was holding her breakfast's cup in her hands, but she still hadn't eaten anything. ''In Okhema... it was... adorable to see how Phainon seemed willing to carry out every mission Aglaea sent him on. As if he really wanted to prove to her that she could trust him. That he wouldn't let her down.''

''Why do you say it as if Aglaea saw Phainon as a disappointment?''

''I didn't mean to, Professor,'' Hyacine whispers "but... you weren't there during her real decline. It was... hard to see what she had become.'' Anaxa made an ugly, pained grimace, but did not replies to his beloved student. ''But Phainon remained the same with her. It didn't matter that she responded with a cold stare. It didn't matter that her tone showed impatient disappointment at not achieving our goal. It didn't matter that Aglaea directed her anger towards Phainon when she mistrusted Stelle and Dan Heng... He was always by her side...''

Anaxa nods, his long sigh lasting longer than he would have liked.

''And when she passed away... Phainon... I truly swore I saw the light in his eyes disappear. The hope. The desire to... keep fighting..."

''But he kept them.''

Hyacine nods, her eyes moistening again. ''He kept them for too long'' she couldn't avoid to replies, biting her lip so she wouldn't cry again.

Anaxa shows his support once more, the poor healer still unaccustomed to such displays of affection from the man she admired most. "It's hard. What he's had to endure is hard. That we discovered the truth. That... that now he has to recover from all that suffering.'' Hyacine nods, hiding her face in her palms, silent sobs being the only response Anaxa received. ''But now he's here. And he's trying. Yesterday... well...''

''You two were the ones who suffered the least under his sword. It's understandable that... your presence affects him less than mine. Than the others.''

Anaxa sighs, relieved that Hyacine finally understood. ''Besides...'' the young woman adds ''the way Phainon sees us is not the same as the way he sees Lady Aglaea and you.''

''Oh? And how does he see me?'' he raises his eyebrow, curious.

''Aww, come on, Professor,'' Hyacine laughs, wiping away her last tears. ''Are you serious?''

But Hyacine was concerned by how serious the man had become, and how his gaze seemed to be lost.

''Aglaea... says the same thing. That I am not aware of how important I have been to Phainon's life.''

''You have been, Professor!'' Hyacine confirmed.

''And I never realised it, it seems,'' he shakes his head, unable to help feeling disappointed. ''And... I'm sure I've given Phainon that impression. That... he was never been important to me.''

Faced with Hyacine's silence, Anaxa let out a dry laugh, confirming his sad suspicions.

But he was surprised to feel his sweet student's touch on his wrist. ''Well... you said it. Now we're here. All of us. Let's not dwell on the past and take advantage of this present he has given us.''

Anaxa couldn't help but laugh at his student's words, agreeing with her.

After a few seconds of peace, the professor snapped, with something resembling a sharp bark, that she must finish her breakfast.

Hyacine waited outside when Anaxa left the room, immediately asking about her friend's condition.

''His fever has dropped to 38º.'' *

''He still has a fever'' Hyacine mutters, dissatisfied.

''But it's not life-threatening. And it's closer to dropping to 36º than rising back to 40º. I remind you, my dear student, that when you arrived, Phainon's fever was almost reaching 42º.''

''And I'm sure when he transformed, it exceeded 44º...'' Anaxa decided to remain silent.

Hyacine nods, an awkward silence falling between them, until Anaxa decided to take a chance and break it, asking if she wanted to come in and say goodbye.

''No,'' the young woman says too quickly ''N–no... I don't want to come back and... bother him like that.''

Anaxa sighs, accompanying her downstairs, his hand once again on the healer's shoulder.

‘I have a theory that he reacted that way to you because of the horrible hallucination he had before you arrived. Maybe now, or tomorrow, or next week, who knows, he'll be eager to talk to you again.’

The smile Hyacine gave was so sad that it broke Anaxa's heart, leading to another awkward hug.

''Do you know, Professor, that you're terrible at comforting people?'' Hyacine decidea to break the ice, laughing at the man's snort. ''Stop agreeing with that arrogant woman, my dear student.''

Returning to the main topic, Hyacine asked for only one thing: that they ask Phainon if she could really be with him.

If... the others could be with him.

''When he's lucid, I'll ask him,'' Anaxa promised, and Hyacine nodded with satisfaction. ''Stay here for a couple of days, in the Grove. That way, if my theory is correct and Phainon really needs you, he'll have you right away.''

''There is nothing I want more than to be by his side, but... his comfort is paramount, Professor. Please remember that.''

''Of course'' he adds quietly, hurt to hear his student's throat catch again.

When he returns to the room, it was the image he was so accustomed to.

Phainon asleep and Aglaea's hand buried in his white hair.

The hero's face was still turned towards the woman, as if he did not want to move away from her touch under any circumstances.

Anaxa sighs heavily to get the blonde's attention. ''You should rest. You're about to surpass the boy with the ugliest dark circles under eyes.''

As expected, Aglaea shriekes in disagreement. ''He still has a fever...''

''A shitty fever. It's barely there.'' Anaxa places his hand on Phainon's forehead, opening his eyes in disbelief. ''It's not even warm anymore!'' he snorts indignantly when Aglaea twists her lip. ''Did you know that?''

''It could come back at any moment,'' the woman tries to defend herself, Anaxa bringing his hand to his face where he had taken the temperature, rubbing it under his only eye. ''Stop it!'' Aglaea shouts.

''I'm not doing anything'' he tries to defend himself.

''The way you're reacting! It's driving me crazy!''

''You're the one who's driving me crazy. Any minute by now, I'm going to find you lying on the floor, unconscious, because you're not getting enough rest! Should I remind you that you're still hurt from what happened yesterday!?'' Anaxa scolds her, so seriously that the blonde didn't even argue back.

She turned her face to Phainon, then looked down at the floor, shaking her head. She opened her mouth to try to defend herself, but they had already had this conversation several times. ''He'll be fine, Aglaea—''

''The last time we left him alone for so long was three days ago. And what happened to him? He developed a fever that almost killed him!''

''He was alone for less than six hours, Aglaea, for all the stupid Titans,'' Anaxa snorts, rubbing his hand across his face again. ''the same thing would have happened to him if you had been there! No! In fact, it would have been worse, because I would have had to take care of both of you!''

Finally, he managed to defeats Aglaea in that verbal argument, taking a risk after the conversation they had yesterday, and sits down next to her, affectionately squeezing her shoulder.

He felt that they no longer had to interact as if there were shards of glass on the floor where they walked and had to be careful. He felt that the Aglaea in front of him was truly the woman he had fallen deeply in love with, and not the light of Okhema.

What did he care if all of Okhema, or even Amphoreus, felt safe thanks to her divinity, if it was at the cost of taking away the most beautiful thing that woman had, which was her personality? Her humanity?

He couldn't help but smile when Aglaea rested her head on his shoulder, and he squeezed her hug affectionately. "You can't neglect your health to take care of him, Aglaea. It's not good for you or for him. And the poor boy already feels enough guilt without adding more burden, don't you think?''

''And what do you suggest? That you take care of him?''

''I'm more rested than you are.''

''That doesn't mean you're completely rested. Besides, I remind you that you came off worse in what happened yesterday'' she replies, rightly so.

Anaxa responds with a tired sigh, ''No wonder hospitals need so many staff.'' His only eye looked down at the only figure sleeping. ''You're such a pain in the arse, paliópaido.''

Anaxa laughed when Aglaea hit him hard on the arm, but she wore that radiant smile that, even with all his studies combined, it couldn't get a single word out of Anaxa.

With a gentle push, Anaxa urged her to rest again, relieved but also surprised when the woman obeyed him.

After closing the door, Anaxa crosses his legs, thoughtful, without taking his eyes off the sleeping figure.

''You never stopped to think about how much Phainon appreciates you. I'm sure he can't even believe that it was you who saved him.''

''The way Phainon sees us is not the same as the way he sees Lady Aglaea and you.''

''How he sees you.''

Y̢̦̝͚̥̲̼̑ͤ͝͞O̧ͬ̑Ų̵̴̺̮̦̏͊̔ͣ͑͝

''Mmpfff... lad, even without doing anything, you give me headaches'' Anaxa mutters, unconsciously imitating what Aglaea always did with Phainon.

Resting his hand on that soft, whitish mop of hair.

Anaxa knew what he was doing. He knew what he was going to do. That didn't mean his limbs didn't want to work, as if comforting his poor student wasn't in his system.

But he remembered when he found him.

That look.

That fear.

That... that torture, after so many cycles... And all for them...

He exhales a long sigh, only his thumb moving in the hero's hair, clicking his tongue when he heard a peaceful sleeping sigh from Phainon.

And in that moment, he felt great pity for Aglaea, for not being able to see what the two of them had caused.

That Phainon would once again wear that face full of peace and calm.

Anaxa took advantage of his time watching over Phainon to change his bandages and heal his wounds, relieved to see that the young hero did not seem uncomfortable or tense at all the movement around his body.

He also cleaned the room as quietly as possible. He placed another damp cloth on the young man's forehead, as when he took his temperature again, it was still 37 degrees.

He checked his own wardrobe to see if any of his clothes would fit Phainon when he recovered, realising that, even though the young man was much thinner and had less muscle mass, he was still a damn tower.

''I'll tell Hyacine to buy him something while she's here...''

The Sun was already setting on the horizon when Anaxa felt the need to leave that suffocating room.

After making sure Phainon was resting well, he leaves, his feet leading him without thinking to his sister's room.

To where Aglaea was resting.

He stood in front of the door, motionless, not knowing what to do.

Knock on the door? What if she was still asleep and he woke her up?

Open it? Watch her sleep? As he had done so many times in the past?

No... he couldn't do that.

He couldn't violate her privacy like that...

Even though he was burning with desire to return to...

''What are you doing?'' an amused voice whispers behind him.

Anaxa jumps, startled, snorting at the enjoyment his fright had caused the woman. ''Spying on me, huh?''

''It's not spying if I haven't opened the door'' he defends himself smugly, eliciting another laugh from the blonde.

She moves elegantly to stand beside him, her eyebrows raises playfully, as if waiting for Anaxa to speak.

''You seem to be in a better mood.''

''I am in a better mood.''

''Hmm... who would have thought that listening to me would help you'' Anaxa teases, laughing at the simple gesture of annoyance he had caused in the blonde.

It seemed she was even enjoying it...

They stood still, in silence, in front of the lonely room.

Would she go back to sleep? Would she suggest that Anaxa rest now so she could go back to taking care of Phainon?

But the woman came up with something Anaxa did not expect at all.

''Did you really miss me?''

Anaxa blinks, incredulous at such stupidity. ''Did you really just ask me that, anóitos?''

The way Anaxa responded, so softly, so... tenderly, sent a shiver down the blonde's spine.

She had completely forgotten how that conceited, lonely man could sound when... when he softens his heart.

Aglaea couldn't help but laugh, avoiding her blind gaze for her face won't be on reach of Anaxa's one eye.

She shooks her head, biting her lip. ''What troubles you, dear Aglaea?''

''I can't believe this is happening.''

''That I'm admitting I missed you?''

''And to hear you speak like that again... I can even imagine your face. How... how you are looking at me right now.''

''And how am I looking at you?'' Aglaea opens her mouth but closes it instantly, lowering her face again, embarrassed. ''As if you were the most beautiful thing that ever existed in Amphoreus?''

Anaxa's silence demanded an answer, and Aglaea slowly gave it, nodding in response to the question. ''Heh. Well, tell your blind eyes that they are not mistaken.''

''Anaxa'' Aglaea breathes, as if she were drowning.

''Aglaea?'' he raises his eyebrows in amusement, wanting to know what she really wanted to say.

''We can't go back to the past. That relationship... it's dead.''

''But we're not the same after our break-up either. Or would you say we are?'' Faced with Aglaea's silence, Anaxa moved closer to her, his nose barely an inch from her face. "Do you consider yourself the same woman that Tribios always looked at with concern? The one Hyacine and Castorice mourned because she was no longer the same? The same one who broke my heart and Phainon's trust in order to achieve her goal?"

''I had to do it...''

''What did I just say, you idiot?'' Anaxa whispers affectionately, grabbing Aglaea's wrist when she raised her hand to try to defend herself from those verbal attacks. ''But come on, you're not going to deny that it hurts you to have behaved like that. To have been like that.''

''Of course! It... it tears me apart inside to know how much damage I've done in order for this damn Era Nova to happen'' she replies with a rage that Ceres knew had been repressed for so long.

''So?''

''So what?'' Aglaea snorts, Anaxa joining her, but in an amused tone. ''Do you think we don't deserve a second chance?''

''Do you really think I deserve it, when ever since I've been with you, I've only felt regret for my decision to end my own humanity?''

That confession only elicited a smug and proud smile from the alchemist, his hand cradling that jaw he had done so many times in the past, and yet that touch was still electrifying to him.

''You deserve everything, Aglaea.''

Daringly, Anaxa rested his forehead on the woman's, savouring her breath, their lips brushing against each other, when a loud sound was heard beyond the corridor.

Specifically in the bathroom area.

As if cold water had been thrown on them, they stood paralysed, their lips still just millimetres apart. Anaxa moved away, with difficulty, as if his body did not want to, from where they both stood to look at the door to his own room.

And a rage, so in keeping with his impatience, arose from the depths of his being when he found the door open and, as far as he could see, the room empty.

''I swear I'll kill him'' Anaxa snorts, eliciting a giggle from Aglaea as they both headed towards the source of the sound.

''You!'' Anaxa barks, startling the injured young man who was picking up the broken glass from the vase he had knocked over. ''What the hell are you doing? Drop that right now or you'll cut yourself!''

Phainon backed away as if he were a puppy that had just been chased with a rolled-up newspaper, while Anaxa finished picking up what he had broken.

Aglaea came to the hero's aid, squeezing his shoulder affectionately and asking sympathetically what had happened.

''I... uh, well... I wanted to go to the bathroom and... I tripped...''

''Because you're not ready to walk on your own yet, paliópaido,'' Anaxa snorts, throwing the broken glass in the bin. ''Besides, you know perfectly well that you can use the bath without even leaving your bed. Just call us...''

''It's humiliating, Professor'' Phainon interrupted, closing his eyes and avoiding his gaze.

Anaxa opens his mouth again to speak, but the breath he took before launching into his tirade caught Aglaea's attention, and with a simple gesture, she silenced the man she loves.

Anaxa closes his mouth, swallowing his words, snorting through a small opening as he crossed his arms indignantly.

After nodding, satisfied, Aglaea guided Phainon to the toilet, squeezing his shoulder affectionately once more, and left the bathroom, dragging Anaxa with her, closing the door to give the sick man the privacy he needed and deserved.

Anaxa looks at the closed door and then at Aglaea, letting out another irritated sigh. ''Are you sure you want to leave him alone?''

''It won't even be a minute, Anaxa.''

''But—''

''We must take care of his mental health as well as his physical health, and respecting his dignity is a good way to do that.''

Anaxa snorted, but did not argue with the woman, massaging her forehead, unable to help laughing. ''Damn brat. He truly kills the mood…'' Aglaea replies with a half-smile, ''I don't even remember everything we had sai—''

The man was silenced when Aglaea took hold of his fabric, pulling him towards her, joining their lips.

Anaxa was paralysed for only half a second before wrapping his arms around the waist of the woman he had loved and admired so much, pulling her closer to him. That deep, needy kiss was interrupted sooner than either of them would have liked because they heard the chain ring.

When they separated, Anaxa could only see that mischievous, amused smile that Aglaea only gave him, and as she tapped his nose with her slender finger, they moved completely away from each other when the door opened.

Phainon came out, Anaxa swearing that if he had a tail and ears, they would be drooping, his mentor having no choice but to sigh and show genuine concern for him and not just irritation.

''Do you need help getting to bed?'' Anaxa raises his eyebrow, confused, when Phainon stared between the figures of his two carers, immediately turning away, his eyes narrowing as if in pain.

Anaxa didn't know if he was looking at the small space between Aglaea and Anaxa... or the wounds they still bore from the previous day.

Was the boy really going to behave towards them now as he had behaved towards Hyacine?

''I don't like being left without an answer'' he snorts, trying to bring back the blessed normality of a few days ago.

''I... I don't think so.''

Anaxa and Aglaea nod at the same time, giving the young man space to reach it on his own, when on the fourth step, his knees buckled, Aglaea being quick to catch him before he fell face first onto the floor.

Anaxa reached the other side, the path to the bed being easier and faster.

''I understand that you need privacy to do your things, lad'' Anaxa says suddenly, ''but call us, even if it's just to help you get up. To walk.''

''I wanted to stop being useless'' Phainon mutters, biting his lip, hurt, seeing how his words had wounded Aglaea.

''You're not useless, you're stupid for believing that,'' Anaxa snorts. ''You're injured, Phainon, so it's normal to be dependent. You shouldn't be ashamed of that, especially not with us. Especially not with her'' he says angrily, pointing at the blonde, who finally asked for peace.

She sat down next to Phainon, who accepted her touch on his knee. ''You know perfectly well that Anaxa and I are happy to help you with anything.''

''You don't have a minute's rest for yourselves. I don't leave any of you any privacy. I wanted... to stop being a nuisance,'' Phainon squeezed his eyes shut, as if he couldn't see his two carers in the face. ''To stop being a danger.''

''You'll be a nuisance when you're healthy and still here, getting on our nerves,'' Anaxa replies, "but for now, please get it into that empty head of yours that you need us. And that you are not at all a burden or a nuisance to us. Much less a danger.'' After taking a deep breath, Anaxa sat down in the empty space left on the bed, affectionately squeezing Phainon's neck, just as a father would. ''We want to help you, Phainon. Understand that once and for all, damn it.''

''But... yesterday—"

''What do you remember?'' Aglaea interruptes him delicately.

''Nothing. I... I don't remember anything, but I know I'm the cause of your injuries.''

''You know perfectly well that you were delirious with fever, right?''

''Yes, but—'' He tries to answer his professor, but he interrupted him again.

''You know you're not well, don't you? Neither physically nor mentally?''

''That's no excuse, Profes--''

''Answer this question,'' Phainon snorted at Anaxa's interruptions, but let him finish. ''if it were Aglaea who confused you with Caenis—''

''Why do you always have to use me as an example?'' the woman couldn't help adding, with a chuckle.

''Shut up,'' Anaxa snorts and continued with his suggestion, ''and she attacked you under the effects of obvious mental exhaustion and a horrible fever, would you hold it against her?'' Phainon opens his mouth, only to close it immediately, biting his lip hard. Anaxa gave him a gentle tap on the cheek to prevent him from drawing blood, urging him to answer.

Phainon shook his head, sighing calmly as Aglaea's tender caresses returned to his hair. ''Then don't expect us to be angry with you or, worse still, frightened by your presence. You will never make us feel that way, Phainon.''

Phainon nods weakly, sighing, as if he didn't want to argue anymore. He rested his head on Aglaea's shoulder while his blue eyes were fixed on Anaxa, a slight blush appearing on his cheeks, causing the alchemist to become curious.

''Lady Aglaea, Professor Anaxa, I wanted to apologise for—''

''Anaxágoras.''

The alchemist's correction left the room in an uncomfortable but amusing silence.

''Ugh, Anaxa, you're unbearable, I swear'' Aglaea snorts, rolling her eyes in disbelief.

''He knows perfectly well, and he still mispronounces my name.''

''Everyone mispronounces your name'' Aglaea teases, Anaxa rolling his eye in exasperation.

Fortunately, the argument elicited a half-smile from the hero, leaving both olders satisfied.

''What did you want to tell us, dear?''

Phainon laughes softly, shaking his head. ''Nothing. It's not important.''

Aglaea nods, touching his forehead, relieved that it no longer felt hot. She ran her hands through his hair, Phainon closing his eyes, enjoying the warm caresses of his mentor.

''How are you feeling after that horrible fever?''

''Much better,'' he replies softly. ''My head hardly hurts anymore.''

''Would you like something to make the pain go away completely?'' Phainon shook his head, eliciting a hoarse laugh from the woman. ''I thought so.''

''You're not a big fan of medicines?'' Anaxa raises his eyebrow, curious.

''It's just a minor annoyance. I don't need a pill for that,'' he replies, his eyes still closed. When he opened them, Anaxa sighs, distressed to see them looking so sad. ''So it wasn't my imagination... Hyacine has been here, hasn't she? She's the one who healed me.''

They both nod, Phainon twisting his mouth in a way that the only one who could see him didn't like at all. ''And I haven't even been able to thank her.''

''Do you really think she would want that? Would you want the same from us for bringing the Era Nova?''

''It's not the same'' Phainon replies to his professor.

''Oh, is not? Enlighten me, my precious student. What's the difference?''

''In that I can't even see her'' he whispers weakly, the room cooling at that confession.

Aglaea places her hand on the young man's neck, squeezing it gently and lovingly as if massaging it, in an attempt to relieve all the tension that had built up. ''Is it very hard for you to see her?'' she asks tactfully.

After a few seconds of silence, Phainon nods, responding with a faint < yes > after remembering that Aglaea couldn't see him.

"Her screams... her pleas... so many times I've had to live through it... so many times I've had to live through her death.

She was alone, scared to death, and I was the cause of that nightmare...'' Phainon clenches his jaw, bringing his only hand to his face, massaging the area around his eyes vigorously, probably to stop himself from crying at that very moment. ''And despite that fear, that... that confusion at my betrayal, she was still worried about me. Despite all these cycles, she has come to help me. To save me.

How can I be close to someone so pure? How do I deserve her friendship when, after so many cycles, I have been the cause of her terror? Of her hell?''

''Because you were forced to cause that hell in order to save us.

Because you are still her friend. Because she knows perfectly well that thanks to her pain and your sacrifice, she is now living the life she always wanted,'' Aglaea replies firmly. ''You saved her, Phainon."

Phainon's response was to lift one leg onto the bed, to rest his forehead on his knee, clearly wanting to hide his face. To hide his shame and vulnerability. Aglaea continued to look at him with pity, caressing him incessantly, while Anaxa let out a faint sigh. ''Hyacine is still here. In the Grove'' that information made Phainon tense up, and he did not move his face from its hiding place. "I'm not going to lie to you and say that she would love to see you again and talk to you.

And I truly believe you need it. But I need you to be honest with me, lad.

Is that what you want? Do you want to see her again? At least for now?"

They returned to that tense silence. Suffocating.

Phainon finally revealed his face, his eyes shining with tears that demanded to come out but were still held back by the hero's resistance, receiving the answer Anaxa expected, but that didn't mean it hurt any less.

''No.''

Aglaea pulled him into an embrace, Phainon letting himself be handled like a puppet, opening his eyes in disbelief, his body remaining relaxed however, when Anaxa stroked his shoulder.

He kept his eyes open, as he was sure that with the comfort and warmth he was receiving from those figures he saw as parental, if he closed them he would fall asleep again.

''What about the other members?'' Aglaea asks suddenly, uncertain.

Phainon took just as long to respond, and it was the same answer.

''I don't want to see anyone. Not yet. Their screams... the... the blood. Cas... Cifer... M—'' His mouth opens, clearly wanting to say another name. The only male name on that list, but Phainon ran out of breath, his tears finally coming, unable to even pronounce it.

Aglaea calms him down, assuring him that he didn't have to justify himself. That everyone would understand, and that Hyacine would keep the secret.

The young man shrank back when he received Anaxa's gestures of affection and comfort again, as if he still couldn't believe his professor was there with him. That he cared about him.

After patting him on the shoulder, the alchemist says he was going to prepare dinner, stroking (and ruffling) his hair before leaving.

''Lady Aglaea.''

''Yes, dear?''

The young man melted into the woman's embrace, just as he had done before the weight of the world's hopes rested on his shoulders. ''Thank you for everything.''

═════════════════════

''What do you think of this outfit?'' Hyacine asks.

It was the next day, and Anaxa decided to go to the market and, while he was there, meet with Hyacine to tell her about Phainon's decision.

He did not expect the woman to get up early to buy the clothes Anaxa had asked for the young hero.

''Light blue. It suits him.''

''I saw one that was orange and purple with stripes. I was about to buy it...''

''And give a blind woman eye strain, right?''

Hyacine laughes at the man's reply, sighing with a half-smile. ''How is he?''

''Oh, perfect. The damn guy couldn't have picked a better time to get out of bed, break a vase, and almost fall over just because he wanted to pee.''

''And where were you and Aglaea? How strang— oooohh'' the young healer hums, laughing at the murderous look Anaxa had given her.

''Nothing towards what you're thinking happened''

''Yeah... sure...''

''Ugh... Aglaea is going to have a rough time when she gets back to Okhema and has to deal with you and Tribios.''

Hyacine simply nods with a half-smile, but that cheerful atmosphere was quickly shattered by her next question. ''Did you ask him that?'' Anaxa nods, his gaze showing pain. Harsh. It was all Hyacine needed. ''Oh... I see.''

''He feels a lot of guilt about what he did to you. What he did to all of you.''

''But he had no choice! Besides, he wasn't going to be the only one to sacrifice himself for this New Era!''

''He sacrificed himself. You died by his blade.''

''Ugh... but... thanks to that...'' Hyacine couldn't continue, overcome by the rage and grief she felt, snorting at herself because she didn't want to start crying again in front of so many passers-by. ''Is he always going to feel this way about us?''

Unfortunately for Hyacine, Anaxa did not answer immediately, fearing the worst. ''I don't think so, but... well, I can't talk for him. He has suffered many cycles, Hyacine, and his mental state right now is beyond my comprehension. I can't even imagine what that boy must be feeling after everything he has had to live through and suffer.''

''If only we could remember those cycles too... so he wouldn't be so alone...''

''Oh yes, and we'd all be in the most infinite shit'' Anaxa snorts, amused, sighing when Hyacine shrank her body, still affected by Phainon's decision.

Anaxa's hug was very different from the awkward one hours earlier, Hyacine smiling weakly at that, unable to process the information.

Anaxa, of course, shushing her.

''What are you going to do?''

''Go back to Okhema. I've talked to Cas. Mydei... he's not well, Professor.''

'What do you mean?''

''That he suspects something. A lot. And I... I don't want to hurt him. I don't want to break his trust.'' Anaxa sighs, understanding his student. ''I have to go back as soon as possible so he can see that everything is normal. That I only came here for some notes, as I said the day before yesterday.''

Anaxa nods, apologising to her student for getting her into this situation, melting at the sweet, understanding smile she gave him. Truly, that girl deserved everything good in life.

''Are you leaving now, then?''

Hyacine nods. ''The sooner I get there, the better. So, on the way to Okhema, I can think about how to answer the questions they'll ask me.'' Hyacine's eyes sparkled mischievously, despite still maintaining that sad haze. ''I'm sure Tribios will ask me about both of you.''

''And what will you say?''

She opens her mouth, then closed it, unable to find an answer. Anaxa laughes. ''You can say that you've seen us. And that... well...''

''That when all this is sorted out, we'll see you together?'' Hyacine smiles, excited.

''Don't get ahead of yourself, dear student,'' Anaxa snorts, ruffling her hair, happy to have made her laugh. ''Just make sure Tribios doesn't bother Aglaea too much. The poor thing doesn't even know how to answer her anymore.''

Hyacine nods, without losing that mischievous and cheerful sparkle in her tired and sad eyes.

═════════════════════

When Anaxa returns, he didn't expect to find Aglaea in the kitchen, and couldn't help asking if everything was alright.

''You were taking a long time. I was thinking of making the meal myself.''

''Tsk, desperate woman'' Anaxa snorts, approaching her, lost in those blind eyes that explained why they gave her the title of Light of Okhema.

That, added to the calm smile she wore... how could he not fall for her?

But he wasn't going to let that vile woman know about his weakness, so he grabbed her cheek, pulling her, managing to enrage her as he always did, unable to help laughing when Aglaea pushed him away.

''You're unbearable.''

''You deserve it for being impatient,'' laughes Anaxa, lifting the bags Hyacine had given him as he took out the food he had bought at the market.

Hewent to the counter to prepare the food, Aglaea touching the bags he had left on the table. ''What have you got here? Clothes?''

"For Phainon. Hyacine chose them.'' Seeing Aglaea's worried look, Anaxa couldn't help but laugh. ''They're nice clothes, don't worry. You'd like them.''

''I hope so. Hyacine and Cifer were the only ones who supported Phainon in his horrible taste in clothes. I can see her buying a hideous garment just because she knows Phainon would like it.''

''More than supporting him, I think Cifera was just doing it to annoy you.''

''Ha, sure.''

''Besides, didn't you say that Phainon's mental health was also important? Maybe letting him dress however he want—''

''Over my dead body.''

''Ha!''

The afternoon arrived, both carers feeling relieved by the peaceful day they were enjoying after those days of pure agony.

Phainon tried to stay awake, but it was obvious that he was still exhausted, falling asleep when Anaxa decided to go over a subject with him that he always failed.

Only Aglaea's laughter at this situation prevented Anaxa from throwing his student out the window for such disrespect towards his teachings.

The afternoon was ending, the sun licking the horizon, about to set, when Anaxa felt a warm touch under his eyes.

''Now you're the one with horrible dark circles under your eyes'' Aglaea whispers, Anaxa lost in that soft smile.

The man chuckled, ''An horrible dark circle, you mean'' but his joke did not seem to annoy the blonde, even though she continued to smile softly, her gaze was full of concern. After a long sigh, Anaxa promised that after making dinner, she would go to sleep.

''We have leftovers. Phainon and I can manage with that if he wakes up.''

''Aren't you hungry?''

''Are you?''

Aglaea silenced the man, for it was true that, despite all the work they were doing, between caring for Phainon, keeping the secret, and cleaning the house, they really had little appetite.

''Then I'll go to sleep now. Tomorrow I'll make what I had planned for dinner as lunch.'' Aglaea nods, saying goodbye to him with a light caress on his back.

When the door closed behind him, Aglaea let out a long sigh, relieved that she no longer had to hide the blush that had spread across her cheeks.

But the next day, she knew something was wrong when Anaxa, who had been so calm and pleasant since that confession, he was tense.

Nervous.

Aglaea askshim what was wrong, worrying when he did not answer.

She gently took his wrist, asking again, with a vulnerability she did not think had come from her throat, if he was all right.

She heard Anaxa's uneasy sigh, her skin breaking out in goose bumps when he kissed her forehead.

"I'm fine.I'm sorry, I didn't mean to worry you like that.'' The man made sure the young hero was still asleep and gently led Aglaea out of the room. When they were finally out of earshot of Phainon, Anaxa muttered, overwhelmed ''We have problems, Aglaea."

''What shall we do?' Aglaea asks, worried.

Anaxa simply chuckled thoughtfully, biting his lip as he stared into space.

''Hold on to the hope that that imbecile has gone back to his homeland.''

Chapter End Notes
