See the end of the chapter for more notes

''I've been thinking about going back to the Academy. To teach classes. So that, you know, gives normality to our lifes if that paliópaido comes here'' Anaxa suggested at breakfast.

Aglaea blinked, curious. '' I wanted to return just right away after we reborn, but then that shooting star fell and...'' he sighed, pointing upstairs, where Phainon was resting.

The woman nodded, thinking it was a good idea.

Carrying Phainon's breakfast tray upstairs, Aglaea let out a melodious laugh. ''I'm going to miss you.''

''I'll be gone for a few hours, woman. I think you can live with that.''

''Live? No, I'm gonna to enjoy it.''

She managed to get a mocking laugh out of the man, who tried to trip her up when they finally reached the second floor.

When they opened the door, Phainon was awake, staring at the ceiling.

Anaxa simply placed the tray on the bed, looking at his... now partner? Could they be considered that again? ,worried.

That silence also caught the blind woman's attention, and they both sighed, alarmed.

''Phainon?'' whispered Aglaea, sitting down beside him.

He simply blinked slowly, his gaze still fixed on the ceiling. Faced with such impassivity, Anaxa grunted, massaging his forehead. ''Boy, I'm going to leave you alone with Aglaea because I have to go back to the Academy, so please eat your breakfast.''

Phainon blinked again with the same slowness, but his gaze finally shifted to face his teacher. ''The Academy...'' he whispered, as if in a trance.

Aglaea looked back at the alchemist with concern, but he simply laughed softly, sitting down at the sick boy's knees and patting his leg. ''If you feel like going back, you know what you have to do.'' He tapped the tray with the food gently. ''Eat.''

Phainon murmured, closing his eyes, but his arm rose to pick up a piece of toast and bring it to his mouth. ''Not like that, you animal! Get up and eat like a normal person!'' Anaxa scolded him, his shout startling the two who accompanied him.

Aglaea, guessing what had happened, helped the young man sit up, laughing amusedly. ''What did you want, to choke yourself, silly?''

''Mmm...''

The woman sighed with relief when she heard him eating, gently silencing Anaxa when she knew full well that the alchemist was going to ask something that surely had no answer.

''Well... since I'm no longer needed here, I'm going to try to instil a little knowledge in a pack of hormonal brats.'' Aglaea laughed again, and Anaxa smiled with relief when Phainon's serious face finally disappeared. ''You know what? Sometimes I miss your class. Castorice, Hyacine and you were decent students. At least in that respect.''

''Because you didn't read what Cas wrote.'' Phainon murmured, amused. Anaxa's relief gave way to concern when Aglaea nodded to the young man, both of them complicit in a mystery that Anaxa was unaware of.

''I'm glad you have the humour to ruin the image I had of my dear student...''

Aglaea wanted to accompany him to the entrance, but before they reached the stairs, he stopped her. ''I wouldn't want to find you with a bump on your head. You're already bruised enough'' he murmured, tucking a few blonde strands behind her ear.

''You know I know this house better now than I did years ago, don't you?'' she murmured, offended. Anaxa laughed, resting his forehead against the woman's.

''I'll be back soon'' he whispered, his voice so vulnerable and so full of feeling that she couldn't believe he was capable of speaking in that tone.

Aglaea nodded, giving her a goodbye kiss and asking him to be careful.

When she entered, Phainon sighed loudly to let her know he hadn't fallen asleep.

''We're alone'' she said.

''Yep.''

''Without the grumpy one.'' Aglaea managed to elicit a small laugh from him, but she knew he was up to something.

He was hiding something.

She reached out to squeeze his left shoulder affectionately, when she encountered his arm. ''Does your stump hurt?'' she asked, concerned.

''No...'' he whispered, Aglaea hearing the blankets move, then feeling Phainon's entire arm resting against her. ''It's just that... I don't think it's fair...''

''What you don't find fair?''

''That you're still blind. That I...'' Phainon sighed with anguish, Aglaea nodding, understanding the feeling. ''We made many sacrifices for these consequences to haunt us. What about the others? What kind of consequences will they have?''

''I can assure you that except for ours and Tribios who still kept her new form, no one is as badly affected as you think.''

''Then Cas—''

''Her curse is gone.'' the woman informed him, hearing the relieved smile form on Phainon's face. ''And... and Mydei then? H... he's no longer immortal?''

''Unfortunately, we cannot know that. And it is best not to put it to the test.''

''No!'' Phainon replied immediately, making the woman laugh.

''That means your duels will have to be toned down.''

Aglaea lost her smile when she no longer felt Phainon as relaxed as before, asking him affectionately what was wrong.

''Do you think he'll want?''

''He'll want what?''

''Duel with me again? Go back... to doing all the things we used to do.''

''And why shouldn't he will?''

''Because now I'm useless.''

''Phainon! Don't say that about yourself!'' the woman growls.

''It's the truth...''

''No!'' she said firmly. ''I won't allow anyone to call you useless, not even yourself!''

''Bu–but I won't be able to duel him again. If Okhema is in danger again, I won't be able to fight alongside him! Why would he want my company then?''

''Is that all you two ever did? Fight and train?'' She raised her eyebrow, incredulous.

She sensed Phainon shaking his head emphatically. ''Someone like him, so proud, with war and battle in his blood, wouldn't want...'' Phainon closed his eyes, clenching his jaw as he dug his nails into his stump in anger. ''Why would he want to waste his time on someone like me?''

Aglaea couldn't help but shudder at the bitterness and contempt that Phainon exuded through his words.

She remembered the first time Phainon suffered that hallucination. How he begged to be killed, saying he didn't deserve to live. And what the hell, long before discovering the truth, every time he lost a battle or failed to complete a mission.

That face full of bitterness and helplessness. Of... disgust. Aglaea always thought it was anger and disgust towards the Black Tide. Towards the injustice suffered by the heirs and warriors who had to witness the atrocities Lygus left behind.

But she never thought that bitterness was... because Phainon despised himself in that way.

Like the man she had raised since he was a child, Aglaea also clenched her jaw, in a manner so similar to Phainon that no one would doubt they were mother and son, the woman confronting him with a fierceness that could intimidate even an Aeon.

''Waste his time? On someone like you? How dare you even think that of yourself, Phainon!''

''But Agla–''

''No!'' she declared again, Phainon lowering his gaze like a child who had just been scolded. ''In someone like you, you say?'' she repeated, completely indignant. ''Someone who has saved us all? Who has been repeating torture for an insane number of cycles in order to break a system that treated us like toys? Someone who, at that moment, was not human, and yet managed to wound an Aeon!? A damned God far superior and more powerful than our Titans!?''

She heard Phainon let out a trembling whimper, Aglaea abruptly pulling away the hand that was hurting the stump. ''Answer me.''

''I am no longer that hero. I can no longer—''

''Do you really think we want you to keep sacrificing yourself for us!? Do you think that because you can no longer fight as before, everything you have done previously is worthless!? Phainon, neither me I raised you nor Anaxa teach you so badly to become that ignorant!''

''What will become of me if I am no longer a hero?!'' cried the young man, letting out all the bitterness and anguish he had kept inside for so long. ''What use am I if I can never save anyone again?!''

Phainon forced himself to calm down when his cry reassured an indignant Aglaea, who cradled him, as she always did when he had a childish tantrum, wanting to fight against that touch but unable to resist that homely warmth.

''What use are you? Phainon, you don't have to be of any use.

We just want you to live. To be happy. Can you really only be happy by fighting? By saving people? I think that with all those cycles you've lived through, you've more than fulfilled that mission, don't you think?''

Phainon bit his lip, unable to answer that question.

''How about travelling all over Amphoreus? Collecting antiques, or studying them. Or going back to the Academy and dedicating yourself to a particular field? Or simply living peacefully in Okhema, going to the market every day, telling the children your stories and listening to the musicians sing under the fountain. Wouldn't you like that, really?''

Phainon let out a nervous sigh, his body weakening, his forehead falling onto the woman's shoulder.

''You can...'' Aglaea took a deep breath, as if she didn't want to say it. ''You can even go with Stelle. Travel to other galaxies. Meet other cultur–''

''No,'' he cut her off immediately, seriously. ''I'm not going to leave Amphoreus. I could never do that.''

Aglaea laughed, patting him affectionately on the back, finally burying her hand in that mop of white hair, desperate for a hot bath and some shampoo. ''Then if you love Amphoreus, love him in every way, and not just through blood and smoke.''

''Can I even allow myself that?''

''How can you even think that, when you are the one who deserves it most?''

''I... I find it difficult. There have been many occasions when I...'' Phainon couldn't continue, Aglaea nodding, as she didn't need him to finish that sentence.

''We will always be by your side, ready to get that idea out of your head.''

After that sentence, there was a quiet silence.

She could feel Phainon's breath on her skin and his back rising and falling calmly.

For a moment, she thought he had fallen asleep, holding his body carefully as she moved to rest his back against the wall, when he spoke.

''I miss him,'' he confessed, Aglaea sighing sadly, her hands returning to that dirty mop of hair. ''I miss them all so much... but him... ah...''

Phainon did not continue, Aglaea unable to help but laugh at his shyness. ''I doubt the others will be offended that the one you miss the most is the prince, silly.''

She felt Phainon nod against her shoulder, sighing when she didn't get an answer again. ''You miss him, but...?'' She decided to give him a hand, as any progress in showing his feelings was necessary.

''How can't he hate me? Can't they they hate me!?''

''Hate you after you gave them the life they always wanted?''

''He trusted me. He told me about his weakness, and because of that...'' Aglaea felt the blankets they were sitting on crumple, exhaling a sad sigh as she held the young man's wrist again with affection and calm.

''You think about how Mydei must feel, even though, as you rightly said, he has war in his blood, so I very much doubt he is as affected by what you did to him as you expect. But what about you?''

He felt Phainon pull away from her touch, and he could almost imagine that lost puppy look he always wore, which Aglaea always found so adorable to see.

''The Flame Reaver... can't you think of that person, that hero who had to be disguised as a villain, who was forced to kill the person he loved in order to fulfil his goal? How his hands must have trembled at that? How much he would have wanted to hold that body and mourn it, and have to feign indifference while his other half wanted to kill him for what he had done? While he had to listen to the one who would take his place in the next cycle swear revenge on him, knowing that such revenge would never be fulfilled?'''

She heard Phainon's stifled sob, Aglaea not hesitating to cradle his jaw again. ''Damn it, Phainon, why are you incapable of appreciating what you've done for us? To stop seeing you as a monster and start seeing you for what you are? Our bloody saviour? Our light?''

But Phainon shook his head vehemently. ''That's not even my name, and you know it. My real name is Khaslana. The pure embodiment of chaos.''

But Aglaea replied with a proud laugh, ''Do you remember the day I found you?''

Phainon nodded weakly. How could he forget?

So many cycles... so many different deaths, so many endings, some worse than others... but the beginning was always the same.

A badly injured and terrified child on the border of Okhema, who could not even see his own hands.

Most of the soldiers even fled in terror, thinking he was a ghost, as he kept murmuring names.

The names of his neighbours. Of his friends. Of his family...

Finally, that boy collapsed before even reaching the entrance to that imposing city, thinking that the mud and rain would be his grave.

When he felt the warmest touch that could have existed.

''Is he dead?''

''Don't be rude, Ciphera. He's just injured.''

''Very injured'' emphasised the young voice.

The boy opened his eyes, confused, when he saw a face brighter than the sun and a smile that healed the heart.

''Can you get up?'' The boy's response was to let his face fall back onto the muddy ground, hoping that the sweet woman would leave him alone.

He was a monster, after all. Someone who couldn't tell the difference between those beasts and his terrified neighbours, causing those poor souls to fall under his blade.

But no...

The next thing he felt was the woman lifting him up and letting him rest against her body, managing to see how that beautiful white and gold suit was stained with mud and golden blood. And that stranger didn't seem to care in the slightest.

''We're going home, okay?'' whispered that tender voice, the boy unable to do anything but nod, clinging to that warm body as if it were his lifeline. ''What's your name?''

''I couldn't tell you my real name. Khaslana died when Aedes Elysae disappeared in the flames.''

''Khaslana may have died, but not Phainon. Never Phainon.'' The young man clenched his jaw at this, nodding at the woman's words. ''That's why, to me, you'll always be that man. That name. Until the end of my days. You are not chaos, Phainon. You never have been. Not to me, nor to them.''

She sighed with relief when she felt Phainon finally nod, his vulnerable voice returning.

''So... do you think he'll forgive me? That he'll be able to continue loving me despite what I did? Despite having taken advantage of his trust to attack his weakness?' Phainon bit his lip, closing his eyes tightly. ''Even though... I'll never be that warrior he admired so much again?''

Aglaea did not respond immediately. She simply took the chin of the boy she had raised firmly in her hand, looking at him intently, with a calm smile. ''Do you really believe that, Phainon?''

''I want... I need to believe it'' confessed the young man.

''Why?'' she asked, desperate and incredulous.

''Because then everything would be easier...''

Aglaea had no answer for that. It would be repeating incessantly what Phainon already knew but still did not want to accept.

She could only hug him, hoping that the feeling of guilt would soon leave the Saviour of Amphoreus.

''You must have a name, don't you think?'' The boy shrugged indifferently. ''How about Phainon? I think it suits you.''

''Really?'' Cipher snorted amusedly, Aglaea shushing her.

And the boy nodded weakly, knowing that he wanted to hold on to that warm feeling in his chest when he heard that name forever.

________________________________________________________________________

When Anaxa returned that night, his face showing genuine relief, they were both able to breathe easy.

''It's still too early to claim victory, but I haven't heard anything from the Prince of Castrum Kremnos, not even at the border.''

Aglaea nodded, but Anaxa didn't miss the frown on the woman's face. He decided not to bring up the subject, as they both looked genuinely exhausted.

After four days of this new normal, it was Phainon who suggested to Aglaea that she accompany Anaxa to the Academy.

''You've been locked up here with me for almost a month. You're no longer injured, Lady Aglaea.''

Aglaea tried to argue with him, losing completely when the damned Anaxa sided with the hero, the woman angrily showing her defeat.

She decided to accompany him to the Academy, as they had done centuries ago, in that previous cycle, and who knows if even others before that.

Her smile never left her face despite Anaxa's irritation at questions that, according to him, were stupid... but which the man nevertheless answered and explained over and over again.

He really had a passion for teaching...

After class, they took a walk through the Grove, Aglaea feeling that they were once again those two young heirs who were getting to know each other. Who were discovering their identity.

Before Cifer's arrival. Before Phainon's. Before she sacrificed her humanity and Anaxa sacrificed his sanity.

She smiled softly when she felt Anaxa's warm hand beside her, but his tone was as sarcastic as ever. ''What's bothering you, silly?''

''You really won't change'' she quipped amusedly, remembering what Anaxa was like before their breakup.

Just as sarcastic, just as much of a jerk, and just as impatient... but back then she had vision, and the eyes were the mirror of the soul. He was incapable of deceiving her...

But Anaxa also knew Aglaea like the back of his hand, forcing her to sit down, the woman feeling Anaxa's presence in front of her, waiting patiently.

''It's about a conversation Phainon and I had on the first day you returned to the Academy...'' she confessed, not quite sure about saying that. ''And... I don't know what to think anymore, Anaxa.''

''What do you mean?''

''Whether we should hide it more. They have a right to know, Anaxa...''

''Don't you remember how Phainon reacted when he saw Hyacine?''

Aglaea did not respond immediately, sighing with relief when the alchemist sat down beside her, affectionately squeezing her shoulder. ''It's true that the boy has improved, but... he's still not well. Hell, he still can't even take a bath, Aglaea! Despite his damn insistence.''

Aglaea laughed, nodding, because for the past two days Phainon had been very insistent about taking a bath, and she and Anaxa had had some serious arguments.

''He could... he could relapse at any moment, Aglaea. What if his relapse is caused by his reunion with Mydei and he ends up... ends up much worse than those two hallucinations? That fever?'' Aglaea lost her smile, biting her lip, hurt by that possible truth. ''You know very well that I take his vital signs every night. When Phainon asked me if it was necessary, you were the one who told him to be quiet, assuring him that any check-up, no matter how minor, was necessary. But I don't do it just for the sake of doing the minimum, Aglaea.''

''What's wrong with him?'' she asked, worried.

''His heart. I don't like how it sounds, and there's no change.'' Faced with Aglaea's confusion and insistence on knowing what he meant, Anaxa sighed. ''I don't know exactly what's wrong with him either. It's not that it sounds weak, nor is his heartbeat arrhythmic, but... I don't know, it just doesn't sound like it should.''

Aglaea took in this new information in silence, enjoying the support the man was showing her, resting her cheek on his shoulder. ''So what he needs least...''

''...is surprises, yes...''

They both sighed wearily at the same time, Aglaea massaging her face, uttering an irritated murmur, eliciting a small laugh from Anaxa. ''My poor Aglaea, who doesn't know what to do...''

''Shut up.''

''By the way, if you told the prince, where would he go?''

Aglaea shrugged, making an amused face. ''We could finally sleep together in your room.''

''In my sister's one? No, thank you.''

''We'll move Phainon then.''

''And allow our son to commit filthy deeds on my roof? I don't like your libertarian upbringing, dear Aglaea.''

Anaxa managed to elicit another laugh from the blonde, relieved and happy, ending in a hug.

''They'll find out soon enough. Just give it time. Give us time.'' Anaxa raised his eyebrows, looking up at the sky. ''We must take advantage of the fact that he's giving it to us.''

That morning was like any other. In fact, they even encouraged Phainon to go downstairs for breakfast in the kitchen, having to carry him back up immediately when his knees couldn't even hold him up while sitting in the chair.

After making sure he was all right and saying goodbye, as they had been doing for several days, with a kiss on the cheek to Aglaea, Anaxa left his hous—no, his home.

After closing the door, he turned around, heading for the Academy, and froze when he saw the person in front of him.

He was looking around the neighbourhood, his eyes wide with surprise... and perhaps relief, when he caught sight of Anaxa.

''Prince Mydeimos'' said Anaxa, trying to sound completely calm and indifferent.

''Professor Anaxagoras'' replied the young man calmly.

''What are you doing here? Stalking like a lion? Well,'' he arched his eyebrow, trying to sound amused and annoy the prince ''more like lionesses, since they are the ones who hunt.''

But Mydei maintained the same pose and expression, nodding indifferently.

''I just wanted to know how Lady Aglaea and you were doing.''

''I admire your concern for Aglaea, Highness, but concern for me? We've never even met.''

''But you are someone important in the lives of Hyacine and Castorice. And an important member of the Heirs.'' Mydei raised his eyebrow, suspicion showing behind those vibrant golden eyes. ''Can't I show concern for you?''

''Ugh, really, these young people are going to take years off my life. And now is not a good time to say that, because we're not going to last as many years as our previous cycles'' Anaxa snorted, massaging his forehead.

Once again, Mydei showed no irritation at Anaxa's mockery of their conversation.

He simply pursed his lips, uttering a bored murmur.

And Anaxa responded with a similar sigh. ''What are you doing here, Mydeimos?''

''I already told you. Or do you think I came here for something else?''

''I don't know. Maybe you want to enrol in the Academy. A citizen of Castrum Kremnos and the prince, no more less. It would give a good reputation. To both places, or so I think...''

Mydei did not respond. He maintained that look that was driving Anaxa crazy. A cold look, even though his eyes looked like two suns.

''Is something wrong?'' Anaxa snorted, fed up with that silent stare.

''No, nothing.''

''You see, lad, after this well-deserved break I've had with this Era Nova, returning to the academy has been a huge let-down for me. I don't feel like putting up with... nonsense. Do you understand what I mean?''

''My apologies if I'm bothering you. That wasn't my intention.'' he replied, and although he sounded polite and sincere, there was still a coldness in the prince's tone.

Mydei turned his head, staring at the house Anaxa had come out of. ''Lady Aglaea is in there, I suppose?''

''You're right.''

''Do you think I could go in to see her?''

''No. She's resting. Let her sleep.'' Anaxa replied, trying not to sound too hostile and desperate.

''Aham...''

Anaxa blinked at the prince's insolence. ''It's not because of that, you big ass donkey!''

If the prince of Castrum Kremnos was offended by that insult, he certainly did not show it, for his face remained as impassive as ever.

''I have not assimilated anything, professor Anaxagoras.''

Anaxa sighed again, tired, looking at his watch, assuring himself that he was late.

Mydei nodded, fortunately also taking another route away from his neighbourhood. ''Are you going home?''

''I would like to see Lady Aglaea. I haven't been able to see her since the birth of the Era Nova.''

''I didn't know you got along so well.'' replied Anaxa, his jaw tense.

''I could say the same.'' Mydei replied simply, finally showing some emotion, a dangerous and hostile emotion in his gaze. ''Or what's the matter, professor? Can't I be in the Grove?''

''When did I say that?'' Anaxa snorted, trying to remain calm.

''Then it's settled.'' replied Mydei, giving a final snort, like a war horse refusing to be ridden.

The young prince finally turned his back on him, disappearing around the next corner, Anaxa still wondering how his knees remained steady.

He ran his hand over his face, hissing irritably. ''We're really screwed.''

Chapter End Notes

⪩ Yeah Anaxa, you're so screwed x) ⪨

Chapter Summary

''HE LEFT!'' Anaxa shouted before Aglaea could even open her mouth.

The woman blinked, incredulous. ''HE LEFT, AGLAEA. THAT VLÁKAS IS GONE!''

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

''Anaxa?'' asked Aglaea when she heard the door open again. She couldn't see the alchemist's expression, but she could sense the tense atmosphere he brought in from the street. ''What happened?''

Anaxa sighed, rubbing his forehead. ''The immortal boy is here'' he muttered wearily.

Aglaea didn't react as badly as Anaxa had expected, surprising him. ''Are you surprised he's here?''

''No, but I'd appreciate it if he wasn't standing in front of my house like a guard dog, asking me suspicious questions.''

''It's normal for him to be suspicious, Anaxa...''

''Whose side are you supposed to be on, dear?'' Anaxa laughed, muttering wearily again, asking about Phainon.

''Upstairs. Sleeping, I suppose.''

''You suppose?'' He raised his eyebrow, amused, while she sighed.

''He's back to being weird. Elusive. He said he was sleepy and wanted to be left alone.''

''Argh, damn kid'' Anaxa snorted, climbing the stairs.

But Aglaea stopped him, snapping at him to leave the younger alone. ''We can't have to keep on top of him all the time. He deserves some privacy.'' The woman grimaced, shaking her head weakly. ''It's bad enough that he can't leave the house and that we're his only company.''

''Is that such a bad thing?'' Anaxa raised his eyebrow, amused, earning a chuckling snort from the blonde.

While Anaxa made himself a cup of tea before returning to the Academy, Aglaea stood beside him, thinking about what to do about Mydei.

Her thoughts were interrupted when Anaxa tapped her forehead with his finger, telling her not to worry too much about it.

Before leaving, he assured her that he wanted to see how the boy was doing, climbing the stairs again. Aglaea picked up Anaxa's cup to take it to the sink when the man's scream startled her, causing her to drop it and fall to the floor.

She didn't even have to ask what had happened, as the alchemist's hurried footsteps echoed throughout the house.

''HE LEFT!'' Anaxa shouted before Aglaea could even open her mouth.

The woman blinked, incredulous. ''HE LEFT, AGLAEA. THAT VLÁKAS IS GONE!''

They rushed out of the house to look for him, Aglaea cursing the little power her threads had in the Grove. If only they were in Okhema...

If this had happened a couple of days ago, Aglaea knew full well that she would have blamed Anaxa. Phainon would be better guarded in Okhema...

But... trapped...

But now there was no point in trying to find someone to blame when there was no one to blame.

She understood Anaxa's fear of not wanting Phainon, in such a delicate state, to leave for Okhema, so far away.

Understood the alchemist's need, despite his attempts to hide it, to treat and care for the young hero.

But she also understood Phainon... It had been nearly a month since they found him, and the only places he had been allowed to leave his room were the bathroom and the kitchen.

The question was... why had he done it in secret? Had Anaxa and Aglaea behaved in some way that made the boy distrust them? That made him want to escape from that house?

''What if he overheard our conversation about the prince and went to see him?'' was Anaxa's desperate question, seeking an answer to his escape.

Aglaea pursed her lips, unsure. ''You were there when we asked him if he could see the other members again. He couldn't even mention Mydeimos' name. Why now, when I've already told you that he was acting strange this morning, and not in an optimistic way, would things be any different?''

Anaxa pursed his lips, surrendering to the blonde's logic. ''And where the hell could he be...''

''Maybe we're racking our brains when his escape is for the simplest and most stupid reason. Maybe he was just bored and went for a walk.''

''If that's the case, I swear I'll rip his head off'' snorted the alchemist, heading for the academy, as it was the best place to find information.

They went to all the classrooms Phainon had attended in the past, even asking classmates who had repeated the course so many times that they had coincided with the young hero, but found nothing.

Aglaea followed Anaxa, feeling completely lost in that world, when she bumped hard into the back of her beloved, who caught her when, due to the blow and the surprise of the impact, she almost fell to the ground.

After offering a quick apology, Aglaea was pulled away by Anaxa, as if they wanted to hide. ''Did you find him?''

''The prince is here,'' Anaxa snorted ''in the bloody library.''

''Waiting for Phainon?''

Anaxa took a while to answer, sounding hesitant. ''It doesn't seem like it. He's just browsing through books.''

''Should we risk asking him if he's seen him?''

''And have my golden blood bathe the corridors of the Academy? No, dear, thank you.'' Anaxa snorted, again pulling, this time gently, on the blonde to move her away from the library.

''Then what do we do?''

The couple spent most of the day searching for Phainon and avoiding Mydei, a task that fell entirely to Anaxa, as Aglaea could only form threads far away from Okhema, in places she considered home.

If it weren't for the stress of not finding Phainon, Anaxa would feel an inexplicable happiness knowing how well Aglaea was guiding herself, both now and in the past, in his home.

Anaxa was about to suggest going to the outskirts of the Grove, to that place where very important information about the Titans was found, when this time it was Aglaea who stopped him abruptly, her eyes shining with relief.

''Let's go home. Quickly!''

The relief Anaxa felt when he saw that stupid hero sitting on the doorstep of his house, showing no signs of having undergone any kind of transformation, was what prevented him from immediately going over to him and, as he had promised, tearing his head off.

But even so, his steps towards Phainon sounded loud. Angry. Anaxa stepped ahead of Aglaea, his anger towards Phainon for the anguish he had caused them in those hours being greater than not leaving the poor blonde behind.

But when he stood in front of Phainon, an even more intense rage arose within the alchemist when Phainon looked up, annoyed. Irritated.

''Where were you? I've been here waiting for you to open the door for quite some time.''

''Ha, and you have the nerve to get angry with us!? Why didn't you climb in through the window, the same way you escaped?''

Anaxa couldn't help but shout, being stopped by Aglaea, who suggested to go inside and not attract the attention of prying ears.

Anaxa nodded, his jaw tense, impatiently opening the door and waiting for Phainon to go ahead of him.

He snorted at the hero's passivity, his body reacting differently when he led Aglaea into the house.

''Well?'' Anaxa snorted, now in the privacy of his home.

The alchemist dug his nails into his palm as Phainon continued to appear bored, calmly filling a glass with water. ''PHAINON!''

''What?'' That shout seemed to irritate him, angering Anaxa even more.

''WHAT DO YOU MEAN WHAT!? WE DEMAND AN EXPLANATION FOR THE FOOLISHNESS YOU JUST COMMITTED!''

''Am I your prisoner?'' Phainon snorted coldly, Aglaea's hand interposing itself between Anaxa and Phainon, pulling her beloved behind her, now facing the irritated youngling herself.

''You know very well that's not true, Phainon. Honestly, it's insulting that you would even suggest that.''

''But I have to explain every step I take to you. There's a name for that!'' snorted the white-haired, Aglaea taking a deep breath, not losing her cool.

''Because of your situation. Your condition—''

''MY CONDITION IS PERFECT. I'VE BEEN HEALTHY FOR DAYS!''

''Oh yes, your change in attitude proves it completely.'' Anaxa said ironically, snorting with a dry laugh.

''You better close your mouth'' Phainon hissed, clearly threatening.

Although he would never dare to show it, Anaxa blinked, incredulous at the hatred with which Phainon spoke to him. As much as he wanted to, his threat had had the desired effect, as the alchemist's vocal cords stopped working.

But Aglaea sighed patiently and firmly, moving in front of Anaxa, fierce as a lioness.

''Are you going to tell us what's wrong with you or what happened to you?'' Phainon, like a small child, turned his face away. ''If you were really so irritated to be in here, you should have told us! We would have had no problem getting you out!''

''You would have done that!? Really?'' Phainon snorted, not confronting the woman he loves as a mother.

''Yes!'' Aglaea replied firmly, Anaxa bowing his head, overwhelmed by the situation. ''Damn it, Phainon, do you really think we would keep you here as a prisoner? That your mental health doesn't concern us as much as your physical health?

We didn't know you were ready to go outside yet, but it's also your responsibility to communicate with us.

You know I love you with all my heart, and Anaxa is taking care of you as best he can, but if there's no communication between the three of us, we can't know how to help you one hundred per cent!''

Aglaea's words finally calmed the irritated hero, who nodded weakly.

''Don't you remember that yesterday you tried to have breakfast in the kitchen and almost fell down the stairs when you tried to climb them on your own? Again!?'' Phainon grimaced at that, Aglaea raising her hands. ''I'm not saying this to remind you, as you're probably thinking, stupidly—''

''Very stupidly.'' added Anaxa, Phainon snorting at his intervention, but at least he wasn't looking at his teacher with such hatred.

''—that you're useless.'' said Aglaea, tense at Anaxa's interruption. ''But of course, understand that after that, the last thing we could have imagined was that you would want to leave the house, and that you would have the strength to do so!''

Phainon grimaced again, his eyebrows arching in a way that made him look vulnerable. Guilty.

''I... I used the power of the coreflames to keep myself stable. Conscious...''

''WHAT!?'' Anaxa shouted, moving towards him despite Aglaea's attempts to stop him. ''BUT BOY, HOW THE FUCK YOU EVEN THINK OF DOING THAT!? ARE YOU TRULY THAT DENSE!?''

''YES, PROFESSOR, I AM THAT DENSE. I AM THE STUPIDEST THING YOU HAVE EVER HAD THE MISFORTUNE TO MEET! I'M SORRY I'M NOT AS COLD AND PROFESSIONAL AS YOU TO BE ABLE TO HANDLE THIS SITUATION! I'M SORRY FOR BEING SUCH A HUGE, USELESS BURDEN TO YOU!!'' Phainon shouted angrily, walking away, terrified of Anaxa, when he felt his eyes turn golden, quickly climbing the stairs to surely go to his room.

Which he now saw more as a cell than a refuge.

Anaxa sighed wearily, massaging his face with his hand, murmuring calmly when he felt Aglaea's hand on his shoulder. ''You may be the most intelligent man in Amphoreus, but you're terrible at comforting people.''

''You're one to talk'' the man replied with a half-smile.

They fell silent, Anaxa resting his head on his beloved's shoulder, murmuring sadly when Aglaea moved, her body heat no longer felt by Anaxa.

''It's clear that he and you still haven't settled your differences.''

''What do you mean?''

''That he still doesn't believe you care about him, Anaxa. It's obvious.'' Anaxa opened his eyes wide in disbelief, but Aglaea cut her off, shrugging her shoulders. ''What do you want me to say? Your concern is sincere, but it's also sharp—''

''He used those coreflames to wander around the Grove, while the prince, the man he must avoid at all costs, is swarming around there! Forgive me if I want to show my anger towards that brainless fool.''

''Phainon doesn't know Mydei is here.''

''Agh, I know, but—''

''Then why blame him for it? Besides, Anaxa... wouldn't you also go crazy if your only company were us, and you could barely leave your room?''

''If he doesn't go out, it's because of his physical condition, and hey, what's wrong with our company?''

But Aglaea calmly denied it. ''Well, if he faints, or his legs can't take it anymore, we'll be there to help him again. But it's of little use that his physical condition is healing if now we are the ones deteriorating his mental health.''

Anaxa snorted through his nose, clicking his tongue. ''I hate it when you're right.''

''Which is always.'' the woman smiled, amused.

''Ha, you wish.''

Anaxa relaxed when he felt Aglaea's touch again. She took his hand, squeezing it gently. ''Go there. Show him how much you care about him and how much you love him.'' Anaxa blushed at those words, but did not deny them. ''I'll go find Mydei.''

As if a bucket of cold water had been poured over him, Anaxa turned to the blind woman. ''Are you crazy? Do you know what a tremendous miracle it is that those two haven't found each other? And now you want to talk to him yourself? Raise more suspicion?''

''I'm going to tell him that Phainon is here, with us. Alive.''

''AGLAEA, FOR THE SAKE OF THE TITANS—''

''He deserves to know, Anaxa. They deserve to know.''

''Yes, and after tearing your limbs off, he'll come after me to tear my head off and finally ruin Phainon's fragile mental health completely!''

Aglaea shook her head, clicking her tongue. ''I know what I'm doing. And I trust him.''

After a moment's hesitation, Anaxa sighed and nodded. ''And I trust you.'' He rested his forehead against the woman's, the tip of his nose caressing the other's. ''But please be careful.''

''I couldn't bear to lose you again.'' the alchemist dared not say.

When Aglaea left the house to go in search of the prince, Anaxa took a few minutes to go up to the room to confront that irritating beast.

He made himself some chamomile tea, which was probably past its sell-by date as it belonged to his sister, wasting it when he didn't even drink it.

After gathering the courage and, above all, patience, he took a deep breath, climbed the stairs and entered Phainon's room...

...where he was lying down, his back to the door.

But from his breathing, Anaxa could tell that he was awake, forcing himself to remain calm, sitting down slowly on the edge of the bed.

Anaxa remained silent, not knowing how to begin, because everything he could think of, he could imagine Aglaea scolding him for. And if he could imagine that... then unfortunately, he was not on the right track.

Fortunately, Phainon broke the agonising silence with an apology.

Any anger or furious concern Anaxa felt at the discovery of not only Phainon's sudden and unannounced departure, but also his use of the coreflames, was completely calmed by how broken and helpless his student sounded.

''I'm sorry too if... well, all this time I've given you the impression that I wasn't worthy of your trust. Of you not being able to express your concerns to me.''

But Phainon denied it, even without confronting his teacher. ''You've done perfectly, Professor. Both you and Lady Aglaea.''

''Then why, ayópi?''

Phainon shrugged, curling up further in the bed, clutching the blanket that covered nothing of his body. ''I don't know...'' he confessed, with a vulnerability that was heartbreaking.

Anaxa sighed again, moving closer to him, stroking his shoulder, urging him to get up and talk.

For Phainon to speak openly and concisely.

The youngling did not start immediately, and although he obeyed his teacher, he kept his gaze downcast. Evasive.

But Anaxa, unfortunately commonly unknown for his great patience, waited.

If he had ever shown impatience, it was only a sign of his humanity, of his concern for his loved ones, which he had to hide so as not to disrupt his plans. His studies.

But now there was nothing more to fear, all thanks to the man in front of him. It was the least Phainon deserved. That he give him time.

''I... got overwhelmed. I don't know. Being locked up for so long... I could hear the voices of his students, the children playing, the old women running errands... I needed to experience that again. To feel human again.''

''Phainon, you are human.'' Anaxa emphasised seriously, Phainon responding with a dry laugh.

But fortunately, he didn't reply, even though that laugh showed that he didn't quite agree with the professor. ''So, you left through the window. Because you think we would say no.''

Phainon nodded weakly, Anaxa murmuring ''I'm sorry that both Aglaea and I gave you that impression. It was not our intention at all.''

''I'm sorry—''

''Don't apologise when you were right. If you had asked our permission, we would surely have objected.'' Phainon did not respond, sighing wearily and sinking his back further into the bed. ''I would use the excuse that it's for your own good, that you're not fully recovered yet, but... I understand that it's unfair to you. And that you've found this recovery... suffocating.''

''It's not your fault, Professor. It's just that...'' Phainon bit his lip hard, abruptly turning his face away from Anaxa, who raised an eyebrow, curious and annoyed. ''Finish, lad.''

''You're right! I'm not recovered, and I don't know if I ever will be!'' he snorted angrily, earning himself a coughing fit after finishing. Anaxa brought a bowl in case Phainon needed it, as his coughs didn't sound good at all.

When he returned to his side, Phainon simply cleared his throat. Anaxa asked if he needed anything, and he said no, but he had to drink the glass of water Anaxa offered him (or rather, forced him to drink)

After a necessary silence, Anaxa shared what little she could guess about Phainon's condition from his basic checks. ''You don't carry all your coreflames, do you? You managed to get rid of almost all of it when you faced Irontomb.''

Phainon gave a weak, soft laugh, not surprised that his teacher knew that huge secret. ''But you still have some left.''

Phainon nodded, shivering as Anaxa picked up the blanket he had been avoiding so much and placed it over him. ''You know you don't have to cover me, right? I'm not as abrasive as I used to be, but I'm still—''

''Covering someone doesn't just serve to eliminate the cold. Now tell me,'' Anaxa began before Phainon could interrupt with any more nonsense ''what do you mean when you say you don't think you'll ever recover?'' Phainon bit his lip, unsure of how to begin. ''Is it a tiredness that never seems to go away? Chest pains at the slightest exertion? Recurring fatigue?''

Here Phainon was surprised by the alchemist's insight, nodding slowly and asking how he had guessed.

Anaxa laughed haughtily, shrugging his shoulders. ''Do you think I've been doing those nightly medical exams every day out of boredom? Do you think I cared much about a part that you always seemed uncomfortable with me doing?''

''The heart...'' whispered Phainon, clutching the fabric of his shirt right where it covered that organ.

Anaxa nodded. ''If I listened to your heart so intently, it's because I sensed that something was wrong. Not entirely wrong, but it's true that I always did it when you were relaxed. Lying down. Rested.'' Phainon pressed his lips together, understanding what the older meant.

''W... would you like to do it now?'' whispered the young man, clearly uncomfortable with the idea.

Anaxa stared at him, sensing his tension, sighing wearily but understandingly. ''Is there any reason you don't like me listening to your heart?'' Phainon tensed again, lowering his head completely. ''Phainon, I don't want to do anything that makes you uncomfortable, but keeping things to yourself won't help you recover. Unfortunately, there is very little we can do for your physical recovery, now that we are mere mortals, so please, help us, help me free you from that burden you carry.'' Seeing how reluctant Phainon was, Anaxa moved closer to him, squeezing his shoulder affectionately. ''Not telling anyone what you suffered doesn't help anyone. Least of all you.''

Phainon exhaled wearily, nodding with the same weakness, opening his eyes, which had a golden glow.

Anaxa was surprised by this, but remained calm, seeing how Phainon's body, despite his wounds and scars, did not look like those times when his body broke like a vase when he had those outbreaks. Those hallucinations.

''You... you know that I managed to hurt Nanook, make them bleed, and that thanks to that... it was easier to achieve our salvation.''

Anaxa nodded patiently, forcing himself to remain calm as he saw the look of horror on Phainon's face as he recalled that memory.

''Before I managed to hurt him, I fought an Emanator. He was the one who, well...'' He raised his stump, exhaling a dry, bitter laugh. ''When I managed to wound Nanook, I know it was because I burned all the coreflames I could from the rage and helplessness I felt, from everything I had to live through, what I had to do to you, so that it would be in vain... but after that... I was left without strength.''

Phainon sighed deeply, blinking slowly, smiling gratefully at Anaxa when he squeezed his shoulder in a sign of support. ''I remember falling... into the abyss... into nothingness, when...''

His jaw tightened, Anaxa seriously considering stopping the boy when he saw how he looked. ''When that Emanator came back and caught me... and in a matter of seconds I had Nanook in front of me, their stature reduced to that of a normal person, although the wretch was still a giant next to me.''

Anaxa snorted, in a mixture of bitter amusement and horror. If Phainon was one of the tallest and most muscular men he had ever known, what would that God be like if the boy himself called him a giant?

Phainon did not continue. His hand trembled as he clutched his blanket in anger, and inexplicably, no tears fell from his eyes even though his sclera was more red than white.

Anaxa went to stop him. It was still too soon. It had only been a little over a month since he had found him; it wasn't fair to put him through this.

But Phainon cut him off just as the alchemist opened his mouth.

''When I was under the arms of that cruel God... he... put his hand in my chest wound.'' Phainon pulled his shirt down from his neck enough to show that strange scar, Anaxa stopping his wrist when he saw him digging his nails into his still-wounded skin. ''I felt it perfectly, Professor Anaxagoras, how... how he squeezed my heart. How he tortured it.''

Anaxa remained serious, firm, even though his body resisted the tremor of rage and terror at what his precious student was telling him. ''And I... I tried to grab his hand, but I only had one arm and I couldn't touch anything because that God had his limbs separated but functional! And besides, I didn't have all the coreflames with me anymore! If I... if I couldn't face him with those billion pieces of coreflames, how could I, at that moment—''

''Phainon.'' Anaxa replied firmly, seeing how the boy was really trying to hurt himself in the chest.

''Even so, I fought. I promise you, Professor, I tried to fight—''

''I believe you, ayópi…'' whispered Anaxa, in a mixture of tenderness and sorrow.

''But the Emanator decided to grab my arm... and that torture came back... stronger. More scorching.''

Anaxa was startled when something like black cracks appeared around Phainon in the environment. It was as if his room was breaking apart. The atmosphere of the room.

And his eyes were changing from blue to gold... so quickly…

He had to stop the younger now.

''Phainon, come on, calm down, please.''

''I... I still feel Zephyro's hand on my arm, lifting it, giving Nanook complete freedom to put his whole hand in there, as if I were a damn toy, so that he would know what it was like to try to stop his precious Irontomb—''

''Phainon.'' Anaxa whispered again, fearing that those wings would reappear.

''...and I tried to free myself from both of them, but I couldn't. I mustn't. When at that moment I just wanted to run away... to stop suffering, but it was my destiny. It was my goal to save you...''

''Ayópi!''

''...and... and every time... the cold metal of that thing... it's so similar to his hand... I... I don't...''

Anaxa finally silenced that trembling delirium when he took him in an embrace, having to allow that trembling, stiff hand to go to Phainon's chest, his nails finally digging into the place that brought back such bad memories.

But it didn't go any further... Phainon's body seemed inert in the face of that embrace.

''You're not there anymore, Phainon. And you'll never come back. You've sacrificed enough for us, we don't want you to go through that hell again, and we won't allow it. They're just memories now...''

''But they still hurt as if I were living them right now...'' Phainon sobbed, his voice broken.

''Then talk to us! Let it out when it happens again! Share your damn hell with us! Do you think we don't want that? That we don't want to give you back even a tiny part of everything you've done for us?'' And before Phainon could respond indignantly, Anaxa cut him off again. ''And even if you hadn't been the hero who brought about the Nova Era. Even if you hadn't been the one who did the least for this dawn, we would still be by your side! We would still want to support you in this way! Because you are loved, Phainon, get that engraved in that huge empty head of yours!'

Phainon trembled with pure surprise and emotion as Anaxa dried tears that never fell, simply caressing his cheeks with a tenderness so similar to Aglaea's but with Anaxa's characteristic touch. The alchemist sighed with relief when he managed to pull that hand away from the battered skin of his chest.

He waited for whatever Phainon wanted to say, curious when he saw him glancing around the room and beyond the hallway.

''Where is Aglaea?''

''Ugh... if I had only mentioned her in my mind, why should the boy remember her?'' Anaxa huffs, annoyed.

Although, in Phainon's defence, it was normal for him to wonder about her whereabouts if, after suffering what he had just suffered, Aglaea still did not come to his aid.

''What a change of subject to avoid answering me, huh?'' Anaxa laughed, trying to throw him off the scent a little. He couldn't tell him the truth yet without knowing how things had gone between Aglaea and the prince. He laughed amusedly as she saw Phainon lower his head in embarrassment. ''She's gone to... do something. She'll tell you more later.''

''Hmmm...'' Phainon nodded with a sound. After that, he exhaled again, a calmer sigh. ''I'll do it. Or at least I'll try.'' he said, looking back at the professor, who arched his one eye. ''Share my hell with you.''

Anaxa nodded softly, just a thin line that you would need a telescope to see that smile form. ''That's all we need, lad.''

— — — — — — — — — — — — — — — —

It wasn't difficult to find the prince of Castrum Kremnos.

Despite not having the power of her threads in the Grove nor having regained her vision, her power still had a connection to his loved ones, and that bright, furious red aura was unmistakable.

She sat quietly beside him, knowing that Mydei had detected her several metres before. The conversation had to begin in as calm an atmosphere as possible...

Surprisingly, before Aglaea could begin the conversation, Mydei interrupted her with a tired sigh. ''How are you, Lady Aglaea?''

''Still getting used to this new world.''

''You're not the only one, believe me.''

''I imagined as much.''

Another silence, not uncomfortable, but too... informal.

Both heirs respected and appreciated each other, but they never reached that level of intimacy unlike the others.

Castorice, Hyacine, Tribios... Phainon. They all managed to find a place in the hearts of the Heir of Conflict and the Heiress of Romance.

But Mydei arrived too late to meet the Aglaea who had charmed all of Okhema and Amphoreus, and Aglaea did not even have time to get to know him well before the prince left immediately for his desolate home upon receiving the coreflame that was originally intended for Phainon.

By the Titans... that event was only... a few years ago? But it felt like centuries.

''How are the girls?''

''They're fine.'' replied Mydei, Aglaea unable to help smiling when she detected a certain tenderness in the prince's voice. She was greatly pleased to see the love that this powerful man felt for her girls. For her protégées. ''And you?''

Aglaea sighed, shaking her head, unable to continue with such an empty and artificial conversation.

Her lips formed an ugly grimace, sighing again, before dropping the bombshell.

''I'm very sorry, Mydeimos.''

That was all the prince needed to know. Aglaea heard him get up from the marble bench, sensing his anger and, above all, his disbelief.

''I... I HAD AN ARGUMENT WITH CASTORICE! SHE'S SO ANGRY AT ME RIGHT NOW FOR DARING TO ASK IF THE PROFESSOR ANAXAGORAS WOULD BE ABLE TO HIDE THE LOCATION OF PHAINON FROM US!! YOU DON'T KNOW HOW OFFENDED SHE WAS WITH ME FOR THAT!''

Aglaea bit her lip, but remained firm in the face of Mydei's anger. After all, it was to be expected.

But it hurt her deeply to know that she had not only disappointed Mydei, but had also hurt Castorice in a much deeper way. Not only her, but Anaxa as well...

''WHY!?'' Aglaea didn't know how to feel when that anger turned to despair. To... a devastating sadness. ''How could you hide something like this from us when we had been searching for MONTHS!? When...'' Aglaea tensed, praying inside that the cut wasn't because she had made him cry.

By the Titans... Aglaea did not want to be the first person in the world to hear the Prince of Castrum Kremnos cry. She would not know how to deal with something like that.

''...when I thought I had lost him...'' he whispered in a voice so low that Aglaea almost did not detect it, surprised because she never thought the prince could sound so... helpless. Desolate.

After a few seconds of silence, which Aglaea offered to allow him to calm down, the woman began again with another apology. ''If I have hidden this from you, even though it is obvious, I must say that it was not out of malice.''

''I want to believe that, of course, but I can't understand how you could have hidden something like that!'' Aglaea heard a sound of surprise come from the prince. ''Hyacine... she knows, doesn't she?'' Aglaea nodded. ''And you forced her to hide it too!''

''Mydeim—''

''How far could you go with—''

''MYDEI, PLEASE, LISTEN TO ME! THEN YOU CAN JUDGE US AS MUCH AS YOU WANT, BUT YOU MUST LISTEN TO ME FIRST! AT LEAST TO UNDERSTAND HYACINE!''

Aglaea's cry drew curious glances, which were immediately scattered by the threatening gaze of those golden orbs.

Aglaea shook her head wearily. ''If Hyacine has agreed not to tell you anything, it's not because we forced her to, but because... she understood us, as much as it hurt her.'' Her blind green eyes rose up against those furious, intense suns. ''Do you really think I would want to hide something like that from you? That I would want my poor Hyacine to have to go through that lie? Put her through that? You say Castorice is angry with you for suggesting that about Anaxa. If she has that faith and respect for her teacher, doesn't that make you think that Anaxa has hidden that information for a reason?''

''I can't think of a reason why he would have hidden from us that Phainon was alive, along you, when we had believed for months that he was dead! That he had failed to...''

Mydei fell silent again, Aglaea for the first time grateful for her blindness so she wouldn't have to see such an imposing and noble man looking so devastated... because of her and her beloved.

But she had to have faith in Mydei. Hyacine had the strength to endure the prince's questions and carry that lie despite having suffered first-hand Phainon's terror of being in her presence.

If Cipher could hide her lie for centuries to bring about the Era Nova, Mydei could face that horrible truth.

''Phainon is terrified of your presence, Mydeimos.'' she whispered, with a tactfulness that surely surprised even the prince. ''When Hyacine came, it was because Phainon developed such a high fever that we thought we were going to lose him.

She was angry with us for hiding it, and rightly so, just as I understand your indignation. But when Phainon woke up and saw her standing there...''

The blonde shook her head, sighing regretfully. ''I don't want that for you. I don't want anyone to suffer what she suffered. I don't want Phainon to be in that situation if he's not ready yet.'' Despite her blind gaze, Mydei could feel her steady stare on him. ''And unfortunately, he's still not ready, Mydeimos.''

Mydei tried to process the information, not knowing what to do. Not knowing which part of his body to move, not knowing what to say, not knowing... anything.

''But... uh... Anaxagoras and you—''

''We were the ones who fell least under his blade after all those cycles.''

''But you fell likewise!''

''But our relationship with him is completely different from the one he has with the girls. The one he has with you.''

''That doesn't make sense!'' Mydei snorted, helpless. Unable to accept that truth.

Aglaea did not respond to his anger. She only showed him understanding. ''I'm so sorry. That's all I can say, Mydei.''

He heard Mydei clench his jaw tightly, finally letting out an exhausted sigh. ''He... he doesn't want to see me...''

''It's not that he doesn't want to. He longs to be with you again.'' Mydei's back tensed at this. ''But he simply can't, Mydei. Those memories... all the times he had to kill you... all those times he forced himself to kill his friends when they wanted to save him...''

''In my cycles, I may not remember, but if they are in the data collected by the trailblazer, I did not try to save him. I accepted his challenge—''

''Mydeimos, please. Now you're going to tell me that the reason you accepted being killed by him is because you never cared about him, or because you knew that Khaslana had no choice but to kill you in order to continue his mission, and you decided to make it as easy as possible for him by pretending to hate him?''

Mydei fell silent, turning pale, while Aglaea let out a dry laugh. ''Do you really think Phainon doesn't know that? I know... the poor guy isn't very bright about a lot of things. But when it comes to you? Nothing gets past him.''

''Then if he knows me so well, he should know that I don't hold it against him for all those times he killed me! Because it's thanks to those deaths that we are where we are now!''

''It was 33 million cycles, Mydei. As much as Phainon knows you don't hate him, it's not easy to forget that he had to kill the love of his life... that many times.''

But Mydei denied it again. ''You say I challenged him to hide my concern for him. To make him see that I didn't care if he killed me! But that's not true! In most of those cycles, Mydei and Ph— Khaslana, never fell in love! Never—''

''Either you're trying to fool me, or you're blinder than me if you believe that during those 33 million cycles, he never stopped loving you. I remind you that the Flame Reaver is the Phainon who retains the memories of all previous cycles. The Flame Reaver is the Phainon who is at Anaxa's house, resting.''

''He's also that idiot who fainted in that sauna because he thought he could beat me in a competition typical of my homeland!''

Aglaea couldn't help but laugh at that memory, nodding. "And he's also the same person who discovered, a few hours after discovering that the Flame Reaver had killed you, that it was precisely himself. And then... he remembered all of that. Remember all those cycles.''

Mydei snorted, like a caged lion, not knowing what else to say. ''What he has experienced is beyond our reach—''

''THEN CALL THE TRAILBLAZER! LET THOSE STUPID GENIUSES WHO KNOW MORE THAN ALL OF US HELP HIM!'' Faced with Aglaea's surprised look, Mydei let out a dry, desperate laugh. ''HAVE YOU EVEN CONSIDERED THAT!?''

''We've been so... obsessed with Phainon's recovery that we haven't even thought about it. At least I haven't...''

''Tsk, unbelievable.'' Mydei snorted, but rather than anger and indignation, it sounded like a despairing regret at this discovery.

Aglaea remained silent, ashamed that she had overlooked something so important. ''It's not just the memories of those cycles...'' whispered the woman, unable to stop herself from continuing. ''Mydei... in his confrontation with Irontomb. With... Nanook, Phainon lost an arm.'' Mydei's eyes widened, terrified by this information. ''And he...''

''Let me guess. He thinks I wouldn't want to be in his presence anymore, right?'' Aglaea snorted bitterly, nodding. ''Tsk, you did a terrible job raising someone as stupid as him.''

Aglaea pressed her lips together, agreeing with him, not liking the prince's silence. ''What are you going to do?''

Due her blindness, she couldn't see how Mydei deflated like a balloon, letting out the most exhausted sigh in the world. ''I will not be the one to hinder his recovery. I will wait for him, as I always have. In this new Era, in that cycle and in all the previous ones.''

Aglaea nodded, proud before the prince. ''But... please. Keep us informed of his progress.''

''I will, I promise.''

Mydei nodded, tapping the ground with the tip of his sandals, growling inwardly. ''I'll... I'll go back to Okhema. I can tell Cas, right?'' Aglaea nodded. ''And... Lady Aglaea, can you be honest with me?''

''It's the least I owe you, Mydeimos.''

''Do you really think we'll see each other—''

''Of course.''

''—soon?''

There Aglaea fell silent, making an ugly grimace. ''I can't promise you that, Mydei. Phainon has too many ups and downs, and the truth is, even he doesn't know what's best for him. But we will fight to reunite our family soon.''

''Family...'' Mydei whispered weakly. ''Heh, you know that most of the victims of Castrum Kremnos of the Black Tide have not been revived? My friends, my father... my mother...''

''I'm so sorry, Mydeimos...''

''...Aedes Elysae is still a wasteland. No one has been resurrected there either.'' Aglaea nodded weakly at this information. ''But... if I know Phainon as well as I hope I do, I don't think he cares. Because we have Cas. We have Hyacine, Lady Tribios... well, Phainon knows Ciphera better than I do, but I'm getting to know her.''

''How is she?''

''She keeps teasing and laughing about the news that you're in the Grove with Professor Anaxagoras. Joking that she'll pay you a surprise visit, but Lady Tribios has already threatened to cut off her tail and ears if she dares to do that.''

Aglaea laughed softly, feeling sad that she couldn't be close to that crazy girl she loved like her own daughter. Of the other members of the heirs...

Despite her blindness, Aglaea could clearly feel Mydei staring at her.

''I consider you part of my new family too.'' he said, his voice firm, angry... and at the same time vulnerable. Damn it, was this really how the untouchable heirs of Crisos had ended up? Was that what it meant to be more human than demigods? ''As a leader. A head of the family.'' Mydei finished, ending Aglaea's internal debate.

She nodded gratefully. ''Phainon and I will return to Okhema soon, Mydei. I promise.''

''We will eagerly await the return of the last two missing members.'' he whispered wearily, turning away and saying goodbye.

But to Aglaea's surprise, Mydei stopped, stammering uncomfortably, which was unlike the prince. ''I suppose there really are three members. I'm sorry I overlooked your... well, partner, I suppose. No offence if that's not the case, not that I care much.''

Aglaea laughed again, assuring him that he had nothing to worry about, and the prince finally left. This made Aglaea's journey home more difficult and harder than she had expected.

···—–——······——–—······—–—–—······—–—–—···

''How did it go?'' Anaxa asked softly when Aglaea came in and headed straight for the bathroom to wash her face.

''Horrible. Hard. But he understood.''

''Hhmm...'' Anaxa murmured, hugging the blonde, feeling her skin tense. ''Are you all right?''

''I still can't get used to your gestures of affection.'' Aglaea hid her nose in the alchemist's neck, relaxing at his touch. ''It's as if that first relationship we had never existed, and I were a stupid teenager whose crush has reciprocated her feelings and fulfilled her childish, romantic dream.''

Anaxa laughed, Aglaea loving how her shoulders rose at that action, melting further into her embrace. ''So he left the Grove then?''

''Yes... he's going back to Okhema. He's asked us not to delay in going.''

''It all depends on the boy.''

''How is he, by the way?'' The magic of that embrace was broken by Aglaea's concern.

Anaxa shrugged, exhaling a long, bored sigh. ''More or less like you. Things have gone well, but... well. The situation could be better.'' Anaxa looked towards the room where Phainon was. ''I wish it were better.'' Aglaea raised an eyebrow, knowing there was more. But she closed her eyes, a shiver running down her spine when the stubborn, gruff alchemist kissed her forehead. ''We'll talk tomorrow. Now you need to rest.''

He accompanied the woman to his sister's room, Aglaea unable to tear herself away from that pleasant body heat.

''I thought about tomorrow, that he should come with us to the Academy,'' whispered Anaxa's voice, low enough not to even interfere with the peaceful silence.

''Are you sure?''

''If his physical condition deteriorates in the end, I think we can deal with him to get him home.''

Aglaea sighed, nodding to Anaxa's proposal. ''We should tell him that Mydei has been here...''

''Tomorrow too. He'll be asleep or trying to sleep now, and that news will disturb his rest. Besides, who's going to tell him, you? You can barely stand up?''

''Shut up.'' the woman snorted, enjoying the soft laughter she heard behind her.

Aglaea sank into bed, letting out the most peaceful and satisfied sigh, when she heard the door open but the bed did not give way. ''Where are you going?''

''I have to take some notes. I won't be long.''

''But is it about Phainon?''

''Aglaea, go to sleep. As I said, we'll talk tomorrow.'' When the woman opened her mouth again, the man snorted with a calmness that, months ago, she would have found impossible to believe in him. ''Don't be stubborn, woman, and go to sleep.''

Aglaea grumbled, but to her misfortune, she obeyed him, because although he was right that she was tired... she knew that whatever Anaxa wanted to investigate... was not Aglaea's subject.

The main reason why their relationship had worked so well in the past, and why Aglaea had regained hope that her future would be spent growing old by his side, was that Anaxa always counted on her when he needed her knowledge.

But she couldn't help feeling useless, knowing so little about what was happening to her beloved protégé.

Mydei's question came back to her mind, wondering if Anaxa had also completely forgotten to ask for help from people who knew Lygus better or from the Aeons who had played so much with her world... or if there was another reason why he wanted to hide Phainon so desperately.
