See the end of the chapter for more notes

Aglaea stayed by Phainon's side the whole time as he descended the stairs, the poor boy having to lean on her when one of his feet gave way on the penultimate step, his motherly figure always at his side, ready to hold him up.

Just like in the old days...

・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・

''Lady Aglaea, I told you I'm fine!'' snorted a young Phainon who was even shorter than the blonde in that time.

She, however, was cleaning his face, running her tongue over the handkerchief she was washing it with, making the younger blush. ''Lady Aglaea!!! They're looking at us!''

''And?''

''It's embarrassiiiiiiiiing— LOOK, CIPHER IS ALREADY LAUGHING!''

''Ignore that andreíkelo'' laughed Aglaea affectionately, patting the younger on the back to indicate that they should go home.

The blonde tried to help her protégé, but he ensure her he was alright, walking several strides ahead of the woman.

But after a few steps, Phainon's knees gave way, and Aglaea immediately caught him before he fell to the ground. ''What were you saying?'' the woman teased, and the younger couldn't help but join in her laughter.

・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・

''Even blind, you're always so quick to catch me.'' whispered Phainon, when he regained his footing, his only arm unable to break free from the now slim and small body, compared to his own, of the woman who had almost given him life.

Aglaea laughed tenderly, stroking her protégé's hair. ''Whenever I can, I will be there to support each and every one of you.''

Phainon nodded, Anaxa's heavy footsteps echoing behind them as he descended the stairs.

''Are we leaving now?''

They walked very slowly, Aglaea staying close to Phainon the whole time while Anaxa brought up the rear.

Suddenly, the alchemist saw his partner looking at him anxiously, understanding what she meant.

''Before we go to the Academy, we have to tell you something.''

Phainon blinked, incredulous, looking at his two companions. ''Is it... important?''

''Quite'' whispered Aglaea, still hesitant.

''Is it good news?'' he whispered with a small smile, Aglaea frowning with pity and guilt.

''No, dear. I wish it were'' Phainon lost that faint smile, a worried expression forming on his face.

''It's not horrible or serious news either, lad, calm down. But it's news you deserve to know... even if it hurts to hear it.''

Phainon blinked slowly, looking at the two figures he considered parental.

Aglaea took a breath, finally letting out that horrible secret that should never have been one. ''Mydei was here. He arrived at the Grove yesterday and spent the whole day looking for you, like a madman.''

Aglaea clasped her hands, wishing she could see Phainon's reaction, being calmed by Anaxa, as the alchemist would surely have noticed her tension.

''Yesterday, Aglaea went to talk to him. She explained the situation and, surprisingly, he understood—''

''Of course he would understand. Mydei is one of the most tolerant and understanding people I have ever met in my life.'' Phainon cut him off sharply, his gaze lowering, his eyes wide open. Affected. Surprised.

Anaxa sighed, apologising for that comment. ''He'll wait for you, lad. As long as you need.''

Phainon said and did nothing. He stared at the floor, his expression tense and difficult to understand.

Although Aglaea couldn't see his reaction, she felt his regret, approaching the hero, relieved that he accepted her touch.

''What we talked the other day... have you changed your mind?'' Phainon blinked very slowly, still without looking up. ''I can quickly send one of my garmentmakers to tell him to come back.

He'd be here before sunset.''

''No.'' Phainon whispered weakly. ''No... don't do that, Lady Aglaea, please.''

The blonde nodded, stroking his hair, which was still dirty, due to Anaxa's insistence that the poor hero was not yet ready to take a bath.

''When we get back from the Academy, how about I run you a bath? We can stop by the soap shop and buy your favourite scent.'' Raising an amused eyebrow at Anaxa, the blonde added that she doubted he had any.

She managed to elicit a weak but sincere laugh from the hero, who nodded with a sound that showed he was eager to finally feel his body and hair clean.

''You've already cleaned your body.'' Anaxa snorted indignantly.

''With wet towels, Professor.'' Phainon replied, unconvinced, rushing ahead of the pair, urging them to hurry.

''You're just going for a walk. I'm going to have to put up with a bunch of students, most of whom don't want to be there. So slow down, ayópi''

They walked in silence again, broken by Phainon when Aglaea took his wrist and squeezed it affectionately, knowing that the white-haired man wanted to say something.

''I want to see him...''

''But?''

Phainon clenched his jaw, making a great effort not to bite his lip, as he would surely cause himself serious injury if he did so. ''What if... I'm not ready yet? What if I react the same way I reacted to the poor Hyacine?'' Phainon melted at the touch of his motherly figure, as she cradled his tense jaw affectionately, finally relaxing it. ''I can't see that expression on Mydei, Aglaea... I don't want to hurt him any more...''

Aglaea sighed, saddened by that last sentence, but the guilt Phainon felt would not go away overnight.

It had been 33 million cycles.

Thirty-three million.

It was... bloody outrageous.

No one could ever understand the grief and pain Phainon carried. That's why the least each of them could do was to respect, understand, and above all, love him again as they had always loved him in those previous cycles, even though the pain of betrayal was even greater because it came from a loved one.

''As Anaxa said, he will wait for you as long as it takes.''

Phainon nodded, sounding convinced, and they both started walking again, afraid of being scolded by the harsh alchemist.

''By the way,'' Anaxa said suddenly when he finally saw them by his side, arching his single eyebrow, amused, looking at Phainon ''what did you think we were going to say to you? I saw you looking too happy for a brief moment, lad.''

''Ah... uhh... well... heh'' Phainon tensed, his teeth showing in that nervous smile as he scratched his head. ''It's... it's just stupid, Professor!''

''Ohh... now I'd like to know what it is.''

''You don't want to know, Lady Aglaea, believe me.'' muttered Phainon, hiding his face in his hands.

''Come on, lad, now I'm curious too.''

''If you tell me, I'll tell you stories about when Anaxa was after me and I ignored her.' laughed Aglaea, looking at her beloved with feigned cruelty.

''What a liar you are.''

That discussion completely cheers up Phainon, but the two older ones did not give up, waiting for Phainon's answer.

''I... uh, well... I thought... heh...'' He looked at Aglaea, embarrassed, his gaze so deep that even Aglaea felt it. ''That you're gonna told me you are expecting'' Aglaea blinks, very slowly, disbelief on her face ''Ex…expecting a baby, of course''

Anaxa cuts that silence with a howly laugh, clapping his hands and then gently patting Phainon on the back. ''That's the funniest thing I've ever heard in my life, and I've had to listen to some utter nonsense.''

''Agh... shut up, Professor!'' muttered Phainon, completely embarrassed, unable to look Aglaea in the face. ''I... well! You look so good together lately, and I don't know... Aglaea is leaving so suddenly, so...''

''Well, the most logical thing to think is that she's pregnant. Yes, that makes sense.'' Anaxa teased him again, affectionately.

''Anaxa...'' Aglaea scolded him.

''Besides, it doesn't make sense. Unless you think she and I made up the same day I called her to let her know you were alive—''

''ANAXÁGORAS!'' Aglaea snorted, her cheeks the same colour as Phainon's.

Anaxa simply laughed wickedly, Phainon snorting and shaking his head. ''Sometimes you're impossible, Professor!'' he muttered, walking ahead of the couple, Anaxa swearing she could see smoke coming out of his big white head.

''Aaah... that was a good one. I really enjoyed that laugh.''

''You're very cruel.'' Aglaea replied, unable to laugh now that Phainon had finally walked away from them.

''Does that fool realise that something like that happening between us is practically impossible? Besides, nothing has happened between us yet.''

Aglaea rolled her eyes, amused by that last comment, without giving it too much importance. ''Impossible? You think so? Because I think you're capable, through experimentation, of achieving something like that.''

''Would you like to have my baby, dear?'' he raised his eyebrow, amused.

''When dromas fly.''

''Don't bring dromas into this!''

— — — — — — — — — — — — — — — —

The return to the Academy was... strange.

Many people still remembered Phainon. They spoke to him as if nothing had happened.

A student who had attended remedial classes with Phainon, where he failed and she barely passed, asked him if they would see each other again in the new classes.

Phainon felt as if he were not a human being who had obtained billions of coreflames inside him. As if he did not have to reset lives and lives that were almost identical, killing his loved ones for them.

As if he had not been in hell itself, facing two terrifying creatures from the universe when he was merely data created by a vile and brilliant mind.

He was simply... Phainon, the bright-smiling student of the Grove, who always drove Professor Anaxágoras crazy.

And for some reason... no matter how hard he tried to reconnect with that past of his, where he was so happy... there was something. A feeling that prevented him from feeling the happiness and peace he was struggling so hard to achieve.

“Hey, what happened to the prince of Castrum Kremnos? ”

“Oh, you're right! I haven't seen him all day! ”

“Haven't you been to the library? You know he's almost always there since he arrived. ”

“Noo... I stopped by and the guard told me he hasn't been there all day. ”

“Awww... don't tell me he's left! He was so kind... ”

“Only kind? ” laughed one of the students, her group bursting into laughter.

Phainon stopped dead in his tracks when he heard that conversation, Aglaea slowly approaching him, while Anaxa continued walking towards his class, unaware that he was being left alone.

''Do you want to go home?'' the blonde asked affectionately.

''Mydei would love this place... I... I would have loved to show him this place...''

Aglaea smiled weakly, lifting her chin, snorting irritably at feeling Anaxa so far away. She didn't want to shout like a vulgar coarse woman, so she asked Phainon to wait there.

But as soon as she tried to leave, Phainon stopped her, without her noticing how hard his nails were digging into her wrist.

''Phainon, calm down—''

''It would have been perfect... he would show me the library he promised me, and I would show him the place where I was educated... but he never got to do that... because I burned his beloved library before we had that chance.'' Phainon began to laugh, Aglaea not caring that strangers from the Academy were watching her, shouting Anaxa's name. ''I... I killed him before we could... before we got there...''

Suddenly, Phainon's grip on her disappeared, the woman hearing only a metallic, artificial squeak as her threads broke when they tried to detect Phainon's aura.

She was paralysed for only a brief second, not detecting anything, no, but feeling the pain of detecting whatever was in front of Phainon.

She tried to cover Phainon with her body, even though the younger was twice her size. When she began to hear screams and frightened whispers, she growled, hating with all her soul her blindness for not knowing what the hell was happening to Phainon, and because every time she touched him, she suffered like an electric shock and the skin under her palm disappeared.

''Ti sto kaló!?'' Anaxa snorted, Aglaea feeling immense relief.

''Let's go home, now!''

That irritating sound accompanied them all the way, Aglaea not knowing how many times Phainon almost fell face-first onto the ground because, again and again, his body disappeared only to reappear.

Growling irritably, the woman summoned her garmentmakers, Anaxa asking if she was crazy.

''Lady Tribios will find out that you summoned them, and she will know that one of the reasons you are in danger. Do you want her to come—''

''I DON'T CARE!'' Aglaea snorted. ''I DON'T CARE WHO COMES, WHO FINDS OUT, OR WHAT THEY MIGHT SAY! TI DIÁOLO IS WRONG WITH HIM, ANAXA!? WHY AM I NOT EVEN HEARING HIM!?''

The man remained silent, insisting that the most important thing was to get home.

Aglaea's garmentmakers arrived in a matter of seconds, their presence helping to speed up the journey home.

When they finally arrived home, they didn't even go to the bedroom.

They laid Phainon down on the kitchen table, Anaxa lovingly pushing Aglaea aside, assuring her that if he needs her help, he would ask for it.

The woman clenched her fists in anger, but remained still, not wanting to hinder anything that might help Phainon.

When she heard the first whimper of pain coming from his throat, she didn't know how to feel. Relieved to finally hear his voice? Or terrified that this was the first thing she had heard?

But when Anaxa's irritated and helpless snort joined the incessant whimpering, the woman couldn't take it anymore.

She called her garmentmakers again, walking out the door.

''Aglaea—''

''I'm leaving.''

''I figured as much, but why?'' Anaxa snorted, leaving Phainon briefly in the care of the garmentmakers.

''Don't you realise, Anaxa? We can't do this alone! This is too much for us!''

''We've been taking care of Phainon since—''

''AND LOOK AT HIM NOW! HOW MANY RELAPSES MUST HE SUFFER BEFORE WE UNDERSTAND THAT WE ARE NOT THE HELP HE NEEDS!? WE ARE NOT HELPING HIM, ANAXA, FOR MNESTIA'S SAKE!''

''AND YOU THINK THAT PRINCE, OR YOUR DEAR CIPHER, OR EVEN LADY TRIBIOS, WHO HASN'T EVEN REGAINED HER FORM YET, IS JUST THE HELP WE NEED!?''

''I'm not going to ask them for help, but rather the genius friends of the trailblazer.''

Anaxa paled at this, stopping the blonde, who was snorting his name in irritation.

''You can't do that!''

''WHY?'' she roared like a lioness. ''WHY CAN'T I ASK FOR HELP FROM PEOPLE WHO CLEARLY KNEW THE BASTARD WHO LEFT PHAINON IN THIS SITUATION BETTER THAN US?''

''BECAUSE I DON'T KNOW IF THEY WANT TO HELP HIM, AGLAEA! BECAUSE I DON'T KNOW IF, KNOWING THAT PHAINON HAS SURVIVED, HE WILL BE IN DANGER AGAIN!''

Finally, Aglaea stopped struggling, opening her blind eyes wide, shaking her head in disbelief. ''They wouldn't dare.''

''Phainon is an Emanator of Destruction now, Aglaea. You also remember what Stelle told us—''

''Phainon detests that Aeon. He would never serve him!''

''You and I know that well, but what about them?''

''They are friends of Stelle! She would do anything to prevent them from harming Phainon! I trust her!''

''And so do I, and I doubt that those two geniuses would be capable of harming Phainon any further, but if those two know, the rest of the circle will sooner or later know too, and with that, the entire universe! We are no longer hidden, Aglaea, we are now in full view of all the other beings in this immense universe! Do you want Amphoreus to go back to war, when we are even weaker than we were before?!''

Aglaea remained silent, poor Phainon's whimpers still piercing her eardrums.

She snorts, with that fierce expression, shooking her head. ''If they want war, they'll get it. But I won't allow Phainon to continue suffering.'' Although she continued to appear furious, her eyes softened when she looked up at Anaxa. ''Let me go, my love.''

Anaxa's arms trembled at this plea, clenching his jaw in rage and helplessness, but finally obeying the blonde.

But before leaving, she promised him something. ''We haven't gone through hell to let some bloody aliens think they can take my loved ones away from me. Let whoever has to come, come, but Phainon needs outside help, Anaxa.''

And with that, Anaxa watched the woman he wishes to never loose again leaving his house, taking her telestate, surely to call the trailblazer.

He slammed the door shut when he saw most of his neighbours peering in, returning to what had disrupted the day, the week, and surely the entire month.

''Phainon... boy... ti sto kaló is going on with you?''

···—–——······——–—······—–—–—······—–—–—···

''I'm so sorry, Mydei...''

''Don't apologise again. I understand, I really do.'' whispered Mydei into his telestate, feeling saddened by the guilt that weighed on the poor healer. ''Hyacine, of all people, you are the one who least deserves our anger.''

''Even so... you suspected…''

''And you had to lie even though I know how much you hate that. So please, don't torture yourself anymore.''

He sighed with relief when Hyacine nodded, laughing softly as Ica purred to show her support for her friend.

''How much further do you have until you arrive to Okhema?''

''...

Quite a while. I've been at the entrance to the Grove for a couple of hours... thinking.''

''Mydei...''

''I just have to be patient, but... whatever... I hate that.'

''Heh, I know. Patience it's not a very common trait among your people.'' Hyacine laughed softly, eliciting an amused snort from the prince.

''I'll be there soon, I promise. And if you want, It will be me who talk to Casto—'' Mydei fell silent when he received another incoming call, his eyes widening in panic when he saw Aglaea's name. ''Hyacine, I'll call you right back!'' He hung up before receiving a response.

''Lady Agla—''

''Please return to the Grove as soon as possible.''

''What happened? What happened to him!?'' shouts Mydei, turning around inmediately.

''You're right, Mydei. We should have asked for help. I called Stelle, she'll come with Dan Heng to pick me up so I can talk to those two geniuses. But Anaxa can't do it alone.''

''But he... is he…'' Mydei fell silent at Aglaea's sigh. ''Something happened to him.

I don't know how to explain it very well because of my blindness, but it's something that has frightened even Anaxa.'' Mydei could feel Aglaea's anger even through the telestate. ''After so much suffering, he still has to go through these things...''

But Mydei slowed his pace, remaining... silent. Unsure. ''Are you sure I won't make his condition worse?"

Aglaea's silence killed him inside, and he closed his eyes tightly. ''I don't know, Mydeimos. But Anaxa doesn't deserve to be alone. Please call the girls. Be there, helping him even if it's only a little.''

Mydei nodded, wishing her luck, as he immediately called his healer friend.

''Mydei? What happened? Lady Tribios has left without saying anything!''

''Bring Cas and Cipher to the Grove immediately!''

After hanging up again, he hurried off, so different from his journey back to Okhema, looking at the sky. Looking at that shining sun.

''Hang in there, Phainon. Hang in there a little longer.''

Chapter Summary

····

Chapter Notes

It's here... it's finally here ( ๑ ˃̵ᴗ˂̵)و that damn reunion

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Anaxa sighed, without answering his beloved. His attention returned to the figure, still not recovered, who continued to suffer convulsions in his bed.

He had to be grateful that Aglaea's garmentmakers had not left, for he did not know how he could have lifted Phainon up to his room without their help.

He stood in front of the boy, his jaw tense, not knowing how to help or how to find out what the hell was happening to him.

In the absence of ideas, Anaxa had tried to comfort him. To reassure him.

But it was of little use, when every touch Phainon received caused him to have that break in space again and change his appearance. And that strange convulsion... it seemed very painful.

His mind did not abandon Aglaea either.

Although he understood the woman, for a brief moment he saw that cold, determined look in the weaver's eyes again. The same look he had seen thousands of years ago, in that previous cycle, when he lost her. When she sacrificed her humanity.

And Anaxa knew, very clearly, that Aglaea would take that path again without hesitation if it meant saving and protecting Phainon.

And he couldn't lose her... Not again... Not at this dawn...

Phainon's moan of pain brought him back to his senses, Anaxa feeling guilty for thinking about her when the hero needed him, but as soon as he sat down to try, and who knows, wake him up!? Calm him down!? That damn convulsion returned, causing one of the wounds on his torso to break open, as if it were glass, abruptly, golden blood flowing slowly from the opening.

''σκατά'' Anaxa growls, getting up to fetch his alchemy supplies and heal Phainon in the only way he could be healed when he looked like that.

He returned to the injured side so quickly that he almost tripped, falling and hissing helplessly when he saw those black wings glisten again, disappearing, along with Phainon's golden hair, as soon as he felt the strange healing the alchemist was using on his torso to cure him.

But again, that damn glitch returned, and Phainon took on a form that Anaxa knew but had never seen at dawn.

The Flame Reaver...

He was surprised to see the golden blood mixed with ghostly blue blood, Phainon coughing up that strange new blood.

''μαλακίες, μαλακίες! Boy! Boy, stay with me, please!'' Anaxa begged, shaking him hard, feeling so desperate and scared that he didn't even consider the possibility of hurting him. ''Come on, Phainon, σκατά, come back to your senses!''

Phainon still maintained that primal form, those empty eyes... hollow, staring at him.

He let out a dry, exhausted groan, his head falling as if it couldn't support its weight, held up by Anaxa. ''Boy, come on, come on. Talk to me. Stay conscious, please!''

Because if Phainon fell into a sleep in that state... Anaxa didn't know what would become of him.

Phainon groaned again, annoyed and tired, but his eyes opened once more, a single tear falling, which did not evaporate.

Not this...

''Pr...fes...'' Phainon muttered, exhaling another exhausted groan.

''Yes. That's right, lad, it's me! Tell me anything. What you feel, what you remember! I need to know what's happening to yo—''

Anaxa fell silent, tense, when he heard a knock at the door.

μαλακίες... the prince.

He forget about him…

Anaxa quickly glance at Phainon, who is struggling to keep his eyes open, gently laying him back on the bed.

But as soon as I get up to open the door and get some help, the Flame Reaver's appearance disappears, taking on the form of the Emanator once more, the previous blue blood being overshadowed by more bright golden blood.

''NO!!'' Anaxa growled, stressed. ''BOY! OPEN THE FUCKING DOOR! BREAK IT DOWN, I KNOW YOU CAN!'' Anaxa shouts, knowing that Mydei can hear him.

It didn't even occur to him to ask the garmentmakers to go and open the door for the prince, because as soon as they saw Phainon trying to get up, they went to stop him, and truth be told, the slightest help was needed.

Anaxa cast his healing spell on the strange wounds the poor hero had on his inhuman body, clenching his jaw in anger when he saw that it had little effect.

The prince's heavy footsteps reached the room, Anaxa wondering what his reaction would be when he saw Phainon looking like that.

He expected questions. He expected sadness. But Mydei immediately stood next to Anaxa, asking firmly what he needed.

Anaxa shook his head exhausted, saying he didn't know.

''Why is he like this?'' asked Mydei, pushing Aglaea's garmentmakers aside so that he could hold Phainon.

Anaxa shook his head again, not knowing what to say, sinking into dissociation due to his exhaustion.

Mydei wrinkled his nose, dissatisfied. He turned his sad gaze to the suffering figure, clenching his jaw. ''We should sedate him. You must have—''

''No! What if I put him to sleep and he never wakes up?'' Anaxa snorted, upset.

''Then give him something for the pain!''

''Boy, for someone who's supposed to be holding him down, you're doing a terrible job!'' Anaxa snorted angrily. ''Touch his arm properly and you'll know what I'm talking about!''

Mydei blinked, confused, but obeyed, his face turning pale when he noticed Phainon's skin was like... like clay. It wasn't human skin at all.

''I can't give him anything right now!''

Mydei remained silent, Phainon's tense wings catching his attention. He reached out and touched them, gently and lovingly squeezing those new limbs on his beloved's body.

That 'caress' seemed to calm Phainon briefly, as his jaw was no longer clenched in pain, and he finally let his body go still.

But those detestable, horrible moans of pain did not cease... and Anaxa knew he would lose his mind if he had to listen for another minute to the boy he wanted to care for and protect continuing to suffer like that without him being able to do anything.

''Bring the painkiller. Whatever... whatever you think he needs!''

''Didn't you just haven't heard—''

''JUST BRING IT, PROFESSOR ANAXÁGORAS!'' Mydei snorted, stressed, the older one blinking in disbelief, but he obeyed.

After all... what he can lose?

He decided to bring an analgesic that contained laudanum, which Anaxa had modified to have a much stronger effect.

He picked up the bottle with the syringe, shrugging his shoulders, wondering where the hell he was going to inject Phainon if he still hadn't returned to his human body.

And he was completely sure that if he returned to it, Phainon would return to either of his other two bodies to protect himself from the needle.

But Mydei grabbed his left wing, bending it down, stroking the part where those strange feathers came out. ''Here. This is flesh.''

Anaxa approached, surprised by the prince's suggestion.

''How do we know it will reach his bloodstream?''

Mydei clenched his jaw in anger, breaking one of his bracelets, whispering an apology to Phainon, then making a cut in that spot, golden blood staining those strange but beautiful feathers.

Tearing off part of his red cloth to plug the small wound, Mydei urged Anaxa to administer the damn analgesic, the alchemist nodding.

But as soon as Phainon felt the needle, he tried to pull away, Mydei being quick to restrain him. ''Even with your wings, you don't make it easy for me, right lad?'' Anaxa snorted with a tired smile, managing to achieve his goal thanks to Mydei.

But after administering the liquid, Phainon used gravitational power to push Anaxa and Mydei away from him, trying to escape from that room again, that broken convulsion returning to him so quickly that he didn't even have time to move away from the bed.

And... the figure he took on this time was once again that of the Flame Reaver...

Anaxa tensed at the reaction Mydei might have. In case he was paralysed or perhaps even resentment would arise in him, but the prince quickly approached Phainon, cradling that broken figure in his arms.

Phainon tried to break free from that grip, Mydei cradling his head, whispering something that Anaxa couldn't hear because of its low... and intimate tone.

But he didn't care or worry about it when he achieved his goal, which was to finally calm the poor hero.

The alchemist rose painfully, approaching the duo, relieved to see his body calm... even though his face said otherwise.

He was still in intense pain, and despite having his eyes closed, his body cried out that he was alert.

But a slight calm had finally arrived, the poor hero completely melted in the arms of his beloved.

Mydei laid him down on the bed, without letting go of his only hand, and even though Anaxa had never seen these two interact in the previous cycle... he had to admit that he was surprised by how little Mydei was affected by the fact that the figure he was seeing was not really his Phainon.

But rather his murderer.

Mydei continued to look at that broken figure as if... as if he were his everything.

''How do I treat his wounds?'' asked Mydei, snapping Anaxa out of his trance.

The body of the Flame Reaver was identical to that of the Emanator, after all. Only the colour of the blood had changed, and fortunately, its flow, which was lighter and less worrying.

''I'll take care of it'' Anaxa replied.

This time, his healing was effective, those strange, hollow wounds ceasing their blood loss.

Unfortunately, he couldn't tell if Phainon was regaining colour, due to his new face, and he wasn't going to consider his breathing valid now, when his chest was completely open, with blue flames inside instead of organs.

Could he risk feeling calm?

She grumbles, at seeing Phainon's breathing becoming softer. Sleepier.

So he gently slaps Phainon, clearly angering the prince for that action.

''What are you doing!?''

''Don't you remember what I told you before? He must not fall asleep.''

''He's clearly exhausted!!''

''And what he just went through reminds me too much of the reports of the battle of Hyacine and the others against Aquila. We don't know what could happen to him if he stays asleep.'' Anaxa snorted, finally disturbing the hero's 'light' rest.

Phainon squeezed his eyes shut, annoyed, Anaxa muttering pitifully, ''I know, lad, I know. I'm sorry, but I need you awake and you know it.''

Mydei snorted, helpless, but didn't argue with the alchemist again.

''Talk to him. Say something to him to keep him awake. A… anything!'' he snapped at the prince for the look the blond was giving to him.

''Do you think he'll be able to strike up a conversation with me?'' the prince replies, angrily.

''Of course not! But if all he gets is silence, he'll go back to sleep.''

''Then why don't you talk to him! You're clearly much more articulate than I am'' he replies again, tensely.

Anaxa snorted, rolling his eyes wearily. ''I must go to my office.'' Mydei pressed his lips together, dissatisfied. ''I need to know what the hell just happened to him, because what he's been through isn't normal.''

That statement calmed the prince, who nodded weakly, Anaxa looking again at the figure who was falling back asleep. ''Please, don't let him fall asleep. I know he deserves it, but he also deserves to live as he has always lived, and not as...'' The alchemist clenched his jaw in anger, ''as he was programmed by that imbecile genius.''

Mydei nodded again, gently shaking Phainon to wake him, the clear pain showing on his face when Phainon muttered weakly and heavily, interrupted again when he was just trying to rest.

══════════════════════════════════════════

After leaving the room, Anaxa staggered, as he had not slept for more than 24 hours, well the last night he had also stayed up all night trying to find out how Phainon was doing.

He never thought he would miss that his only concern was why the boy's heart beats weaker and why his recovery was so slow.

It had been less than five hours since that had been his only concern regarding his recovery, and now he felt like he was in the beggining. Or even worse, because when Anaxa found him, wounded and looking like the Emanator, he never showed the Flame Reaver's face or suffered... that horrible glitches and seizures he had just experienced.

His eye closed as soon as he sat down in the chair, and he slapped his face to wake himself up.

If he hadn't gone to bed yesterday when the woman of his life was waiting for him, what was the point of going now, when her life and the boy's were in grave danger?

The hours passed, and in front of him there was only a jumble of written gibberish, trying to make sense of something coded, his tired mind unable to help him.

He read over and over again the reports obtained by the trailblazer of the name of the programme that Lygus had given Phainon.

Neikos496.

He even tried to decipher what that name and numbering could mean, without getting anything out of the code.

It made no sense.

What had just happened to him made no damn sense.

...

Unless...

Anaxa plugged in the computer, one of many in the centre of his planet (and he was the quickest to figure out how it worked, with his friends from that spatial train congratulating him for it, Anaxa feeling super stupid for receiving praise for understanding such a simple device), and decided to infect it with a virus, but not before uninstalling the hard drive that the trailblazer had given him earlier.

He watched the computer's reaction, feeling an horrible chill as he understood the situation.

Then he decided to put the hard drive with the antivirus back in, grateful to be sitting down because if he had been standing, his knees would have buckled at the antivirus's reaction.

His lip trembled, his throat broke, and he hid his face in his hands, almost sobbing.

''Professor Anaxa?'' whispered an unfamiliar voice.

Anaxa turned quickly, surprised to see a tall, beautiful woman with a very familiar hair colour.

''Lady Tribios?''

The woman nodded, with a gentle smile. ''Oh... I... I had no idea you had regained your body.''

''It happened when I arrived at the Grove. I don't know how to explain it, but I felt so much concern for Agy... that it happened.'' whispered the sweet priestess, her eyes looking sad.

''I see... What did she tell you?''

''Only that you needed me. And not to worry about her.''

‘Tsk, of course. The fact that she went to another planet to ask the enemy for help, knowing that if that enemy refused, she would be enraged, is absolutely not worrying about her!'' Anaxa snorted, the priestess looking at the alchemist with pity.

''Professor Anaxa, please go and rest.''

Anaxa shook his head, harshly. ''I need to figure out how to fix this. How to save the boy.''

'Do you already have an idea of what happened to him?'' whispered the woman, surprised.

Anaxa smiled bitterly, shaking his head, completely unaware that Tribios knew the truth about Phainon. ''It can't be that... It has to not be that.''

Tribios slowly approached the alchemist, stroking his back. ''What do you think is wrong with Snowy, Naxy?''

Anaxa continued to stare at the computer screen, his single eye turning red, exhaling the most weary of sighs. ''That unlike us, Phainon has not yet obtained his humanity...'' He hid his face in his hands again, his body completely weakening. ''And he probably never will.''

Tribios blinked, confused, but remained calm. ''What Snowy has experienced... cannot be understood by human logic.'' Anaxa nodded weakly. ''But... forgive my ignorance, Professor, what happens if he doesn't obtain his humanity? In previous cycles, we weren't human and we were fine. Does Snowy really need it?''

''I don't know.'' Anaxa confessed. ''I don't know what will happen to him if he doesn't get his humanity. I don't know what the hell will happen to him if he finally gets it.'' He massages his forehead, sighing so tired and even Tribios shivers at that, his gaze heading out to the corridor, as if he had the hero's room in front of him. ''I don't know if what happened to him is Aglaea's and my fault.''

''Your fault? Why?''

''For treating him that way. For... for giving him love and warmth again. For treating him like... like our loved one.''

Tribios bit her lip, understanding the situation. ''And now the bloody prince is here too and... agh…''

''Naxy, you should go and rest.''

''Again with that nonsense!? Can't you see I can't?'' Anaxa snorted, irritated.

''With your head in the state it's in right now, you're not going to find any solution. The person standing before me right now is not the talented Professor Anaxágoras, who was able to guess the truth behind the gods, but Naxy, worried about his student.'' Anaxa twisted his lip, but did not argue. ''Please, go to sleep.''

But Anaxa shook his head slowly. ''I need to figure out what the hell happened to him. How the hell to save him.''

Tribios sighed, dissatisfied, skimming through Anaxa's reports. ''Did you compile all the data from the previous cycles?''

''Since I don't remember them, I asked the trailblazer to get them for me. Don't ask me how she got them, right now that's the least of my worries.''

Tribios pursed her lips, annoyed, Anaxa raising an eyebrow. ''Why don't you go with the boy? I think you'd be a better choice to be with him than Mydei. After all, this new body of yours was never known to him.''

''I'm not going to take away the intimacy De so desperately needs and deserves with Snowy, Anaxa.'' Tribios replied seriously.

Anaxa sighed, letting out a slight snort, assuring her that it wasn't his intention to sound that way. ''Snowy is recovering, and that makes him vulnerable.'' whispered Tribios, finally understanding what Anaxa was thinking. ''And being with De is possible—''

''To break him completely. Let him make him feel more human than ever.''

''And that's, unfortunately, bad.''

Anaxa sighed again, hiding his face in his hands. ''I don't know, Lady Tribios...''

Tribios picked up a couple of sheets of paper, tilting her head slightly. ''Perhaps I can find some answers at the temple of Oronix.''

''Why do you want to go there?''

''Time has always been the key to our Amphoreus. To our simulation. What better place to go than there?''

''Oronix is dead, Lady Tribios. All the titans fell.''

''But not her teachings. Not her legacy.'' the woman replied softly, placing the papers back on the desk. ''So come on, move aside, I have to copy all your reports that I think are important.''

''Pfft, then it's going to be all of them.'' Anaxa snorted, with a half-smile.

''All the more reason for you to move out of the way as soon as possible.''

Anaxa sighed wearily. ''Lady Tribios, for the last time, I won—''

''I'm asking you nicely, Anaxágoras.'' replied Tribios, with a coldness that even the alchemist felt penetrate his bones. ''You are the most important man to Agy. I will not allow her to lose the love of her life in order to save Snowy alone. So move aside.''

Anaxa gave in to Tribios' threat, getting up from his seat and heading for the door. ''Now that you mention that ηλίθιος,'' whispered the alchemist weakly, leaning against the doorframe, ''could you ask her what happened to the boy before he had that cosmic epileptic seizure? I never found out. We were... in too much of a hurry to take him home to look after him.''

Tribios turned, sadly, her gaze saying it all.

''Why don't you ask her yourself?'' Those blue sad eyes said.

But Tribios showed why she was Anaxa's favourite. She showed why she was the most respected and loved, and nodded to the alchemist, assuring him that she would ask her as soon as she finished with her work.

''Thank you, Lady Tribios.'' whispered Anaxa, before finally going to bed.

Finding Phainon still in his Flame Reaver's form did not lift his spirits, but Mydei continued to hold him as if he were his entire world, and not his killer.

And with that slight relief, he gathered enough strength to make it to his bed.

To that cold and lonely bed.

  • - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

Mydei continued to hold that weakened and fragile body with a care he never knew he was capable of in his entire existence.

He sighed, exhausted, his hand caressing Phainon's strange, scarred back, wondering if his father had ever caressed his mother like that before succumbing to the corruption of the Black Tide.

He would never have the chance to know, for those corrupt souls who had died before Phainon's journey did not live to see this dawn.

The pain he felt when he saw Castrum Kremnos still desolate. Still without a single resurrected soul ready to enjoy the new kingdom that Mydei had planned for them.

There were still inhabitants, of course (although most of them, despite the efforts of Krateros and his friends, disagreed with the ideals of the future new king), but it was not the same.

His friends would not return.

He would never have that second chance with his father.

And his mother... he really hoped to be able to meet her.

To hug her.

But he managed to cope with all that when he thought of Phainon.

When he wished for that second life, that second chance with Phainon.

Now they could have the life they had always wanted. They could do everything Mydei had always wanted to do with him, but had never been able to, because he was too preoccupied with protecting Amphoreus.

They could... they could have a life as lovers, as Mydei had always wanted, together with him.

...

But Phainon never appeared.

And that desolation, that pain in his chest, was greater than all the hardships Mydei had suffered because of his position as prince of Castrum Kremnos.

His mother's sacrifice, the death of his friends, his father's madness, the fall of his kingdom... nothing could compare to knowing that Phainon had died or disappeared, without having the opportunity to enjoy this new life that had been given to them all thanks to his blood and suffering.

That helplessness... that injustice... Mydei felt it killing him inside, slowly.

But the fear of becoming like his father forced him to remain calm. Patient.

Hopeful.

And even though it wasn't the reunion he wanted, even though the face in front of him wasn't exactly that of his beloved Deliverer... it was him.

It was his Phainon.

His hks.

And he was there, next to him. Alive.

Mydei's throat trembled as he hugged that fragile body even closer, so in need of a sleep that was being denied him.

''What have you been doing all this time? Before these two found you?'' he whispered, his voice breaking. ''Have you been hiding? Avoiding us?'' Although his eyes were half open, Phainon did not respond. ''Or have you continued to sacrifice your body for us?''

Phainon simply let out a tired, numb groan, his eyes closing again. Mydei clenched his jaw, waking him up. ''Phai, come on, wake up.'' Phainon snorted as hard as he could through his nose, showing his irritation, but Mydei achieved his goal. ''Believe me, I hate it too... but your beloved professor knows what he's doing.

...

I hope so.''

Phainon groaned wearily again, resting his forehead on the prince's neck. ''This is going to be difficult. You've always been a sleepyhead.'' replied the prince with a sad smile. ''Hey, Phainon,'' he whispered in his ear, shaking his shoulder. ''if you stay awake until Anaxágoras sees fit, I promise I'll never force you to get up early again. Is that okay with you?''

Mydei made a great effort not to break down at the lack of interaction he received in response to the hero's proposal.

There was only silence, which had to be broken when Phainon's forehead slipped from his skin, his head falling lifelessly, tenderly held by Mydei, who had to wake him up again.

This time Phainon growled, clearly annoyed, his eyes tightly shut, as if he were trying to open them but couldn't, no matter how hard he tried.

And the truth was... Mydei didn't know if he wanted him to open them.

If he want his hks to see him.

Ever since he had learned the truth from Aglaea, he had been indignant and angry with her for daring to hide something so important from him.

But now that he had seen the truth... now that he had before him what Aglaea had feared so much... he understood her.

How would he react if Phainon woke up and looked at Mydei with terror? Or with pain? Or... even with disgust?

For not being able to share the burden of that mission with him? For... leaving him alone in an inhuman sacrifice?

And what would happen when he recovered?

''Because he must recover… right!?'' whispered an inner voice, sending a shiver down his spine.

What would happen to their relationship?

Would Phainon continue to see Mydeimos, his rival prince whom he always challenged over every little thing? The one who always made him smile, and who could spend all day talking about his exploits, driving the blond mad?

...

Would he continue to see him as the love of his life, as he promised the night before Mydeimos left Okhema?

Or would the blond now be reduced to a victim of Lygus' plans? A victim at the hands of the very person standing in front of him? The Flame Reaver?

Would Phainon be able to look at him again? To touch him? To kiss him?

Or would the memory of all the times he was forced to kill him be too much for the hero, and he wouldn't be able to bear being in the prince's presence?

If that happened... what the hell would Mydei do? How the hell could Mydei bear to know that the love of his life was alive... but not with him?

Time? Maybe that's what he needed?

But if he didn't react well to Hyacine when he had a fever... how would he react to him after suffering... that completely inexplicable thing he had just suffered?

Without thinking, he opened his mobile phone, thinking of seeking help, hoping for a message from his friends.

But his chat was empty.

Not a single question, not a single call... nothing.

Hyacine had probably notified the others immediately, and they were rushing to the Grove.

Perhaps... when they arrived... Mydei would ask them to take care of Phainon instead of him?

But Mydei snorted immediately, rejecting that idea.

Who could take care of him? Lady Tribios, when Trianne died savagely at the hands of Phainon from the other cycle? Or Cipher, who died alone and covering up a lie?

He immediately thought of Cas, laughing bitterly at his ignorance.

Cas died the same way as Hyacine. As he did. Why on Nikador's name would Phainon react well to Cas unlike the two of them, when Castorice, along with Aglaea, was the one who spent the most time with Phainon?

But then a person came to mind, his eyes widening at that possible suggestion.

The trailblazer was Phainon's light. She was the one who had been by his side all this time. The one who didn't have to see that 'corrupt' side. Whose blood never stained the hero's hands.

He immediately took out his mobile phone, looking for the girl's chat, and as soon as the keyboard opened and he began to type, a voice made him freeze. A voice that said his name.

Mydei slowly turned towards the source of the call, leaving his mobile phone on the bed, incredulous.

Phainon stood with his eyes open; black, hollow eyes with just a hint of blue, unfortunately unfamiliar.

They stared at each other, Mydei unable to utter a word, blinking slowly.

His body was as tense as a rabbit facing a predator.

Phainon, on the other hand, maintained that tired look. It was the only feeling you could get from those half-dead eyes.

But what was clear was how fixed he was on the prince's face. As if it were the only thing that existed at that precise moment.

Faced with that suffocating silence, Mydei tried to speak, feeling completely stupid for not responding to the wounded man.

But his throat still wouldn't work, only his fingers speaking for him, caressing the gash that ran down from his eye to his chin, which so worried the prince.

Phainon watched that hand move down, then looked back up at the prince's face, calling him again.

Mydei gave the most tender and patient smile ever seen, nodding gently, cradling that shattered face. He felt ashamed when he tried to speak again, his voice so hoarse that he could not utter a complete sentence.

Phainon narrowed his eyes at this new caress, his head falling back against that enormous hand, making Mydei smile even more.

''Mydei...'' he repeated for the third time.

The blond man didn't know if it was because it was the only word he could say at that moment or... because Phainon really didn't believe he was there with him.

''It's me, hks. It's me.'' he whispered, his voice still hoarse, lifting Phainon's face so that the prince could kiss his forehead.

That dull gaze continued to stare at him intently when he opened his eyes again, Mydei responding with a soft smile. ''Are you hungry?'' he said, simply to give him something to talk about that might help with his recovery, while also keeping him awake.

Phainon blinked slowly, saying nothing. ''Or do you need to go to the bathroom?'' Nothing. Mydei forced himself to calm down at Phainon's lack of reaction to... to everything. ''Do you want me to call Professor An—''

Phainon finally reacted, grabbing Mydei's cloak, pulling on it with what little strength he had at that moment, Mydei looking at him sadly.

He saw how he tried to squeeze his cloak with all his might. How his only hand trembled...

What did he want? What was he thinking at that damn moment?

''Mydei...'' he whispered again, his voice sounding more broken.

More... human.

Mydei gave him all the time he needed while Phainon seemed to make sure he was really there in front of him.

Alive.

Warm.

Breathing.

Phainon clenched his jaw, the first tear falling, sliding down his emaciated face, the next ones wiped away by the prince's thumb.

He repeated that sacred name again, like an affirmation, a relief, of having his presence by his side, his voice now completely broken sounding exactly like that of his beloved Phainon.

He let himself be sheltered by Mydei's arms, accepting those kisses on his strange hair, while the other continued to clench the red cloak, his fingers touching that warm skin, where he felt a rhythmic and strong pulse through his skin.

''Mydei...'' he repeated for the last time, all the sorrow behind that tone would never be understood, but it would be supported.

Mydei was unable to say anything to him. To assure him of anything.

He could only hug him, kiss him and cry for him, all with a bitter joy, clinging to the hope that this would only become a bitter memory.

''I found you...'' he whispered, his voice also breaking. ''I finally found you, my Deliverer.''

When Anaxa awoke, he refused to admit that he really needed a rest.

His mind no longer hurt so much, and new ideas to help Phainon popped into his head.

After freshening up, he headed back to his office, glancing into Phainon's room.

He sighed wearily when he saw that Phainon's appearance had not changed at all.

But then again... he looked... completely calm? Pain-free?

...

And asleep... next to the prince.

Anaxa approached irritably, raising his hand towards Phainon, ready to wake him, when a pair of golden eyes suddenly opened. Mydei grabbed Anaxa's wrist tightly and aggressively, while, with chilling speed, he pulled his other arm from where he was holding Phainon, to interpose it between Anaxa's hand and the hero's body.

Anaxa blinked in disbelief at the fierce look the prince gave him, as if he were an enemy. As if he were that Aeon who had caused all this suffering to the man they both wanted to help.

''What are you doing!?' Anaxa snorted, when he managed to regain his composure.

Mydei blinked slowly, not changing his posture. ''That's what I should be asking.''

''I told you he shouldn't sleep!''

''And I already told you that he was exhausted.''

''Agh, αγόρι, what if during his sleep—''

''Nothing will happen to him just because he's sleeping.'' Mydei replied, slowly releasing the alchemist's wrist.

Anaxa rubbed the reddened area, understanding why this man was so feared. He hadn't even squeezed hard... and his skin was already bruised...

''And how do you know that?''

''And how do you know that sleeping would do him more harm than good, when he was begging for a rest?'' Mydei's angry face softened completely, like a chameleon, when his gaze turned to Phainon. ''Look at him. We're talking loudly, and he doesn't even flinch.''

Anaxa snorted, hating the feeling that the prince was right. ''It's a guess, lad. We can't risk—''

''You have guesses. I have a proof.''

''A proof!? Proof of what? How can you prove that he's no longer in critical condition!?''

Mydei was slow to look away from the figure now resting on his body, because his arm was still in front of his inhuman torso, his face no longer showing any anger when he faced Anaxa. ''I have no proof that he is no longer in a critical condition,'' Anaxa rolled his eyes, massaging his forehead in irritation ''but I do have proof that it is not a cause for concern that he is asleep.''

''And what kind of proof is that?''

''That he recognised me yesterday,'' he replied calmly ''and he didn't... he didn't lose his temper.''

Mydei finally managed to silence the alchemist, who looked worriedly at the figure they had once feared so much. ''But how did he react?''

Mydei sighed, pulling the battered body closer to him. He explained dryly and briefly how Phainon reacted to his presence. How he called out to him incessantly.

His... his cries.

Anaxa sat down on the bed, feeling his knees buckle, as he sighed wearily. ''That's a good sign.'' Mydei affirmed.

''How can you be so sure of that?''

Mydei pressed his lips together, lowering his gaze. ''It's a feeling I have.''

''That's no use to me, Υψηλότατος .''

''But at least you can see that he's asleep, and that he looks much better than yesterday!''

Anaxa raised his eyebrow, for it must be impossible for Phainon to improve. Phainon would only improve when he returned to his original body. To his human body.

But again, Mydei shut him up when it was obvious that the Flame Reaver's face was calm, and his body was not tense at all, unlike yesterday.

Anaxa remained silent for a while, nodding weakly, finally conceding victory to Mydei.

''Why hasn't he changed his appearance?'' Anaxa muttered, more to himself than to get an answer, after agreeing with Mydei.

''Haven't you found out anything?''

''I have a... theory. But I'd like to wait a little longer before confirming it.'

''Why? If it helps Phainon...''

''That's the thing, Υψηλότατος . That theory, rather than helping Phainon, would harm him even more.''

Mydei blinked in disbelief, turning his gaze back to the sleeping figure. ''Then we must find another solution.''

‘That's what I was getting at, νεαρός'' muttered Anaxa, as if all the years he had accumulated over all those cycles had fallen from his shoulders in one fell swoop. ''Let's see if I can get Lady Tribios to—''

''Lady Tribios left this morning. She said she had to go to the temple of Oronix.''

Anaxa blinked, confused. ''This morning? Wait, what time is it?''

''It's noon. I couldn't tell you the exact time.''

''NOON!?'' Anaxa growls, getting out of bed, indignant. ''And why didn't either of you wake me up earlier?''

''According to Lady Tribios, she wanted to make sure you got the rest you needed. And no offence, but you'll understand that right now my top priority is him.''

Anaxa growled again, rubbing under his eyes. ''I've wasted a lot of time.''

''Phainon isn't going anywhere. And neither am I. So make up for that lost time as soon as possible.''

To the prince's surprise, Anaxa agreed with him, turning around to leave once and for all. But the alchemist stopped when he caught sight of the three garmentmakers, grimacing in pain and slowly turning his face away.

''Why don't you trust her?'' Mydei's voice rang out, stopping Anaxa in his tracks.

''Excuse me?''

''It's obvious you're upset with her. But the question is, why?''

''I'm not upset with her.'' he snorted, overly defensive.

Mydei shrugged. ''I just wanted to help you. But if you don't want to talk about it, that's your problem.''

Anaxa grimaced, sulky, but gave in to the prince's words. ''She went to those geniuses for help.''

''I know. It was either that or both of you would end up losing your minds too. And who knows if Phainon would have ended up dead.''

''Do you even know who the circle's main enemy is, Υψηλότατος ?''

''And why that affect to Phainon?'' Mydei muttered, curling his lip in irritation.

''He's an Emanat—''

''He hurt Nanook. He hates everything related to Destruct—''

''Do you really think that will be enough for them not to see the danger in him? That just because he is a traitor, he is no longer an Emanator?''

''Then what do you suggest? Continue to allow him to suffer even more? I think more than 33 million cycles is enough suffering, καθηγητής .''

''Are you really asking me that?''

''Then accept that if we want Phainon to recover, we need help from outsite, and that means taking risks! And if we have to go to war again, we'll go to war! And if we lose that war, and with it our new dawn, so be it, but with Phainon by our side, and not underground! Or even worse, still suffering unimaginable torture!''

Anaxa remained silent, shaking his head in amusement and weariness, but he did not reply to anything the prince said.

He left the room without saying a word, taking out his telestate, relieved to see a message from the priestess.

''Even if you don't believe it, she needs you.''

Damn Tribios... and damn... Aglaea.

How is she doing? Is she having problems? Is she handling the situation well?

Aglaea may not have been as intelligent as he was, but what could not be denied about her was how good she was at relating to other people, especially when interests were involved.

It was not for nothing that the former leader of the Heirs of Crisos and Empress of Okhema chose her as her heir.

And yet... that anguish... that fear still lingered in Anaxa.

If they hurt her... if... if he lost her again...

Seeing that his mind couldn't stop thinking about Aglaea, and he couldn't even come up with a new suggestion about what the hell had happened to Phainon, he decided to leave his suffocating room, asking Mydei if he was hungry before heading to the kitchen.

What Anaxa prepared was as simple as possible: two pita breads with feta cheese, cucumber, tomato, and black olives (as he doubted that Phainon would be able to eat right now).

Mydei looked at the sandwich with amusement, raising an eyebrow, Anaxa surprised to see the prince so... relaxed. Homely.

''You're lucky I'm not very hungry, or I'd be tearing into his sandwich until I was full.''

''What's wrong with it? It's how my sister always made it for me.'' Anaxa snorted, clearly not offended.

''Then I'll let it be out of respect for the dead,'' he said before taking a bite ''but know that your sister has left out half the ingredients that this type of sandwich usually has.''

''How delicate the prince of the most conflictive nation in Amphoreus is.'' Anaxa rolled his eyes, also taking a small bite.

It was obvious that both were eating to satisfy their natural hunger, but that their appetite was limited.

Mydei still did not let go of his beautiful cargo, but he held it in a position that prevented any crumbs from falling on the bed or Phainon, his gaze fixed ahead, keeping his back straight while he ate.

Meanwhile Anaxa was sitting next to him, the alchemist could seeing the wounded man and couldn't help but sigh with the sadness that still lingered in his body due to his student's condition.

They ate in silence, only Mydei finishing his sandwich, Anaxa handing him a wet cloth and a dry one to wash his hands, the prince thanking him.

''Where are the girls? Aglaea told me they were coming.''

''Investigating. Hyacine is here, while Cas is in the Tartarus and Cipher...''

''Is she all right?'' he asks, worried for the prince's silence.

''I spoke to her a few hours ago and she's... quite nervous. Because of Phainon's condition, because she knows the truth, but above all because of...'' Mydei sighed, pulling Phainon closer to his body again, his clean hand going to the Flame Reaver' strange hair. ''Because of Aglaea. She's very worried about her. Like you, she doesn't trust genies.''

''Oh my, I've found an ally where I least expected it.'' Anaxa quipped, amused. But he raised his eyebrow in disbelief when he saw Mydei stroking Phainon's hair, drawing the prince's attention and asking him what was wrong. ''You can do that!?''

''Do what!?''

''His hair!'' Anaxa reached out his hand towards the strands that also looked like clay, blinking in astonishment as he noticed how soft that hair was, just like on the boy's original body. ''It can't be... I've seen the reports and the appearance of this Phainon when I unmasked him for the first time—''

''That was the Phainon from other cycles. The one I have here is ours. The same one who was born in our recurrence.'' explained Mydei, Anaxa feeling like an imbecile if someone like Mydei felt the need to explain that to him.

''I know, άλαλος! But I mean... if our Phainon is still the Phainon from that recurrence, the one who didn't have to live through any of that—''

''He did live through all that. He had no choice when he killed his other self to obtain his power. That... that Phainon, the original Flame Reaver, sacrificed himself in exchange for passing on all his pain and grief to our Saviour. Phainon is Phainon... but with all the memories of past cycles.''

Anaxa muttered, rubbing his forehead. "I know all that, Υψηλότατος . I know it all too well! But if at first I didn't expect Phainon to be able to take this form, because it is, so to speak, the most corrupt of all the cycles lived, I expected even less that this form would be different from his previous cycles!''

''Are you saying that just because of the hair?'' Mydei raised his eyebrow, with a hint of indifference.

''And who knows what else...''

''His eyes... were dark. Empty. But, I don't know, human?''

''Weren't they hollow?'' Anaxa asks, well he knew the true form of the Flame Reaver after asking the trailblazer about it, Mydei shook his head. ''Well, then that's another change too.'' he joked, unnerved by so much information. He looked back at the sleeping figure, hissing wearily ''If only he were lucid... to answer each of my questions...'' Anaxa hid his face between his legs again, growling irritably ''Agh, why didn't I do all that when he was still fine? Why didn't I think to ask him all those things?''

''You wouldn't take importance to it.''

''Of course I had to care!''

But Mydei simply shrugged ''Thinking about what you could have done in the past is stupid, καθηγητής . You can't reset your life or travel back in time, so don't focus on what you didn't do and could have done, but rather on what you can do now.''

''Now the prince of Castrum Kremnos is coming to give me lessons. Heh, the ironies of life.''

Mydai shrugged again, his gaze focused solely on the sleeping figure, still stroking the hair that had so unsettled Anaxa.

With an indignant snort, Anaxa got up, picking up the tray with the food and dirty napkins, ready to return to his office, but Mydei stopped him again. ''What is your theory about what is happening to Phainon?''

''I told you it's one I want to rule out.''

''But it may be just the right one. What's wrong with him? Why did this happen to him?''

Anaxa slowly placed the tray on the small table in the entrance hall, turning towards the prince just as slowly.

He briefly explained his theory that Phainon was still a piece of computer data, and that perhaps being an human like them were not suitable for him, because of everything he had had to sacrifice to stop Irontomb.

That his humanity acted like a virus, and those convulsions were his system's reacting to the attack.

''And that's why he doesn't change his appearance? This body is the one he obtained artificially. Playing along with Lygus.'' That name was spat out with disgust by the prince. ''Perhaps this body is his antivirus?''

''It's a possibility, yes...'' murmurs Anaxa, agreeing with Mydei.

''But what I don't understand is... why now? Why not before? Just when, as you rightly said, Phainon was recovering. Slowly, yes, but he was recovering.''

''Because of a conversation he had with Aglaea, surely. They were talking about you.'' Anaxa didn't see how Mydei tensed up completely at that information. ''It seems that it was a sensitive subject for Phainon and... his humanity, his guilt and sadness, feelings of a living being and not a computer system, attacked. And to protect his integrity or his body, the antivirus reacted by giving him those horrible convulsions. The fact that, after finally remaining in this body, he has not suffered any of that again, makes me think that your theory is correct.'' Anaxa says.

Mydei still did not answer him, the alchemist looking up. ''When he recognised you, you really didn't manage to see any kind of break—'' Anaxa blinked, confused, at the prince's gesture. ''What's wrong?''

''What... what did they talk about that caused Phainon, when he was finally recovering, to end up like this? Was it my death? Did they talk about something Phainon was forced to do, not just to me, but to all the other heirs?''

''No, it wasn't that. It was something bizarre, actually. They talked about a library.''

Mydei paled at this, looking at Phainon, terrified. ''A library...'' His lips tightened, his jaw trembling. ''Are you telling me that after everything he's had to endure... after that damn horrible recovery he had, what caused him to break down... what caused his own system to attack him... was that fucking library!?''

''Wow, did I miss something, Υψηλότατος ? Relax—''

''NO! HE LOST HIS HOME! FORCED HIMSELF TO BURN IT TO THE GROUND! TO KILL HIS FAMILY, HIS NEIGHBOURS, HIS... HIS FRIENDS AND ALLIES! AND WHAT MADE HIM BROKE COMPLETELY IS THE BLOODY LIBRARY I PROMISED TO SHOW HIM WHEN WE SAID GOODBYE!?''

''It would mean a lot to Phainon, Mydeimos. What I don't know is why—''

''That library is Garnabiphoro!'' Mydei snorted, Anaxa turning pale, understanding the situation. ''It was...''

''Reduced to ashes. Yes, I know.''

Mydei pressed his lips together in anger, looking back at the sleeping boy. ''Why do I always have to be the one to cause you this pain? Damn it, Deliverer...''

Mydei opened his eyes in surprise when Anaxa approached him, the prince without even seeing him, calmly taking him by the wrist.

Mydei followed his gaze, immediately loosening his grip on Phainon, feeling guilty for the force he was exerting (although, to tell the truth, Phainon didn't seem to be affected by it).

''Sorry...'' he muttered, embarrassed.

Anaxa sighed ''I don't think this is the first time we're going to have this loss of temper. Being human again… this vulnerability… it's pretty difficult to adapt to.''

Mydei agreed, pressing his lips together again in pain, resting his nose on Phainon's even whiter hair. And he asked, in the most broken voice Anaxa had ever heard in an adult man, what they were going to do.

Anaxa sighed, with the same weariness ''As much as I hate to say this... wait for Aglaea. Wait for the solution from those two geniuses.''

Cipher stared angrily at her telestate, unable to bring her fingers to the keyboard.

''Fine!? Am I fine!? My little brother is dying and my mother is missing! How the hell am I supposed to be fine!?'' she thought to herself, blocking the telestate.

''Come on, Zagreus! We must—''

''Shouldn't you rest, Cipher? You look stressed...''

''Stressed!? Me, stressed!? HA!'' Cipher laughed, her eyes bloodshot. ''I'M FINE. WHY WOULD I NOT BE, WHEN I'M IN THIS FUCKING RENAISSANCE, WITHOUT MY MOTHER BY MY SIDE AND WITH PHAINON STILL SUFFERING THE DEVASTATION THAT FUCKING GENIUS HAS CAUSED US! HOW THE HELL COULD I NOT BE FINE, ZAGREUS!!?'' she shouted with all her soul, slamming her telestate on the floor, breaking it instantly.

The heiress and the titan stood staring at the broken device, Zagreus looking at its friend with pity. ''I'll find you a new one...'' whispered the titan weakly, disappearing from the scene.

Tears came to Cipher's eyes without her expecting it, her anger still lingering.

She decided to vent by kicking the ground and hitting trees... having to stop when she kicked a stone, letting out a cry similar to an actor playing a renegade prince in the a Middle Earth.

She knelt on the ground, unable to move from the incredible helplessness she felt.

Although she was happy to hear the news that Aglaea had left for the Grove because Anaxa had called her, she couldn't help feeling sad and helpless, as she wanted to make up for as much time as possible with her.

With the mother she never had.

She loved Phainon with all her soul, but he wouldn't never understand. He already had a mother. A caring and loving mother, as he always told her when they slept together.

She didn't... the first human warmth she received in her life was from that damn weaver.

And now she was gone... And who knew if she would ever see her again...

Her helplessness and agony were interrupted when he heard a shrill sound in the sky. For a moment he feared it was Aquila, immediately realising how incredibly stupid that sounded.

Hyacine perhaps? Had she managed to find something?

She decided to follow the noise, stopping abruptly when he saw a lone carriage land elegantly on the ground.

From it emerged a tall, beautiful woman with a black veil, violet hair, and fierce, spectacular eyes.

And behind her...

...

No...

''You were very brave when you confronted Herta. Not everyone would dare to talk back to that woman.'' laughed Black Swan, helping Aglaea out of the carriage.

''I suppose a mother's instinct is something even a genius must fear.'' laughed the blonde, immediately stopping her laughter and turning pale.

Black Swan asked worriedly what was wrong, the blind woman moving away from her. ''Cifera!?'' she shout in a whisper. Was that possible? Yes... Aglaea's voice could achieve such incoherence. ''CIFERA, ARE YOU TH—''

Aglaea was silenced by a hug that came quickly and suddenly, immediately closing her arms around her daughter's figure.

Her little girl.

She hugged her tightly when she felt her shoulder wet, kissing the furry ears of her beloved daughter.

''I'm here, darling. I'm here now, and I'll never leave you again, I promise.''

Cipher couldn't even speak, her claws tearing even Aglaea's clothes. She knew that if it were any other situation, the blonde would be reprimanding her immediately, but right now... right now Cipher could fool the whole world again that Aglaea didn't care at all.

''Aglaea... I... they...'' the poor cat tried to say, her voice unable to function.

But Aglaea's hugs and calm murmur were like a revival for the young woman, taking a deep breath to bring the newcomer up to speed. ''Phainon now looks like the Flame Reaver! And... and he still hasn't woken up! Anaxa and Mydei are very worried, and the others can't find anything, and I... I haven't been able to... I've failed him, Aglaea.''

''You haven't failed anyone, dear.''

''I can't help Phainon! No one can find what he needs!'' she cried out in anger and helplessness, feeling calmed by the tranquillity exuded by her motherly figure.

Aglaea smiled, turning her blind gaze towards the other woman who approached the couple.

''Perhaps she can help him, Cifera.''

Chapter End Notes
