When Mydei came to his senses, he abruptly opened his eyes, realising what had happened.

How could he have fallen asleep?

He muttered a curse, focusing his attention on the figure he was still holding, sighing with relief.

It did not appear that falling asleep had caused any harm to Phainon.

He sighed reluctantly when he saw that the hero still looked the same, stroking the break Phainon has under his eye again, as if that skin was porcelain.

But that touch made Phainon's eyes react, and once again, those eyes, not like his Phainon's but not so unfamiliar either, opened again.

As on the other occasion, Phainon immediately focused his tired gaze on Mydei, the prince feeling small fore that penetrating blue, forcing himself out of his trance.

''Hey'' was all he could think of, Phainon responding with a slow blink. ''H... how are you feeling?''

He was not surprised when silence answered him, but the prince did not give up. ''You must be hungry. You've been sleeping for days.''

Phainon still did not speak, but responded to Mydei by shaking his head. ''No? You're not hungry, really?'' Phainon nodded weakly. ''Then is there something you want to do? Or would you rather go back to sleep? Do you want me to put you on the mattress? Maybe you're uncomfortable in this position.''

Mydei felt a pleasant shiver when he heard a small laugh from the lips of that figure, raising his eyebrow, snorting ironically. ''What did you found funny? Please, share it with me'' he asked, brushing a few strands of hair from Phainon's forehead, his thumb caressing that cold skin.

Those eyes were still not Phainon's, but Mydei saw a warmth that he had not been able to see the other time he woke up.

All the times he faced the Flame Reaver...

''It's strange... to see you talk so much.'' whispered Phainon, his voice as strange as his eyes.

It was rough and hissing, but that country tone. That... tenderness that only Phainon's voice could convey was still there.

''I'm worried about you, HKS.'' he replied, losing his smile, this time caressing below his neck, near the openings on his chest.

He saw Phainon try to breathe deeply, his chest rising, as if it were difficult for him to fill his lungs (did he even have any?), unable to reach his maximum capacity, exhaling hoarsely.

''Are you having trouble breathing?''

''Everything hurts...'' was Phainon's reply, Mydei nodding, slowly placing him on the mattress.

''I'll be right back, okay? Try to stay awake.'' Phainon nodded, and the prince left for the room of the only person who could help his beloved at that moment.

═════════════════════════════════

He was surprised to see Anaxa with several screens showing the Flame Reaver, Phainon himself, in those cycles where he coincided with the Deliverer.

Where he was forced to murder his loved ones in order to save them.

“'Anaxágoras”

Anaxa was startled by the prince's call, rubbing his eyes. ''What?''

''Phainon is awake.'' All the fatigue that Anaxa had been carrying since Phainon took over that body and remained unchanged vanished in an instant, and he immediately got up from his chair. ''And he says he's in pain all over.'' Anaxa nodded, leaving the room immediately. ''I've also noticed that he has trouble breathing.''

''But does the boy even have lungs for that to be difficult?''

Mydei shrugged, both of them reaching the room that Anaxa was eager to burn out of disgust, approaching his student, relieved to see him rational.

''νεαρός,'' he whispered with a cheerful calm that didn't fit in his chest, ''how are you feeling?''

Phainon replied with the typical murmur that a human makes when they want to say ‘I could be better’ wearing a tired smile.

Anaxa responded with an equally tired but relieved laugh, stroking his hair, still unaccustomed to how soft it felt to the touch. ''Do you think you're up to answering questions? Or would you prefer we let you rest a little longer?''

Phainon's smile faded, his gaze fixed on the door, with both Mydei and Anaxa following his gaze, confused. ''Phainon?'' asked the prince.

''Where is Aglaea?'' was the wounded man's question.

It broke the prince's heart how vulnerable and lost Phainon sounded when he asked that. Like a child who had lost his family and was asking about them.

He tried to answer, but Anaxa stopped him, and Mydei allowed it.

Phainon was his beloved... but talking about Aglaea belonged to Anaxa.

''She was very frightened when that happened to you.

And I couldn't find, and still can't find, a reason why that happened to you. So she called the Trailblazers, to go and talk to that genius who helped us defeat Lygus.''

''And do you know if she's okay?'' Phainon's voice was becoming more and more like his own, sounding completely worried.

Anaxa wished he could deceive him, as he didn't know what consequences it might have to overwhelm or worry the boy now... but he couldn't do that to him.

Besides... Anaxa was terrible at lying.

''I don't know, lad. I just hope—''

''Aglaea is fine. Lady Tribios spoke to her recently. It's just that your teacher is stubborn and won't talk to her on the telestate because they're angry.'' Mydei interrupted, both of them blinking in astonishment at the prince's intervention.

Anaxa turned slowly, wishing he had his former powers to end the young man's life, while Phainon seemed to have calmed down completely.

''Lady Tribios... has she been here?''

''Mainly helping Anaxa. He almost collapsed from exhaustion trying to find the answer to what happened to you.''

''Mydeimos!'' Anaxa snorted, wanting to stop him.

''Now she left to the temple of Oronix to find answers. She says she'll give you all the time you need, Deliverer. But if you need her at your side, she'll be there before the sun sets.''

Phainon blinked again, calm returning to his body. ''And... and the others? Cipher? Cas? ... Hyacine... how is Hyac—''

''They're all fine.'' Mydei reassured him again. ''Searching like crazy for answers to cure you. And if there isn't one, we're not worried, because we'll still be by your side. Whether you want us there or not.'

Phainon bit his lip, lowering his gaze, his only arm carefully scratching his stump. ''I... uh... ah... I want to see them, but—''

''Phainon, you know perfectly well that they'll give you all the time you need.''

''No... it's not that! But how... how would they react if they saw their friend looking... looking like this?'' he muttered, pointing at himself.

But Mydei shrugged, smiling slightly. ''Cipher will surely ask you if that inner fire you have inside you can be taken out and sold.'' His hand went to Phainon's chest, gently caressing the area around the opening. ''Hyacine will need Ica's help to calm down when she sees how you look, and Cas... ha, Cas won't care what you look like when she's finally able to give you a hug.''

Phainon opened his mouth in disbelief, exhaling a weak, happy laugh. ''Her curse... her curse has—''

A cough interrupted the two men. If it weren't for his new body, Phainon would have been completely flushed by the way Anaxa was looking at them. ''I know you've forgotten my presence, but yes, νεαροί, I'm still here.'' he snorted boredly. Phainon apologised while Mydei rolled his eyes, a mischievous gleam in his golden ones.

Anaxa sighed wearily, settling back on the bed. ''If you're well enough to hear your boyfriend chatter on like this—''

''See how you're more talkative than usual'' Phainon teased, Mydei accepting the jab.

''Are you ready to answer questions then?''

''I... uh, Professor, I'll try, but... the truth is, I don't know exactly what happened to me. I don't remember anything.''

''I'll tell you what happened to you. You almost gave Aglaea and me a heart attack.

Not even when you were immersed in those nightmares did that happen to you.'' Phainon lowered his gaze, nodding weakly. ''How? Why, Phainon? You really don't remember anything? Not what you felt, not what you thought? As stupid as you may find it, anything you remember is useful!''

''I... uh, well... Aglaea and I were...'' Phainon looked worriedly at Mydei, who nodded with a calm smile. ''I know what you and Lady Aglaea were talking about. Don't worry, Phainon. Continue.'' Phainon nodded, turning his gaze to his beloved teacher. ''We were talking about Mydei and... our promise.

When I remembered that I burned it. And... and I felt so much anger... so much disgust towards myself... I felt, I don't know. Fear. Anger. Contempt for myself...''

''But why did that happen to you on that occasion and not on others? Why did you remember the library when you saw Hyacine or when we told you that Mydei already knew you were alive?''

''Because I burned that library on my own decision, Anaxa!'' Phainon confessed, his voice breaking. ''My mission, to defeat the Black Tide... destroying that library had nothing to do with that! It was purely my decision!''

Anaxa fell silent, looking worriedly at Mydei.

But the prince remained calm, sitting behind Phainon, his arm around his waist, his nose resting on the wounded man's shoulder, achieving his goal; Phainon's body calmed down, as did his expression.

''So... that decision to destroy that library, that promise... unlike when you had to kill us, you didn't do it for our future?''

Phainon denied Anaxa's deduction. ''I burned it out of the rage I felt at being forced to kill Mydei. Because of the helplessness I felt at being stronger than him...'' Phainon turned weakly towards the blond man's face, Mydei swearing he saw tears that did not fall forming in Phainon's dark eyes. ''For all these cycles, I never stopped wishing that you would surpass me. That... that you would be the one to kill me. When we made bets, we always ended up in a tie. So why!?''

Phainon clenched his jaw, his body trembling, accepting Mydei's embrace. ''Why, in all those millions of cycles, did you never beat me? Did you saved yourself!?''

Mydei did not answer him. There was nothing to say, nothing that could ease the pain of his beloved.

Anaxa also let him breathe. He let him cry, knowing that his body was capable of doing so, even though he was not shedding any tears at that moment.

But when the professor also showed his support through touch, Phainon calmed down, taking a deep breath before continuing. ''I f... I felt so many things in such a short time. It overwhelmed me. It was as if... my own body, my own mind was suffocating me.'' Anaxa nodded at his words. ''Then... I don't know if I attacked you...''

''You tried to run away, and you used your gravitational power to push us away from you, but no, you didn't attack us.'' Mydei said immediately.

Phainon looked at his professor, knowing why it was so important for him to confirm that.

''It wasn't like the other time, Phainon. I promise.'' Anaxa whispered calmly, stroking his knee to confirm it.

Phainon sighed with relief, resting his head on his beloved's chest. ''After that pain... that confusion... as if I were back in another plane where everything I felt, everything I had experienced, came back to me all at once... I returned to this form and...'' Phainon took another deep breath, closing his eyes. ''And finally, my head is giving me peace.''

He opened them again, slightly, when Anaxa caressed his forehead. ''So you're saying that this form, even though you're aware of what you did and what you feel, doesn't make you feel that pain you felt in your... well, let's say your original body.''

Phainon nodded weakly again. ''I just feel very physically tired. And a little pain. But my mind is fine, Professor. It doesn't... it doesn't torture me. At least not in that way.''

Anaxa nodded slowly, watching her student intently. ''Can you return to your original body?''

Phainon bit his lip, but nodded. ''And do you think you could return to this one if your mind starts torturing you again?''

''I don't know, Professor.''

''Then stay in this form for now. What surprises me is what Mydei told me earlier. Do you have trouble breathing?'' Phainon nodded again, slowly. ''Is it as if you can never fill your lungs? As if you don't have enough strength?'' Phainon nodded again. ''But lad, forgive me if I sound blunt, do you even have lungs?''

''I don't know.'' he repeated, exhaling a tired laugh. He watched sadly as his teacher rubbed his forehead, confused. ''You want me to transform into... well, my human form, to check my vital signs?''

Anaxa snorted, his lips puffing like a horse's. ''...We'd better wait for your idiot mother.'' Phainon blushed at that, lowering his head when he heard Mydei chuckle amusedly. ''Maybe she really has found help.''

The alchemist stood up as if a tonne of bricks had been lifted from him. ''I'll make you something to eat—''

''He says he's not hungry.''

Anaxa looked at him, his one eye glaring, Phainon closing his ones. ''It's true, Professor... I'm sorry.''

But Anaxa let it go, asking Mydei if he was hungry. ''I'll make something for myself later. Can you think of a solution?''

''Maybe.''

''Then go to your office. Don't waste your time here.''

But as Anaxa was leaving the room, Phainon stopped him. ''Professor, please go and rest. I don't want... I don't want you to collapse again because of me.''

Mydei expected Anaxa to snap at him that he didn't have time for that, but the professor nodded slowly. ''Can you wait, then?''

''Of course, Professor. Please rest.''

Anaxa nodded. Mydei felt stunned, even though he didn't show it, and said goodbye to them, promising before closing the door that he would speak to Aglaea.

A peaceful silence reigned in the room where the two men were, Phainon smiling slightly when Mydei's caresses returned to his chin.

''Are you sure you don't want anything to eat? Even just to taste something?''

Phainon shook his head again, hearing Mydei's tired sigh. ''What about a wee?''

''Mydeimos, please.'' the wounded man snorted in embarrassment.

''I mean, you haven't left this bed all day. Do you want me to bring you a bedpan?''

''Please, not you too!'' Phainon growled. ''I'm fine! At least in that respect!''

''Hmm...'' he muttered, not entirely convinced.

But he let it go because... what else could Phainon want?

''Do you want me to talk to the girls? To tell them you're awake?'' Phainon didn't answer. ''Or do you want to talk?'' He felt Phainon's back bristle, despite his strange skin, dismissing that option. ''Phainon... if you don't want to do anything, then rest—''

''I'd love to take a bath.'' he cut him off firmly.

Mydei blinked, as this was the last thing he expected, especially seeing that body.

''Is it safe for you?''

''It's just a bath, Mydei.''

''I should ask Anax—''

''Mydei! It's... it's just a bath! And the professor deserves a rest!''

Mydei did not fail to notice how nervous Phainon was, but when he begged him, the prince of Castrum Kremnos gave in, helping Phainon up to go to the bathroom.

═════════════════════════════════

═════════════════════════════════

Mydei said nothing about Phainon's strange body when he undressed him.

All the openings around his body... the absence of his parts (maybe that's why he doesn't need to go to the bathroom)... that skin so cold, so... inhuman...

Mydei was irritated by Phainon's stubbornness, because he knew he hadn't felt anything when he sat in the bath.

It wasn't like he was dirty, and the prince was worried that water would get in through those holes and cause him problems.

On top of that, Phainon remained in that damn silence, Mydei not knowing how the hell to break it.

Until... Phainon apologised to Mydei, and before the prince could wonder why the hell he was saying that, a golden glow engulfed Phainon, and the Hero of Amphoreus returned before his eyes.

Finally having human skin, with its receptors and all that skin stuff, Phainon exhaled a satisfied sigh, submerging himself further into the water, closing his eyes, enjoying the bath.

Mydei snorted softly, kneeling beside him, and with a towel, he cleaned the remains of golden blood that his body still bore, causing Phainon to open his eyes again.

''I'm sorry...'' he repeats

''Were you lying when you said you didn't know how to return to your Flame Reaver form?''

''...No... I don't know how to return, but I could try.''

''Damn it, Phainon...'' Mydei snorted, his touch still as careful as ever.

The young hero looked guilty (even more than he should, according to Mydei), biting his lip as he avoided his gaze. ''I needed... Mydei, you don't know how long... I...'' His whole body trembled again, and Mydei turned on the hot water tap while massaging his shoulder to calm him down. ''I feel so dirty... I needed this, Mydei…''

Mydei did not agree, as he felt they were doing something wrong by hiding it from Anaxa, but he understood his beloved, and let him know in the best way he knew how.

With gestures. With caresses.

''I...'' Mydei's actions worked, and Phainon spoke again. ''Mydei, I... I still...''

The hero clenched his jaw tightly, and Mydei gently reprimanded him for fear that he would break his teeth, for who knew if the young farmer from Aedes Elysae would be capable of that now.

''Mydei...'' he repeated, sobbing, as if that name were a prayer ''I still feel your blood on my hands...''

His stump moved as if his arm had returned to him, while with his only hand he clenched it tightly in front of him, his nails digging into his palm.

''Phainon.'' Mydei finally said, trying to loosen his grip, but the white-haired man was exerting so much force and was so tense that the poor prince couldn't. ''Phainon, come on.'' he snapped, trying again.

''How can you not hate me?'' he mumbled, his voice breaking, unable to lift his gaze to look at Mydei. ''How... how can you even touch me?''

He tried to pull his hand away from Mydei, but Mydei held his wrist firmly, and the tears that had been so eager to fall minutes before began to flow uncontrollably.

No more words came out of Phainon's mouth, for every vowel he tried to utter was cut off by a sob, while the poor hero shook his head disconsolately, trying to make his skin bleed again with his fingernails, as punishment for everything he had done to Cas, to Hyacine, to Cipher... to the man in front of him whom he had loved so much for millions of cycles.

His eyes were clouded with tears, but he could hear a splash in the water perfectly, and the next thing he felt after Mydei let go of his wrist was his warm body embracing him.

Phainon tried to break free from that comfort. From that refuge.

He didn't deserve it.

He saw the water, transparent blue, turn golden.

Transforming into the blood of his Mydei.

But he felt so weak that he was unable to even move, crying as he curled up in the curve of the blond's neck, while the latter remained calm, his fingers tracing lines of comfort down the hero's spine, his kisses on his hair a lullaby for that overwhelmed and tortured mind.

His voice... warm, tender and full of feeling, managed to make him believe that he deserved this. That he deserved this second chance. Alive. Together with him. Together with his family.

But that magic was broken when Mydei's soft, calm voice became agitated.

''Phainon!'' he snorted, worried, breaking their embrace.

Phainon desperately clung to Mydei's arm so he wouldn't let go, but Mydei shook him off like a lion shaking off a puppy.

''Phainon, you're bleeding too much! I didn't... damn it, I didn't realise your injuries were so serious!'' He got out of the bath, grabbing a towel to pull Phainon out. ''ANAXÁGORAS! ANAXA!''

''No! Don't call him!'' he begged as he held him in his arms.

But Mydei ignored him, continuing to shout for the alchemist, when they heard loud footsteps and the professor muttering confusedly.

Suddenly silence, Phainon hiding his face in Mydei's neck, wishing the earth would swallow him up.

The bathroom door opened abruptly, Mydei stunned by the alchemist's anger.

''What the hell is this?'' he snorted, with a rage that even Mydei respected. ''I leave you alone for ten minutes, and you decide to ignore my orders?''

''W-what orders?''

Anaxa blinked at Mydei's question, turning to Phainon. ''Phainon!'' he snorted, the white-haired man slowly facing his teacher. ''Was this your idea?''

Phainon said nothing, Mydei putting him back in his grip. ''You can shout whatever you need to shout later, but now we have to tend to his wounds.''

''Tsk, of course.'' He snorted, both of them leaving the bathroom. ''Wounds that wouldn't need treating if you had listened to me!''

Phainon still didn't respond, too humiliated to face Anaxa. Or Mydei.

The prince placed him on the bed, Anaxa treating those open wounds rather curtly, while he was trying to dry him (and himself also)

''Anaxágoras.'' Mydei reprimanded him at how he was treating his beloved.

''Don't you dare, prince! This idiot knew perfectly well that he shouldn't bathe yet! That his wounds were still fragile! And not only did he decide to ignore me, but he also hid the truth from you! Who knows if he lied to achieve this!''

Phainon grimaced in pain and guilt, still unable to say anything, when Anaxa took his chin, gently but firmly, and the alchemist could feel the prince tense up behind him. ''Why, boy? Why are you so difficult?''

''I needed to wash this filth off, Professor.'' he whispered miserably, Anaxa shaking his head with a snort. ''You have to put up with it, Phainon, damn it! You're not even dirty enough for a bath to be a priority!''

''Anaxág—''

‘No, νεαρός! Don't defend him! He doesn't deserve it!'' He turned to Phainon, whose eyes, those eyes he missed so much but was unable to say so because of his anger, were once again crystal clear with pain and sorrow. ''My patience has a limit, Phainon, and you—!''

Anaxa's anger was cut short by the melody of his telestate. The alchemist wanted to ignore it, but Mydei tilted his head to read who it was, blurting out that it was Aglaea.

Anaxa immediately let go of Phainon and picked up his mobile phone, his anger still lingering in his body. In his voice.

''You are the most untimely thing on the face of Amphoreus, I swear, dear.''

He never thought he would miss hearing that melodious female laugh so much. ''Stop scolding my poor Phainon and get out of your house. Meet me in the main square. You know, the one where you first met the Flame Reaver.'' she ended with a mocking laugh.

''I know perfectly well where the main square is, άλαλος.'' he snorted, looking at those cursed garmetmakers, trying not to smile because he was still very angry with Phainon. ''See you there.''

The decision to hang up felt even harder than getting angry with Phainon. The alchemist slowly turned to the poor, miserable boy lying in bed. ''You have been saved by that woman. Again. How privileged you are.''

''Professor, I—''

"We'll talk about this later. I have to meet with her. But Phainon—'' The words he was about to utter were that he was very disappointed in him, but when he saw his face, and above all, when he saw the guard dog at his side, glaring at him, the alchemist calmed down, stifling those sharp words inside him. ''Please don't disobey me again.''

Phainon nodded, his face still showing his remorse. ''You know I only care about you.''

''I know, Professor... I know.''

Anaxa sighed again, stroking the hero's hair as if he were a small child, assuring him that she would return soon, finally leaving the couple alone.

That expression became even worse when Mydei sat down beside him, and the first thing he said was an apology.

He was even still wearing those soaked clothes…

Mydei sighed deeply, his hand going to Phainon's thigh, caressing it affectionately. ''Look, Phainon... do you know how long I've been searching for you, all over Amphoreus, hoping that I would see you again? That we would enjoy this dawn together?''

Phainon grimaced in pain, unable to say anything. ''You did wrong. You should have listened to Anaxa, and above all, you shouldn't have lied to me, but...'' Mydei laughed sadly, blinking rapidly because he didn't want to break down in front of Phainon. Not now. ''But I give a fuck about it…now that I finally have you by my side, I don't want to be angry at you.''

Phainon slowly raised his gaze, melting at Mydei's touch when he cradled his jaw. But please, don't lie to me never again.''

''I promise. I... I don't even know why...''

''You felt dirty, you knew Anaxagoras would forbid it, and you took advantage of the situation with me. Phainon, it's wrong, yes, but it's what anyone in your situation would do. I'm not angry.'' He emphasised the last part firmly, Phainon nodding gratefully, pulling Mydei's arm with his only arm so he could kiss his skin.

He shivered with pleasure when he felt Mydei right in front of him, finally looking up.

Not even the most beautiful sunset in Amphoreus could compare to the way Phainon's blue eyes gazed at Mydei's golden ones, the prince slowly taking his beloved's jaw again, resting his forehead against his, waiting as he inhaled the hero's scent.

Phainon stood still for a millisecond, unable to believe that he had Mydei there in front of him, waiting. Loving him. After everything he had done. After everything that had happened.

And with a desperation worthy of an animal finally freed from its chains, Phainon released Mydei's arm to pull at the fabric of his clothes, sealing his lips, impatient. With desperate ferocity.

That kiss was as intense as it was clumsy, Mydei breaking it with a soft laugh, settling Phainon on his lap, now setting the pace, calming Phainon as he caressed the back of his neck, whispering things that were not in the Castrum Kremnos dictionary.

''Ψυχή μου''

''Καρδιά μου''

''Χρυσέ μου''

Phainon had to stop, trying to catch his breath, not only because of the kisses, but also because his lungs and his sobs prevented him from giving his best.

Mydei dried his tears, the hero melting before that gold, brighter than all the stars combined, when Mydei whispered one last promise, sealing both his lips again and his future.

'' 'Ήλιε μου ''

chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

''Then why are you here?''

''I already told you. My power is related to memories, and I could help Phainon, who knows... by sorting through his memories. Undoing his traumas...''

''You can do that?''

Chapter Notes

Hii, it's been a while hahaha

Have to be honest, after the ending of Amphoreus I was struggling with the ending of this fic. It was written since the end of 3.4, taking the fandom theories of the final or my own opinions (I truly thought that 3.5 gonna be the end of Amphoreus, with Stelle defeating Irontomb with the help of Phainon' sacrifice xD, yeah, I don't pay attention to the news or the streams of HSR AHAHAHHA) so with all the enormous changes respect what I thought it's gonna be the ending of Amphoreus and Phainon... I didn't know how to finish this fic exactly how I always imagined ( – ⌓ – )

You'll see how lazy and hurried are these two last chapters, because it's the only final I find comfortable with it but still... agh, still didn't fit so well. My fault for waiting to 3.5 to write the final and, at least for the lore of this fic, being a big dissapointment HAHAHAHAHAH It won't success again.

But anyway, the main theme of this fic were Anaxa and Aglaea being a paternal figures to Phainon and taking care of him while they're getting together again, so I'm satisfied how it ended (even if I would like a better ending, but I just have a huge writer's block)

See the end of the chapter for more notes

When Anaxa arrived at the designated location, he forced himself to remain calm upon seeing the figure who was competing with Phainon to see who could cause him the strongest headaches.

Aglaea had her back turned, talking to a stranger dressed in purple, with a calm and pleasant face.

He saw the woman smile mischievously, hearing the footsteps of her beloved, but Anaxa still made his presence known with a throat clearing.

She did not greet him. She simply smiled at him with those amusing eyes that Anaxa could not take his eyes off, until, knowing that there was a third person watching this spectacle that resembled a mating ritual, but with the female captivating the male, Anaxa broke his gaze on Aglaea's beautiful face to look up and down at the stranger.

''Hello?''

The unknown woman laughed, looking at Aglaea. ''Oh dear, you weren't lying at all. From here I can feel how sharp and dangerous his tongue is.''

''Excuse me?''

Aglaea joined in the woman's laughter, Anaxa shivering as he felt Aglaea's hand on his skin again, her breath so close to his face.

''Anaxa, this is Black Swan, the person I think can help us.''

''Black Swan? What kind of name is that? It sounds like something out of a children's book about cats.'' he snorted, raising his eyebrow.

The two women laughed again, the stranger, Black Swan, simply shrugging her shoulders. ''Names don't matter when you have a power behind you that's difficult to bear.'' Anaxa looked amused and incredulous again, as if he thought the woman was exaggerating. ''Aglaea has told us what is happening to Phainon.''

''But you're not that genius who came with the Trailblazer to defeat Lygus.'' Anaxa replied, the woman sighing.

''No, I'm not her. And I have no doubt that she would find the solution to your boy's problem sooner than I would. But based on what Lady Aglaea has told me, I have my theories about what is happening to him and how it relates to his memories. And I am an expert at solving those kinds of problems.''

Anaxa nodded, surprised to see how Aglaea's face changed. ''Is everything okay?''

The blonde sighed reluctantly, but Anaxa was not satisfied, crossing his arms and mentioning his name.

''It's just... that... agh, Anaxa, you were right,'' Aglaea snorted, Anaxa hearing Black Swan's soft sigh. ''Herta... the genius... has suggested... how she was talking about Phainon...''

''Αγαπητός, know that I could listen to you talk until I'm blue in the face, but please, structure your sentences.''

''They wanted to experiment on him! Or... or treat him as if he were... something inhuman! They spoke of him in a way... agh!'' the woman snorted angrily, Anaxa forcing himself to remain calm, for the fear that these powerful people might come down to Amphoreus to kidnap Phainon and experiment on him terrified him even more than the Black Tide itself.

Black Swan seemed to see the alchemist's fear, smiling gently. ''Lady Herta won't do anything like that, and although I agree that her words were inappropriate, I really doubt she would want to experiment on your boy. Only help him... in a way that would not take his mental health into account.''

''But she spoke of him as if he were an object of interest! And not a bloody human being!'' snorted Aglaea, Black Swan nodding in agreement.

''Well, but I suppose they will respect that we don't want her to touch the boy, right?'' Anaxa decided to cut to the chase, wanting to get to the point as soon as possible so that she could heal Phainon once and for all.

The two women nodded, Black Swan assuring Phainon that neither Herta nor any other genius would touch him without his permission.

''Then why are you here?''

''I already told you. My power is related to memories, and I could help Phainon, who knows... by sorting through his memories. Undoing his traumas...''

''You can do that?''

Black Swan nodded to Anaxa, Aglaea laughing at her beloved's reaction. "Only Phainon remembers the previous cycles, unlike us. I have seen your message and your theories, and I have shared them with both Black Swan and those two geniuses. Screwllum wants me to tell you that he greatly admires your cunning and wisdom.''

Anaxa looked up, as if he cared little about receiving praise from someone so unknown to him. ''Black Swan has a theory that the reason he -is not yet human-, the reason he suffers all those kinds of... incidents, is because of his memories. And we're not just talking about trauma.''

''Hhmm... as if a human body couldn't handle that amount of memories. Of stimuli.''

''Exactly.'' Black Swan smiled at Anaxa's conclusion.

''But we figured that out long before that strange convulsion he had. Of course it will be hard for Phainon to bear that burden."

''Not difficult, dear, but impossible.'' Black Swan whispered empathetically. Anaxa snorted, but did not reply, for the woman was right.

Thirty-three million memories? And such horrible ones? If Phainon obtained a human brain, human reasoning and a human heart... he would not be able to bear that burden.

No one could.

''I don't know if I can completely free him from all those memories, but perhaps I can mould them in a way that they are no longer painful for him. That those memories, those traumas... are suitable for a human body.''

''So you can't make him forget those 33 million cycles like you did with us?''

''No. I never erased memories, don't matter how horrible they were. It could be very dangerous, Professor Anaxágoras.'' muttered the woman. ''We could risk losing Phainon forever. Without memories, we are nothing, and if I decided to borrow all his past memories, I can risk too to erasing the actual ones. The happy ones. Did he truly deserves that? To start a new life with his condition and his age, along strangers who he means everything to them even thought he won't remember nothing?''

Anaxa sighed, nodding at the woman's suggestion. ''And what do you suggest?''

"Enter inside him. Find out what is happening to him. How his memories are affecting his body. His mind.''

''And then what?'' snorted the alchemist incredulously.

''I can't confirm anything until I see it with my own eyes, Professor." laughed Black Swan, Anaxa feeling relieved to see Aglaea's face, which was also worried and uncertain.

Black Swan sensed their distrust of her and laughed softly. ''You know perfectly well that if I fail to cure your boy, you still have Lady Herta.''

Aglaea nodded weakly, assuring both of them that she herself would apologise for her words and beg for the genie's help if necessary if Black Swan's theory did not work on the boy.

Anaxa looked sadly at his beloved, worried about her aversion to the genie being their only salvation.

He should feel happy that he was right, that he now had Aglaea by his side... but that sad and worried face... damn it, he would do anything to make that expression disappear from her face.

He slowly moved his hand towards the blonde's, who was startled by the sudden touch, smiling softly when Anaxa closed his hand against her palm.

After making sure she had calmed the love of her life, Anaxa nodded to Black Swan. ''I hope you're the one who manages to help Phainon.''

''I hope so too, Professor Anaxágoras, and not because I don't trust Herta, but... because a hero like him deserves his happy ending as soon as possible.''

═════════════════════════════════

''So you think Black Swan is right?'' asked Anaxa, as they both walked slowly back to the alchemist's house, Black Swan several metres behind them to give them some privacy.

Aglaea shrugged, sighing regretfully. ''I don't know... it seems so simple... Just furnishing their memories to make them suitable for human life.''

''Her power is beyond our understanding. It's best not to prejudge.''

Aglaea couldn't help but laugh. ''I missed your reprimands.''

''And I missed your sentimentality.''

They both laughed again, Aglaea sighing calmly. "Black Swan is trustworthy. I feel it in the depths of my soul. And... ahe's probably right about that woman, Herta.

...

But the way she talked about curing him...''

''The boy doesn't deserve to go through that, even if it's his salvation.'' sighed Anaxa, Aglaea nodding sadly.

She calmed down when she felt her beloved's warm hand on her back, her smile returning. ''I saw Cipher. She was... so upset. It took me a lot to calm her down when she saw me again.''

Anaxa nodded sadly, letting the woman finish. ''I managed to meet with Castorice and Hyacine, and they have stayed to take care of her. They are near the Grove, eager to receive any optimistic news.''

''And Lady Tribios?"

''Still at the temple, but I'll ask her to come soon. Her power could help Black Swan.''

''She's not the bearer of the coreflame of Time.'' Anaxa enjoyed the irritating look the blonde gave her at that obvious statement. "But she has knowledge about that Titan. Besides, even if she had the coreflame of Time, it would be of little use to her now, don't you think?''

Anaxa continued to laugh, making Aglaea snort with annoyance. ''You love to annoy me.''

''If you could see your expression... your green eyes shine like so feral. They make you look beautiful."

Aglaea snorted, blushing, and stood up to wait for Black Swan, when the woman laughed as she reached the couple, apologising because she had seen a bookshop with some interesting volumes, leaving them alone.

Aglaea snorted, whispering a -traitor- under her breath, making Anaxa laugh again.

But after those necessary seconds of comfortable silence, Aglaea raised her blind gaze to her beloved. ''I'm sorry I scared you like that.'' the woman could almost imagine Anaxa losing that arrogant smile. ''Not only for making you worry about my safety by leaving so suddenly, so far away, to a place you considered hostile, but also... for make you think you lost me again, just as you lost me the first time.''

Aglaea grimaced at Anaxa's silence, cursing her blindness. ''I... Anaxa, I promise you—''

The alchemist silenced the worried woman when he cradled her jaw and sealed her lips, whispering a plea not to do that again when they both had to separate to catch their breath.

Aglaea imitated the man, promising him, while resting her forehead on his, those kisses that were promises and necessity being the only words they needed at that moment.

When they parted, Anaxa was the first to laugh, caressing his beloved's nose with the tip of his own, his two thumbs stroking the soft cheeks of the most beautiful woman in Okhema.

''I can't lose you.'' the man confessed, Aglaea's beautiful green eyes saddened. ''Not now. I could have gotten over you once— well, no, wait. I thought I got over you that first time, but I doubt I could handle a second time, Aglaea.''

''What do you mean?''

''When you chose the Flame chasers journey, I felt more resentment and contempt than sadness and pain, and I truly believed that all my love had turned to hate.'' Aglaea pressed her lips together at this revelation, nodding sympathetically.

But she blinked in confusion at the alchemist's dry, bitter laugh. ''And as soon as Stelle and Phainon came to the Grove, saying that you needed me... I discovered that all that hatred was just a figment of my imagination. And that belief that I had gotten over you... it completely collapsed when I saw you again after so many centuries.''

Aglaea lowered her hands to rest on Anaxa's neck, caressing the taut skin of her beloved. "Radiant as ever... as beautiful, as fierce, as I have always loved those traits in you. Those eyes... those eyes that were like visual wells for me, as I fell and fell and couldn't escape that beauty...

...

And I found them so empty. So... different from those eyes that made me fall completely in love. How I hate them. How I hate those eyes, Aglaea.''

''They're not like that anymore.''

''I saw them!'' growled the alchemist, clenching his jaw. "When you said that, that you would do anything to save Phainon, for a moment I saw those eyes, so determined to carry out your goal that it didn't matter what sacrifice you were going to make... I saw that coldness again. And to see those hateful eyes again that don't suit you at all, when I get this perfect green back..."

Aglaea kissed Anaxa again to calm him down, the alchemist murmuring gratefully, unable to break away from that union...

But the conversation had to continue.

''You say that when you saw me again, I was just as beautiful as when you fell in love with me... but empty. Like I was inhuman.''

Anaxa nodded regretfully, Aglaea able to imagine perfectly how the alchemist could not take his eyes off her sparkling green eyes.

But the woman laughed, amused. ''I really thought I had succeeded. That I had completely sacrificed all my humanity, all my capacity to love, despite who the bearer was... until you said that damn phrase, and made me blush like a hormonal teenager.''

''Aglaea, dear Aglaea ~~'' Anaxa whispered again, Aglaea hissing in embarrassment, ''You really are the most dearest thing to me...''

''And you decided to kill yourself in front of me...'' Aglaea replied, Anaxa tensing at that retort, lowering his gaze.

But he sighed with relief when he felt Aglaea's forgiveness as the woman buried her fingers in the man's thick, soft hair. "We both sacrificed what we loved most about each other for our goal. But that goal has already been achieved. Let's... let's stop sacrificing our essence, Anaxa.''

''I want to save the boy. I would do anything, but to lose you again, Aglaea...''

''I promise never to sacrifice my humanity again, but you must promise me that you won't sacrifice yours either. Not for me, not for Phainon, not for anyone, Anaxágoras, I mean it."

''You didn't need to say that last part if you called me by my name like that. I take it for granted when you call me that.''

Aglaea snorted with laughter, muttering -idiot-, when Anaxa kissed her again, as if he had run out of air and his oxygen was what he could feel through his beloved.

When they separated, they looked at the street that led right to Anaxa's house.

They were less than two minutes away from seeing Phainon again. From reuniting with Mydei. And Anaxa couldn't help but worry when he heard the blonde's uneasy sigh.

''I really hope that not only Black Swan can help Phainon... but also that he allows himself to be helped.''

''Why wouldn't he want that?''

''That foolish boy probably thinks he deserves the burden of those memories. I know him too well to recognise that self-loathing he has.''

''Heh, well, he's made up his mind if he thinks he can surrendering like that while having that beast he has as a partner. As if the prince would allow that.''

''I hope so, Anaxa... I really hope so...''

『minutes before』

After treating his wounds caused by taking the bath he shouldn't have, Mydei finally changed out of his wet clothes, sighing amusedly when he managed to find a pair of pyjama trousers that fit him reasonably well.

''Hasn't your beloved professor bought you any clothes?''

Phainon replied with a weak smile, ''These past few weeks, I've been more naked than you. My only clothes are these stupid bandages that I can't get rid of.''

Mydei sharply pushed Phainon's hand away from his bandages, the hero dramatising pain that wasn't real, while the prince settled back into bed.

He sighed patiently when he saw that Phainon seemed reluctant to lean against him, even though his gaze begged him to, taking him by his only wrist and pulling him to rest against his chest.

He smiled with relief when he heard the resigned sigh of his beloved, Phainon's body finally relaxing at his touch, both waiting for the arrival of the alchemist and the weaver.

Phainon's tranquillity turned to tension when Mydei's caresses on his belly moved up to his stump, causing a pleasant tingling sensation that his body wanted to enjoy but his mind prevented him from doing so.

He knew that Mydei had detected his change of mood, but the prince continued to caress what Phainon considered to be a horrible piece of flesh.

''Doesn't it disgust you?'' he couldn't help asking.

Although Mydei knew perfectly well what he was referring to, he decided to play dumb, his eyes unopened, his caresses uninterrupted.

''What disgusts me? This situation? Of course, we would be better off—''

''Mydei...''

"Or the fact that you're not eating? That also disgusts me and makes me angry—''

''Mydeimos!" he snorted, finally that golden glint reappearing, facing Phainon firmly.

They remained silent for a couple of seconds, neither of them giving in to the visual dispute they were having, Mydei clicking his tongue, tired of the useless silence.

''Are you asking because it's really you who's disgusted, or are you seriously asking me such nonsense?'' he snorted loudly, wanting Phainon to feel his anger. He sighed with satisfaction when Phainon finally lowered his gaze, his lip twisting into a sour grimace. ''Don't make me stop missing your nonsense, Deliverer.''

''But it's... Mydei, damn it, you can't deny it!''

''Deny what?''

''THAT IT'S HORRIBLE! THAT I'M NOW HORRIBLE! BOTH INSIDE AND OUT!''

At that cry, Phainon tried to move away from the warmth that was so pleasant to him, but Mydei prevented him, causing the hero to fall back against his chest, immobilised as the hand that had been caressing his stump now went to his hair, while the free hand ensured he couldn't escape, placing his palm on his chest.

''Do you remember that time I was wounded in the stomach? That horrible wound that didn't kill me?'' Phainon blinked in confusion at the question, nodding painfully.

Of course he remembers. It was one of the worst weeks of Phainon's life. "Do you remember how awful that wound smelled? How awful the wound looked every time Hyacine and you had to treat me to slightly ease my pain? My screams and delirium? My fever?''

''Of course I do.''

''How could you not… What did you do, Deliverer?''

''Wh... what do you mean?"

''What did you do when it was impossible to even be in that room because of the smell of rot, guts, and iron? When I was raging with pain and couldn't even tell who was next to me? When even the most experienced doctors couldn't look at my wound without turning green first.'' Phainon clenched his jaw, falling silent. ''Come on, hks, tell me.''

''beingbyyourside''

''What? I didn't hear you.''

''Being by your side!'' Mydei snorted, nodding simply.

"Being by my side. Taking care of me. Healing me. Reassuring me.'' Mydei took his chin, forcing him to look at him. ''Kissing me. You think I don't remember, but believe me, I remember perfectly, Phainon. And believe me when I tell you that those kisses were the best sedative I've ever received.''

''Idiot.'' Phainon snorted, unable to suppress a smile.

''How did you see that wound?'' Phainon growled Mydei's name, fed up, but the prince did not give up. ''Come on, say it. Did you see it as ugly? Did you ever stop taking care of it? If I still had that scar, would you stop feeling attracted to my belly?''

Phainon snorted slowly, shaking his head even more slowly. ''Then why the hell would I find something about you that is a war scar ugly, Phainon? Do you think I'm that superficial?'' Phainon finally shook his head, hiding his face in Mydei's neck when he hugged him, his tension melting away when the prince kissed his hair.

''Don't ever ask me such a stupid question again, okay?'' Phainon nodded, promising.

They returned to that comfortable silence, Mydei thinking that Phainon had fallen asleep, surprised by the unexpected question that came from the hero.

''Are you still immortal?''

Mydei sighed calmly, lowering his hand to the back of the man's neck. ''I don't know,'' he confessed, feeling the white-haired man shiver. "Obviously, I haven't tried it and I won't, but my theory is that I'm not. I'm not anymore. Cas doesn't have his curse, so why should I still have mine?''

''Yours isn't a curse, Mydei...'' The prince couldn't help but laugh tenderly at Phainon's fear, kissing his forehead again and ending up on his lips. ''Hks... I'm not going to abandon you so soon, you can breathe easy."

He stretched his shoulders a little, just enough so as not to disturb Phainon, who was still resting against his body. ''Besides... we don't have much to fight for now, would you say? At most, we would have to be careful with our confrontations.''

The mockery with which Mydei wanted to speak ceased, but his calm and empathetic smile remained, in response to Phainon's expression.

''Our battles... yes...''

Mydei traced circles on Phainon's chest, feeling his heartbeat against his fingertips, the prince whispering hoarsely. ''Just because you don't have an arm doesn't mean—''

"I didn't come out of that fight just one-armed, Mydei. I think... I think Nanook did something inside me.'' Mydei raised an eyebrow, curious. ''To... to my heart..."

The caresses on his chest ceased, Phainon breathing shakily when he felt Mydei's palm open in that area, closing his eyes, ashamed.

''No wonder I found your breathing bad...''

''I'm sorry...''

''What the hell are you sorry for, Phainon? That you sacrificed so much fighting literally destruction personified? You made a god bleed, Phainon. A god!''

''He and Zephyro took my arm and my healthy heart, and all I managed to do was make a stupid cut on his cheek!'' Phainon snorted.

"And with just that cut, you managed to break the cycle. You managed to get Amphoreus out of that artificial bubble, eliminating his damn mission to give him real life. Human life. Damn it, Phainon, you should have died in that fight, and here you are with me, alive! Do you really think I care that we now have to lead a quieter life because of your new disability?!"

But Phainon's silence did not calm the prince, the hero rolling his eyes nervously, like a child who had just been caught doing something naughty.

''Phain—''

''I don't know if I should be here. Well... what's happening to me is proof of that...''

''And what do you suggest then? That we give up? That we let you die?''

Phainon clenched his jaw tightly, Mydei forcing him to relax as she cradled him cautiously. ''No... I don't want that, Mydei...''

Mydei sighed, hugging him again, his back stiffening at Phainon's next words. ''I don't want to die...''

''You're not going to die!'' snorted the prince, surprised and above all terrified by this plea. ''Where the hell did you get that idea!?''

''Even if we don't have the future I always wanted with you... I want to be by your side. By Aglaea's and the professor's side. By the girls' side...''

''Phainon, answer me! Why the hell do you think that!?'' Mydei snorted again, wanting his beloved to focus.

''That I shouldn't be here... Everything that happens to me, all my loss of control is proof of that... My mission was to sacrifice myself to deliver the Era Nova to all of you, so why...

Why am I here?'' He couldn't help but sob slightly, burying his only palm in his face, Mydei's terror clear in his expression.

He hugged him tightly again, letting him cry, letting him tremble. Fear was also very human, and Mydei did nothing to calm that understandable dread. But unlike when he had to make all those sacrifices, now Mydei was by his side.

And he would never leave again.

''Aglaea and Anaxa will come up with the solution. I'm sure of it.'' Mydei tried to reassure him, a promise he also wanted to serve himself as well.

When the couple returned, Aglaea immediately sensed Phainon's distress, the hero welcoming the woman who had always been a refuge for him, managing to calm him down.

She asked no questions, reassuring him with gentle words that everything would be all right. That they just had to hold on a little longer.

Mydei sighed, grateful that Phainon finally felt so calm, explaining to Anaxa and the newcomer (whom the professor had forced to wear one of the shirts he had bought for Phainon a few days earlier) what he had told him just right now.

Anaxa looked at his student with regret, while the woman seemed pensive about it. ''Are you the genius Anaxa fears so much?'' the prince asked hostilely.

But the woman laughed, shaking her head, introducing not only her name but also her status, leaving Mydei just as confused as when she started talking. "Let's just say I can get into people's memories and alter them. As long as, of course, that memory is not stronger than my power'' she laughed gracefully, Mydei turning his gaze to his beloved.

''And you think you can help him?''

''I can try.'' she replied with a smile, which was not enough for Mydei.

Phainon needed to stop suffering NOW.

Everyone sensed the prince's impatience, and it was Aglaea who finally spoke to the trio. ''We'd better get started as soon as possible, then.'' Her blind gaze turned to the man she loved like a son, caressing his hair tenderly, causing Phainon to look up. ''Do you think you're ready?''

''Will it hurt?'' asked Mydei before Phainon even opened his mouth.

Black Swan laughed again, calmly shaking her head. ''Physically, no. But I can understand that you might feel uncomfortable with someone discovering your memories.''

''A little... yes...'' confirmed the hero.

"I assure you that I will be strictly professional, and of course, I will not judge any of your actions. Believe me, dear, this is what I do for a living, and no matter how many deaths you have on your conscience, I doubt you are the worst person I have ever encountered.''

''Hm... now I'm curious about the kind of people you've dealt with.'' Anaxa replied with a smug smile.

''You don't want to know, Professor ~~ Well, then, dear, are you ready?"

''Wh... what do I have to do?''

''Just stay calm and keep the room quiet. The rest of you can leave if you want, although I seriously doubt you will.''

''As long as you're comfortable with us being here.'' replied Aglaea, with Phainon assuring him that it was fine with them by his side.

Black Swan nodded, standing in front of the young man, striking a posture very similar to that of prayer, and closed her eyes.

The tips of her hair, as well as a violet aura that was enveloping her, glowed, that beautiful magic ending immediately, as did the action of the unknown woman.

She blinked in confusion, the three of them looking concerned at her reaction.

''I can't access it. It's... dear, your inner self is really dangerous.''

''I... I'm not doing it on purpose, I promise,'' replied Phainon, embarrassed.

"I know, I know, but it's like... I don't have the access key to your memory. As if your mind were a dark and eternal limbo.''

Phainon sighed, not knowing what to say, until Anaxa asked if it was because it was her.

''What do you mean?''

''What if it's someone else? If you use your power to put someone he trusts in their mind, could it work?"

''Hmm... yes, of course, I can do that, but I don't know if you would be able to find the solution to what is happening inside them, or if the same thing would happen as happened to me.''

''It's worth a try.''

''What do you mean, Anaxa?'' Aglaea raised her eyebrow, confused.

''If we are the ones who get inside the boy's head, maybe we can access his memories and perhaps find the solution to why he has not yet achieved stability.''

Anaxa did not miss how Phainon paled at this, resting his hand on the hero's knee. "Phainon, you have no reason to be afraid. Because you have nothing to hide to us. Enough of this silent suffering of yours, all right?'' Phainon did not respond, Anaxa pressing his hand gently against Phainon's knee. ''Trust us, lad. You won't lose us, whatever we see inside you."

Phainon clenched his jaw but nodded, looking wearily at the violet woman, giving permission to the three most important people in his life to enter his memories. His tired mind.

"The only thing I can't guarantee is how long I can keep three people inside the memories of one, and on top of that, one with a memory as unstable and chaotic as yours.

You must be quick and efficient, if you manage to find anything.''

''We will be.'' Mydei replied firmly.

''Then lie down, dear, and if you feel sleepy, don't hesitate to sleep. These kinds of processes cause a lot of drowsiness, and you, find a position that won't make you fall. You will be unconscious and vulnerable for a good few minutes."

Aglaea squeezed Phainon's shoulder before getting out of bed to rest in the chair that had been her bed for the first few days since Anaxa had called her, surprising her.

Anaxa stood beside her, crossing his legs, his arm lightly touching that of her beloved.

And Mydei simply leaned against the wall of the room, in a position that would be uncomfortable for any human being, but not for the prince of Castrum Kremnos.

He looked at Phainon, nodding bravely, taking his hand to convey the warmth and calm that they both so desperately needed.

And after a long, shaky sigh, Phainon assured Black Swan that he was ready.

Chapter End Notes

Αγαπητός -- read as Agapitós, means ''dearest, love''

Free him from this burden.''

Mydei did not expect such a sudden and dizzying movement when Phainon nodded to Black Swan.

He did not even have time to react.

It was as if he were riding on Aquila's back, while the Titan plummeted at a suffocating speed.

When he finally felt solid ground, he managed to open his eyes.

He still felt horribly dizzy, and his knees buckled when he tried to stand up, but as he sat on the ground, Mydei observed the new world he found himself in.

The mind of his beloved... more chaotic and terrifying than he had expected.

''Deliverer... you bloody idiot,'' he growled to himself, the dizziness finally subsiding a little, allowing him to stand up.

He was on a kind of mountain, at the highest peak, where a scattered path led downwards.

Mydei advanced slowly, hurrying as his balance gradually returned, pulling his claws out of the ground when an earthquake struck, surprising him and almost causing him to fall into the void.

''Τι διάολο, Phainon. You better not have done this on purpose!'' he snorted.

When he managed to climb down that terrifying mountain and advanced along that dry and intimidating path, he stood still, paralysed, upon finding a new scene in what was the territory of his beloved's tired and disturbed mind.

Kephale... the statue of Kephale, like the one in Okhema... broken. Completely destroyed, golden blood dripping from each of its openings as well as from its eyes, as if...

As if the statue were crying.

And a huge sword, Phainon' sword, piercing its chest.

''Γαμώτο, Phainon...'' He clenched his teeth, shaking his head, trying to understand why something like this was inside the hero's mind.

He realised that all the damage his beloved suffered was in that statue, so he rushed towards it, knowing that he had very little time left.

The path narrowed more and more, Mydei praying that he had not taken the wrong path...

...

When in front of him stood a dry, bent tree...

And leaning against it was the Flame Reaver.

█████████░░

Anaxa muttered in pain, massaging his temple after falling onto the cold, hard floor of a temple.

He blinked, trying to figure out where he was, unable to recognise what kind of temple it was, even though it seemed familiar.

He decided to move forward, feeling the ground shake beneath his feet, without losing his balance due to where he was standing.

But he looked up at the ceiling, worried that it might collapse.

He did not know, however, what would happen if the ceiling fell on him.

Would he return to his reality? Would he lose his chance to save Phainon?

...

Could he die right there?

He sighed wearily, forcing himself to stop thinking about it and move forward.

Move forward in search of a cure for his beloved pupil.

He went through several doors, none of which revealed anything.

He found a harp, but despite his respect and admiration for music, he had never made an effort to learn to play an instrument, let alone the harp.

But he smiled inwardly, for Aglaea was one of those who knew how to play that beautiful instrument.

Thinking of that woman made him ponder. Where could she be?

Was she all right?

Was she nearby? Far away?

He ran his fingers over the fine strings of the instrument, a meaningless melody resonating through the temple, Anaxa closing his eyes, almost imagining himself back as that young man who did not yet know what he really was, admiring Aglaea's figure as she delighted all the students with her talent, oblivious to how Anaxa admired her beauty and smile.

But that beautiful memory was shattered when he heard a scream in the air, the alchemist freezing.

He would recognise that scream anywhere...

Unfortunately, it was the only thing he had heard in recent weeks.

He whispered the name of the reason why he was in that place, running to the source of that scream, ending up in a large room with many staircases and crystals blessed by Oronix.

Anaxa blinked in confusion, not knowing what the hell that meant, until he reached one of them, and when he went to touch it, he froze, witnessing that horrible memory of Phainon.

The destruction of his village.

The discovery of the Flame Reaver.

...

Only to discover that the murderer of his neighbours, friends, parents... was himself.

''στο διάολο I do with this?'' Anaxa muttered, until he saw the glass melt into his palm, blinking curiously.

He searched the room more eagerly, seeing more crystals, but only one of them accessible...

...

Unless he played at being Oronix.

He didn't have Stelle by his side, but he begged that, thanks to the power of Black Swan and the fact that he was really in Phainon's mind and not in Amphoreus, he would be able to accomplish this task.

He sighed with relief after collecting the other crystal, discovering that indeed, what Stelle could do with Oronix's gadgets, he could also do, taking a couple of minutes to collect them all, even tripping on one of the stairs due to how fast he was going.

But how could he not?

He had a countdown, and he wasn't going to waste a millisecond to find out what the hell was happening to Phainon and how he could give him the humanity he so deserved.

The crystals, which were more like mementos, burned like lava, Anaxa realising that he was not only having the memory of his Phainon from when his village was destroyed.

From when Aglaea died. When he died. Her friends. Her beloved...

The vast majority of them having to be killed by him.

Each crystal contained the memories of all the Phainons of the past, each step the alchemist took being a veritable torture.

But he wasn't going to give up.

Phainon endured this pain for billions of years.

Anaxa could endure it for a couple of minutes for him.

████████░░░░

Aglaea brushed the bits of wheat scattered through her hair and dress aside, sighing with relief at the soft landing she had had when she fell into the wheat field she had destroyed.

She sighed with relief that she would not have to explain herself to any farmers.

She knew where she was, even though her blindness remained in that strange world.

The scent of this territory was identical to the slight smell Phainon still has, under all that mud and blood when she found him.

She advanced through Aedes Elysae, relieved that her threads were activated in this place, when she heard a child's laughter and tried to follow it.

She felt a chill growing stronger as she followed the laughter, realising that she no longer felt the warm rays of the sun from the village of Phainon on her skin.

Where had that damned child taken her?

''Phainon? Phainon, are you there?'' she called, the laughter still ringing all around her.

''Phain—'' Aglaea fell silent, hissing at how stupid she felt at that moment. ''Khaslana? Are you there? Khaslana!''

The laughter ceased, and Aglaea laughed when she heard loud footsteps behind her, which stopped immediately, her threads detecting a small figure behind her.

She turned slowly, laughing at the surprised sound of the boy. ''You're blind!''

She had forgotten how loud-mouthed Phainon was as a child. It was a trait that Cipher encouraged even more... and Aglaea never thought she would miss it so much.

The blonde smiled, nodding, and the boy immediately apologised. ''Don't worry. You've only spoken the truth, but it's true that it's not nice to point out people's features, as well as their disabilities.''

Phainon nodded, Aglaea being able to perfectly imagine how his lip was curled in that childish gesture she loved to see so much in the past.

''W... what did you want from me, ma'am?''

''I just moved into your village, and I just wanted someone to show it to me.'' Phainon let out an excited sound. ''And I thought you would be the ideal person!''

''Yes! Yes! I'll show you my village! Run, come on, before Piso sees you and gets jealous.''

Aglaea laughed, forgetting for a moment why she was there, as she felt the warm hand of that pure and tender child.

But she was there precisely so that child would not die inside her adult self, which was currently so wounded and tired.

''And this was my grandmother's farm!''

''I didn't know you had a grandmother.''

''Mum has told me about her sometimes! I never met her, but I know this is her farm!''

''And it's abandoned?''

''We use it as a shelter for wild or stray animals when it rains. It's not very common, but anyway...'' Phainon shrugged, eliciting another soft laugh from the woman.

''Hey, Phai—Khaslana,'' the boy murmured with a smile, letting her know he could hear her. ''Are you happy here?''

''Yes! I like training the younger children, and being with my teacher... even though I don't really like being in her class...''

"That's a habit you need to change, dear. It's possible that in the future, you'll have a stricter teacher'' Aglaea laughed, longing for her beloved.

Would that be okay? Would he be having problems?

''I hope not! Or they would dislike me very much, and I don't want anyone to dislike me!''

''Oh dear, I doubt that hypothetical teacher would dislike you. It's obvious from a mile away that you are such a special and loving child that... anyone who knows you would give their life for you.''

Phainon blinked, confused by the woman's words, scratching his head, confused. ''Sorry, I sometimes get very lyrical. What else do you like to do here?'' she decided to change the subject, forcing herself to calm down, for standing before her were the memories of a childish Phainon.

A Phainon... still without pain, without death, without regret...

Without chaos behind him.

''Fishing. Playing with Snowy. Visiting the fairies. And FIGHTING! FIGHTING A LOT WITH THE SWORD!''

''Why is that not surprising?'' smiled Aglaea, Phainon laughing.

''I plan to train to be the best swordsman in Aedes Elysae! And when that happens, I'll go to Castrum Kremnos to be accepted as an apprentice! I'm sure I'll become the strongest soldier in that city! On the whole planet!''

''So your main goal has always been to go to Castrum Kremnos?'' whispered Aglaea, Phainon nodding with a laugh.

Aglaea grimaced, hurt.

The place where she found Phainon was one of the roads leading to Castrum Kremnos.

How would his life, the lives of all of them, have changed if Phainon had accomplished his mission?

Would he have met Mydeimos? Would he have allied himself with him?

Would he have been an enemy of the prince and Okhema, since he would have ended up being trained by Eurypon's men?

...

Would he has prevented Mydei from killing his father, causing the two lovers, in that cycle, to become bitter enemies?

Aglaea shook her head, not wanting to waste time on hypothetical alternate universes, continuing her conversation with the boy, when a female voice called out to her.

''Coming, μητέρα !'' Aglaea heard Phainon jump up, feeling the boy at her side. ''See you another day, ma'am!''

But Aglaea had no other day.

And with the appearance of this new person, the weaver was determined to get to the bottom of the matter.

█████░░░░

''You must be joking,'' Anaxa snorted when he entered another room, completely identical to the previous one.

The difference in the crystals in that room was their colour.

They were a blinding white, unlike the dark purple ones inside Anaxa, causing him indescribable pain.

Anaxa hissed, walking back to pick up those crystals, quickly pulling his hand away from one when he saw how it was contaminating it with that dark purple smoke, as if the Black Tide were inside Anaxa.

What ... what could he do!? The time kept passing!

He looked at the white crystal again, no memory coming to him.

Why was it there? What he has supposed to do?

But he could hardly get angry when another earthquake shook the ground, Anaxa raging at the knowledge that he was running out of time and had made no progress.

His fists were clenched with rage, added to the pain that penetrated his bones, and he struck the white glass angrily, opening his eye in surprise when he heard a faint voice.

He barely managed to catch it, but he recognised it immediately.

It was Castorice...

''Castorice!?'' he called, looking around. ''Are you there, κορίτσι ?''

Silence answered him, Anaxa snorting in dissatisfaction, turning his attention back to the white glass.

He did the same thing as before, this time keeping his hand raised, even though the white glass was being corrupted by the purple smoke.

Anaxa tensed as he heard the cries of pain from his beloved student. Her pleas to Phainon to stop. That there must be another solution.

But deep down, deep down in that regret, in those cries... she heard a laugh.

Laughtera that was all too familiar to him.

...

Of course!

It was the first time Anaxa had heard Castorice laugh, when Anaxa decided to mock Phainon in one of his classes!

He opened his one eye, frowning, determined, remembering that memory strongly, as if he wanted to convey it to that glass.

He smiled when he saw that Castorice's screams were no longer so loud, replaced by the girl's embarrassed murmur and Phainon's laughter, laughter that Anaxa stopped when he snapped at him that he was the least qualified to laugh at anyone.

''Professor, why are you so cruel to me?''

''Pff...''

Anaxa felt his strength falter, Aglaea's words from weeks ago, when Phainon was still unconscious after being rescued by the alchemist, piercing her heart.

''Did you even try? You never dare to think about how much Phainon cares for you. I'm sure he can't even believe that it was you who saved him."

He clenched his teeth, the purple smoke gathering momentum again, Anaxa trying to fight it, but the guilt of how he had treated Phainon in the past made him falter...

Until a halo of light dispelled the smoke completely, it still inside Anaxa, trying to reach the pure crystal.

''Professor Anaxa is going to give me private lessons! It'll just be him and me! Huh!? Why are you laughing, Cas!?''

''I don't know why you're surprised, silly. Professor Anaxágoras thinks very highly of you!''

''You think so? I think I drive him crazy...''

''Oh yes, that too. But believe me, Professor Anaxágoras is not someone who likes to waste time, and I can always see how eager he is to teach you the things you find difficult to understand.''

''Cas, have you heard? Professor Anaxa hit a student! Why are you laughing? Do you know something?''

''All I know is that the student who was hit dared to insult a young student who has difficulty to learn and memorize, calling him a bumpkin because he comes from a village.''

''Really? What a jerk! I hope that student is okay...''

''Something tells me he is…''

''But Professor Anaxa, going so far as to hit him? Seriously? Don't shrug your shoulders, Cas! You know him better than I do!''

''He must care a lot about that student of his, Phainon. I don't know what else to tell you.''

Anaxa sighed, smiling, nodding at that crystal that seemed to want to fight with him.

The contamination of the previous crystal, of the previous memories, continued to try to penetrate the purity of the white crystal, but Anaxa felt the strength within him again.

''Come on, lad, are those really the only good memories you have of Castorice?''

And the beautiful, happy memories won out.

All the moments that his beloved trio had experienced in the Grove when they were students.

When Castorice and Phainon returned to Okhema, Hyacine stayed with Anaxa.

How they both managed to get Phainon to 'hug' Castorice, making the woman cry on more than one occasion.

''If you win... damn it, Phainon, if you win, you can hug her. So come on! Let those good memories prevail over the bad ones. Over the supposed crimes that have already been forgiven!

Don't let Castorice not hug you, when it's her greatest desire..."

And inside him, Anaxa felt something break, the pain he felt diminishing, the pure crystal emitting a strong glow, completely eliminating any trace of corruption around him.

Another earthquake sounded, but this time it was lighter. Like a congratulation on Anaxa's victory.

The man, relieved, searched for the other crystals, finally knowing what he had to do.

███░░░░░░

Aglaea watched Phainon's parents, frowning as she disliked what they were saying to him.

Phainon used to talk to her about his parents.

He used to have nightmares, remembering them. Remembering their deaths.

From what Aglaea could gather, they were a kind, loving, wonderful couple who loved their son with all their hearts.

Why?

Why didn't they seem that way here?

''Don't you understand, dear? That goddess has betrayed us. Don't you think she deserves punishment?''

''I know, μητέρα ... but—''

"No buts. You must obey your mother. N͔͜e̹̯̗̯̽̈́̂ͭ̆̍i̸̷̧̜̗̪͔͐̅̔͊̉̍́̀͆͛̅͂̾ͯk͍̼ͣo̴̸̡̡͉̠̭̚s̥̲̼̲̉̚ ̛̩͓͈͍̼̔̇̈́̇̀̀͟''

Aglaea tensed when she heard that name from Phainon's father, in that squeaky way.

And besides... which goddess were they talking about? They weren't referring to Oronix, were they?

''But Father! I don't know that Nous!'' Aglaea tensed at the mention of that name. ''And besides, I... I don't want to kill! I want to have adventures!''

''You want to train as a soldier in Castrum Kremnos, but you don't want to get blood on your hands? I didn't know my son was such a softie.'' the man snorted, all of young Phainon's cheerfulness disappearing.

Aglaea had to make a great effort not to come out of her hiding place and break the connection, her threads tensing with the anger she felt.

''Because I know that in Castrum Kremnos I could be a hero! That's what I want! To fulfil the wishes of all my loved ones!'' Phainon shouted again, Aglaea nodding, proud of her boy. ''And if it's not in Castrum Kremnos... then in Okhema!''

Aglaea smiled at Phainon's childish voice, snorting when the mother began to speak. ''Okhema? That dangerous place? Why, my love? Why do you want to risk your life for people who will never love you? Who will never appreciate you?''

''Are you really willing to burn, to turn to ashes for a world that would turn its back on you?"

Phainon fell silent at this, Aglaea clenching her fists in anger, trying hard not to go and silence those idiots.

But her threads kept trembling, becoming painful for the woman, clenching her jaw when the parents continue to speak.

''You were not born to be a hero of Amphoreus,

K̸̭̰͖̦̱͖̰ͪͪ̿́̚ẖ̷̡̡̣̬̘̱͍̮͙͚̼̣̲͕͎͇̯͈̈́̎̐̋̀̈́ͨ͋͛͑ͩ͊͢͡͞͡a̠ ̷̧̧̢̛̹̜ͮ͊s̵̨̛̼̺̥̪͎͙̫̤͖̟̹̭̒̊ͭ̾͛̌͑̌̎ͤͮ̍̕̕͢͡͝ͅͅl̨͐a̴̯̖̼ͫ ̴̴̡̡̛̘̦̗̠͉͈̻̞̿͡͠n̶̡̨̺̞͉̫̖̞͉̋̋ͭ̀́͒ͫ͛͊ͭͧ̒̓͗̾͘̚͟͜͜͡ͅͅͅ ̶̨̭̪̋͋̓͛̊̂̕͜ą͉̻ͨ̔, if not the universe. To become our Sun!''

''B... but Dad—”'

''That's why you must stop your stupid idea as soon as possible, or you will become the enemy of your own purpose. What a tragedy, don't you think?''

Neikos... Khaslana... That way of speaking... so illogical to how Phainon spoke of his parents.

Sighing, begging him not to be wrong, Aglaea used her threads on that couple, making them disappear, the figures of Lygus, Zandar appearing in their place.

Phainon cried out in fear, grabbing the first large stick he could find, threatening the new figure who looked at him with cold seriousness.

''How did you manage— oh…'' whispered Zandar, with a grim smile, ''What are you doing here?''

The poor healer covered her mouth with her hands, apologising. The four of them, Phainon, Castorice, Cipher and Hyacine, began to walk to find out what their next destination would be, so engrossed in their conversation that they immediately returned to Aglaea and Anaxa's marriage proposal, not realising that both Mydei and Tribios had been left behind.

''What are you thinking about, De?''

''Where is that refuge?''

''Hehe, it's hard to explain, but if you want, I'll explain it to you tomorrow'' Mydei murmured softly, unable to help but smile at the laughter of his beloved priestess. ''What are you up to, Mydeimos?''

''Me? Nothing.'' replied Mydei, finally starting to walk, Tribios by his side, his gaze never leaving Phainon's beautiful, happy face. ''After all, there's no such thing as romance in Castrum Kremnos, right?''

''But romance and love are the most important things for Okhema, De.''

Mydei nodded, laughing again when Phainon turned to look at him, immediately turning his back on his beloved because of the way the prince was looking at him. Mydei loved that shy side of the hero when they were in the company of their friends.

''And believe me, Lady Tribios. I am well aware of where my home is now.''
